## Does leasebreak.contended name a waiter whose current globs no longer overlap the holder?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B38ebc3e392`

- **Claim.** contended inverts waiting.wait_for_graph, which recomputes a waiter's edges from its STALE recorded ask (lease.waiting globs); a waiter that narrowed its globs after the refused widening is still named for the holder whose file it gave up.
- **Mechanism.** update --globs wider is refused and records lease.waiting with the refused globs; update --globs narrower succeeds (retarget keeps the same lease.event) so the recorded ask stays stale; wait_for_graph recomputes from the stale ask; contended inverts to holder->waiters; the heartbeat surfaces it as a false YIELD REQUESTED.
- **Falsifier.** test_a_waiter_that_narrowed_away_is_not_held_contended asserts 'T2' not in contended(...)[T1] after T2 narrows src/b.py,src/a.py back to src/b.py -- it FAILED before the fix (contended=={'T1':['T2']}) and PASSES after.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Write the regression test, run it on the unfixed code, then after the fix.
FAILED tests/test_lease_yield_disjoint_waiter.py (contended=={'T1':['T2']}), then after filtering contended by current-glob overlap: 1 passed.
```

## Does ddflow heartbeat's inbox delivery delete a message, so a piped heartbeat that lost the text cannot show it again?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-inbox-message-gone-after-heartbeat`

- **Claim.** inbox.take() unlinks each delivered message (delivered once), and heartbeat's consume path calls take(); there is no retention and no read verb
- **Mechanism.** take() = pending() + path.unlink(); heartbeat _inbox(consume=True) -> IB.wake -> IB.take. Nothing is kept, so tail/cut loses the text permanently.
- **Falsifier.** on unfixed code, IB.delivered / IB._delivered_dir do not exist and take() deletes, so a test that reads the message after take fails; on fixed code it passes

**Probe:**


## Should ddflow support UTCP (Universal Tool Calling Protocol), northbound and southbound?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Premature as a first-class surface; worth narrow protocol-neutral groundwork and a watch. UTCP is a young community-governed standard (spec 1.0, Python SDK first released 2025-07-10, 1.2.0 on 2026-09-16) with no documented support in any of ddflow six harnesses, and a consent and trust model ddflow would have to supply itself. UNVERIFIED in part: adoption among ddflow harnesses (one search, no tracker checked), registry design, gRPC support, dependency list, commit activity and contributor count.
- **Mechanism.** UTCP manuals list tools with call templates (HTTP, SSE, CLI, text, WebSocket, MCP bridge) that clients call directly. A northbound ddflow manual would map to CLI call templates running ddflow verbs, bypassing the MCP identity and lease path; a southbound client would let ddflow call HTTP tools without an MCP wrapper but would take provider-supplied call templates that decide where requests and commands go.
- **Falsifier.** Any of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Kilo or Cursor ships documented UTCP support, or UTCP gets neutral governance, or published hardening of manuals and CLI templates: then the verdict is reopened.
- **Budget.** one researcher agent, 15 tool calls

**Sources:** https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/utcp-specification, https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp, https://www.utcp.io/about/about-us, https://pypi.org/project/utcp/, https://www.mend.io/vulnerability-database/CVE-2026-101057/, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.22489

## Does ddflow baseline-red compare only failing test ids, so a new offender in a test already red on the base goes unseen?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-baseline-red-hides-new-offender-in-red-ratchet`

- **Claim.** A failing test id that also fails on the base is always attributed as baseline-red (still_failing) because the comparison uses the id's presence in the base's failing list only, never its failure text; a branch that clears or adds an offender inside an already-red test is hidden.
- **Mechanism.** services/gates/baseline_red.py _verdicts/_tally decide still-failing by 'i in failing' (id membership); the failure text (failed_reasons) is discarded, so an id the base also fails keeps reading baseline-red when the branch changed its assertion output.
- **Falsifier.** If the id-only comparison suffices, a test red on the base with a DIFFERENT failure text on the branch still records partial baseline-red; if a new offender must read as FAILED/new, the text has to be compared.

## Why does a --delta review re-raise a confirmed finding whose fix predates the delta's base?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B2e1f4aedb5`

- **Claim.** A delta review re-sends a CONFIRMED finding a later delta already cleared, whose fix diff is absent, so the reviewer reports it again as unfixed.
- **Mechanism.** context._with_previous_findings lists every prior chunk_finding with its triage for a delta; a confirmed-and-cleared finding (fixed before the delta's base) is not visible in the delta diff, so the reviewer cannot verify the fix and reports 'the named probe is not in this diff'.
- **Falsifier.** The regression test test_a_confirmed_finding_cleared_by_a_delta_is_not_re_sent_in_a_later_delta fails on the unfixed code.

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run pytest -q tests/test_gate_econ_rereview.py::test_a_confirmed_finding_cleared_by_a_delta_is_not_re_sent_in_a_later_delta
FAILED on unfixed code: assert 'bad line' not in second_delta (confirmed finding still re-sent); PASSED after the fix.
```

## What debugging, investigation, research, reverse-engineering and safe-execution capability does ddflow have and plan on 2026-11-05, and where are the gaps and hosts for new work?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Built and wired: bisect (test-file polluter ddmin only, no commit bisect), bug repro bundle and repro-cmd run at a recorded sha, regression fail-before verify, gate verify mutation, verify, flake log, tests selection, recall, similar, research notes (verdict required at filing, immutable, no open-hypothesis state). 'ddflow probe' is a git merge-conflict probe and 'ddflow replay' rebuilds decision history from the log: neither is a debugging tool. Absent in code: any process isolation (no rlimit, namespace, seccomp, container call), any debugger, tracer, dump or binary tool, any kind or pipeline for an investigation (kind=research runs the full implementation pipeline). Planned but far: RE-debug-flow wave 35 with 242 open transitive needs, RF-ledger wave 22 with 118, RF-run wave 23 with 123, RE-accept wave 37 with 341 against the P-reimpl kill date 2026-12-03. Cheap roots exist: SEC-sandbox, TM-target, TM-defect-model, QA-f2p-task, DX-bug-repro-gate-and-mcp, DX-command-log, RE-decide are all wave 0 with no open needs. Decided without a task: debugger and disassembler MCP adapters (D-reimpl-answers point 4 appears only as a sentence in RE-ledger-ingest). New phases are under the D-scope-focus-2026-11 intake freeze until open tasks are under 1500 (2614 open).
- **Mechanism.** The generally useful debug flow was filed as a template behind RS-templates, and RS-templates needs RF-docs, which needs every shipped flow (math, hw, dsp, ml, panel, delegate), so a small template inherits the whole research programme. Execution safety was deferred to SEC-sandbox, which three tracks (RE, TM, RQ) wait on and nobody has started. The research record stores conclusions, so a live hypothesis has nowhere to go until the reasoning log, itself behind P-decisions and P-org-config.
- **Falsifier.** A code search finds a process-isolation call or a debugger or tracer integration in ddflow/, or RE-debug-flow has an open closure under 50, or a task body names a debugger adapter as its deliverable.
- **Budget.** one read-only session, no test suite

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow --json list task (4593 rows, 5 pages) and list phase --limit 1000; open-closure script over needs plus inherited phase needs; ddflow waves --check; git grep -E 'unshare|bwrap|firejail|nsjail|seccomp|setrlimit|RLIMIT_|landlock' and 'gdb|lldb|pdb|strace|ltrace|debugpy|valgrind|py-spy|coredump|objdump|ghidra|radare|frida' over ddflow/; body scan of task events; read services/{bisect,probe,reprobundle,reprocheck,verify,flakes}.py and gates/mutation.py; throwaway repo probe of bug found --repro-cmd and MCP evidence.
Isolation grep: only docker-run string matchers and doc text; jinja SandboxedEnvironment for templates only. Debugger grep over ddflow/: 0 hits. Waves check: 0 stale stamps. Closures: RE-debug-flow 242, RS-templates 241, RF-docs 240, RF-template 60, RF-ledger 118, RF-run 123, TF-flows-code 139, RE-sandbox-gate 67, TM-safety 65, SEC-hunt-engine 4, SEC-sandbox 0, TM-target 0, RE-accept 341. Tasks: 2614 open, 25 running, 3 blocked. Bugs 1459: reproduced recorded on 18 (16 yes, 2 no); 1026 of 1046 fixed carry a regression test. Research 1542: 1413 confirmed, 89 theoretical, 40 refuted. Flake log 49 lines. Probe: both markers written outside the scratch tree and a host variable appeared in the stored output (filed B18cd856a67).
```

## What external practice and tooling (2026) should ddflow adopt to debug applications, libraries, snippets and tests, investigate hard bugs, do lawful reverse engineering and validate hypotheses, and what should go through adapters versus be left alone?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** ddflow should own the investigation RECORD (hypothesis, pre-committed prediction and falsifier, probe, verdict validated/refuted/inconclusive, repro bundle, budget cap) and reach tools only through thin optional subprocess adapters; the published evidence says structure and function-level state beat raw debugger access: bare pdb gained 0.8 points at +$0.60 per task while a function-level interface gained 8.8 points at +$0.26 (arXiv 2604.24212), naive reproduction tests did not help patching while multi-faceted runtime-grounded ones did (arXiv 2607.00990), and LLM refinement of decompiled code raised build rate 75 to 90 percent while behavioural match fell 74 to 62 percent (arXiv 2609.05370), so parity needs differential oracles, not build or shipped-test passes.
- **Mechanism.** Adapters per r-adapters: sandbox (docker first, gVisor/Firecracker later), debug (DAP via debugpy or mcp-debugger, summarised and capped), reduce (predicate contract shared with git bisect exit codes 0/1-127/125), fuzz/property (Hypothesis, Atheris), trace (py-spy, faulthandler), bench (hyperfine, pyperf), re-readonly (Ghidra headless, rizin). Conflicts to settle: D-reimpl-answers item 4 says read-only adapters but DAP evaluate and Ghidra script tools run code, so those must be withheld or sandbox-only; rr in Docker needs SYS_PTRACE plus a loosened seccomp profile, which weakens r-re-sandbox, so rr is own-code only. Run GPL/AGPL tools as separate processes, never import or vendor them (licence effect inferred, not legal advice).
- **Falsifier.** On a seeded set of hard bugs in own code, runs using the investigation record plus function-level trace adapter show no better fix rate, and no lower token cost, than the same agent with shell access alone; or an adapter proves unable to keep the sandbox class limits on this host.
- **Budget.** no paid model calls; web research plus read-only host probes

**Probe:**

```console
$ Read-only host probe: command -v for each tool; /proc/sys/kernel/{perf_event_paranoid,yama/ptrace_scope,apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns}; readlink /proc/self/ns/user and Seccomp in /proc/self/status to exclude nesting; bwrap --unshare-all and --unshare-net; docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --memory 256m --pids-limit 64 on local image ddflow:pytest; perf stat; bpftrace; gdb -p on a non-child; gdb --args; py-spy record -- cmd
PRESENT gdb 15.1, strace, perf, bpftrace, bwrap 0.9.0, docker 29.9.2 (runc, cgroup v2), rootless podman 4.9.3, uv, py-spy 0.4.2, gcc. ABSENT rr valgrind lldb runsc firecracker nix ghidra r2 rizin frida afl-fuzz cvise creduce hyperfine clang. Ubuntu 24.04. perf_event_paranoid=4 and perf stat refused; ptrace_scope=1 and gdb attach to a non-child refused, gdb --args and py-spy launch worked; bpftrace: root only; /dev/kvm exists, not accessible to this user; ulimit -c 0 and core_pattern=apport; apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 and bwrap failed (uid map Permission denied; RTM_NEWADDR not permitted) in the initial user namespace with Seccomp 0, so not a nesting artefact; docker no-network, read-only, cap-drop run succeeded.
```

**Sources:** https://arxiv.org/html/2503.21557, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.24212, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00990, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08717, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.06749v3, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09858, https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.02195, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16354, https://arxiv.org/html/2404.05427v3, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01185, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05370, https://github.com/debugmcpdev/mcp-debugger, https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/specification, https://rr-project.org/, https://github.com/rr-debugger/rr, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bisect, https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/, https://gvisor.dev/docs/architecture_guide/security/, https://gvisor.dev/docs/architecture_guide/platforms/, https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md, https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime, https://github.com/google/nsjail, https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra, https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin, https://github.com/angr/angr, https://github.com/google/bindiff, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/1201, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/24/article/6, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/24/article/5

## Can the core tier of tools/list return under the 40,000 ratchet by cutting rationale text only, with no tool or argument dropped and no CLI help changed?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-main-red-core-tools-budget`

- **Claim.** Removing explanatory rationale from seven core argument descriptions and the shared relation text brings core from 40,538 to under 40,000. Lean and families need nothing: B66b0d8218e-2 already put them under their limits.
- **Mechanism.** tools/list serves Param.help. The chosen params set cli_help separately, so the MCP text can shrink without moving any CLI help. Text is counted once per listing tool, and relation repeats in 4 core tools.

## Does the forbidden-command guard miss commands after a semicolon when the line holds a multi-line quoted string?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-forbidden-guard-multiline-quote-bypass`

- **Claim.** A multi-line quoted string stops _split from treating ; as a command separator, so commands after the ; are never matched.
- **Mechanism.** _split tokenizes each physical line separately. A quote spanning a newline makes shlex raise ValueError on the line that opens it, so the line.split() fallback is used, which leaves ; glued to the preceding word (-q;, main;), and the after-; commands are swallowed into the first command.
- **Falsifier.** check('echo a; git push origin main; python3 -c "<newline>print(1)"') returns a Refusal naming git push instead of None.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 - run _split/check on the repro line in the worktree
split -> [['echo','a;','git','push','origin','main;','python3','-c','"']]; check -> None (one-line form is refused)
```

## When ddflow creates a task, can it estimate complexity and change size (files, lines), tag it and write it in the description, so the optimizer and gate merging can use it? How accurate, what is stored, and which decisions are safe on an estimate?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `GV-complexity-score`

- **Claim.** MEASURED, all 1,547 items with task.added+worktree.merged+item.completed (2026-09-28..11-05), rolling-origin test on 1,145 items trained only on items merged before each block. Size = added+deleted lines of landed_before..landed_after excluding generated paths. Buckets <=50, <=150, <=400, <=1000, >1000. Deterministic creation-time features are moderately useful for RANK, weak for buckets: naive modal hit 28.5%, within-one 70%; compact 9-feature ridge with text-kNN rho 0.515, hit 35.6%, within-one 77.6%; 56-feature boosted model rho 0.525, 35.6%, 79.0%; at claim rho 0.564. Median error x2.7. Most of it is between kinds: within-kind rho bugfix 0.23, phase task 0.34, dx 0.37, auto CI fix 0.15, doc 0.11, split/move -0.17. Model judgement beats it: a blind rating of title, body and globs by this session's model (no extra paid call), 140 items in two seeded samples, rho 0.825 vs 0.552 on the same items, hit 51% vs 33%, within-one 95% vs 80%; on 60 phase tasks (the open queue's shape) 0.84 vs 0.48, paired bootstrap difference 95% CI 0.20..0.56. Filers' 'Effort N days' notes: rho 0.77, n=19. Cost is not predictable beyond size: actual lines vs findings 0.51, gate seconds 0.52, rounds 0.34, confirmed HIGH 0.27; direct creation-time models rounds 0.10, gate seconds 0.16, with MAE worse than a constant median. Underestimates: boosted est<=150 lines n=437: 29.7% over 150, 8.7% over 400, 1.6% over 1000; those items hold 20% of confirmed HIGH and 22% of confirmed MEDIUM+ findings; est<=50 n=161 still has a confirmed MEDIUM+ finding in 24.8%. Blind model est<=150 n=56: 3.6% over 400 (Wilson 1-12%). So estimates may order, plan and tighten but never lighten a gate; gates already have the actual diff. Optimizer value is small: makespan -3.7% with estimated duration (oracle -8.9%), mean finish -7.7% (oracle -18.5%). THEORETICAL: the storage design (one estimate field feeding GV-complexity-score, snapshot in lease.acquired, ddflow metrics estimate) is not built; a cheap model's accuracy is untested.
- **Mechanism.** Extends, does not replace, GV-complexity-score (r-one-complexity; inputs globs, needs, size, rework, rounds), P-governor.tier-heuristic, TA-signals/TA-add-wire (proposal block), EX-providers (cost-term, Candidate.facts), FT-lane (ordering hint only) and WP-merge-detect-tasks. Why deterministic features plateau: globs cover only 64% of changed files on average (36% fully, 9% none; median precision 0.67; #globs vs real files rho 0.39) and 22% of merged items had none at add, so glob counts say little about work; the scope lives in the body text, which only a reader understands. The estimate is valuable only BEFORE work: at gate time the real diff costs one git call (24 ms each here). Inputs change: 36% of items change between add and claim (globs 26%, body 11%, needs 11%); bucket flips in 35% at claim (54% when globs changed), 2.6% by two buckets or more. Drift: per-block rho 0.30..0.68; p90 conformal bound covered 83% against a nominal 90%, width x3.9. Population shift: open queue is 92% phase tasks and 8% bugfix, merged sample 41% bugfix, so the hard stratum dominates. No task has ever carried a tier: tag (0 in the log), so GV-complexity-score's falsifier 'no better than the tag' compares with nothing and D-path-merge's tier:deep exclusion is a no-op. Task merge cap: on the 140 rated items random pairs estimated <=400 combined really exceed 400 in 51% (deterministic) and 28.5% (model).
- **Falsifier.** A rerun on the next 300 merged items where the compact deterministic estimate falls below rho 0.40 or within-one below 72% (estimate not worth keeping); or a filer-declared or cheap-model estimate that does not beat it by at least 0.10 rho on 100 phase tasks (drop the model input); or est<=150 items over 400 lines above 10%.
- **Budget.** one session, 140 model ratings in-session, no extra paid calls, no test suites

**Probe:**

```console
$ python folds in the session scratchpad: events joined to git diff --numstat --no-renames landed_before landed_after (1,584 diffs, 38 s); features from task.added only, tree and churn as of the creation day; history features use only items merged before creation; numpy ridge and boosted stumps; seven rolling blocks of 180; blind samples seed 20261105 (n=80) and 777 (n=60), 25 outlier ids already seen excluded, outcomes unseen until rated.
n=1547 test=1145; modal hit .285; kind rho .387; globs .367; text stats .270; repo size+churn .283; text-kNN .417; ridge all+hist .527/.364/.788; GBM .525/.356/.790; claim .564/.369/.804; compact+kNN .515/.356/.776; compact no history .441/.329/.769; AUC >400 .769, <=50 .769, any HIGH .616, tiny code fix .678 (precision .105 at lowest 20%, base .052); confusion est<=S 437: >150 .297 >400 .087 >1000 .016 HIGH .085 MED+ .38; all test >400 .252 HIGH .151 MED+ .507; blind n=80 .792 vs .581, n=60 .837 vs .478, pooled .825 vs .552; LPT est cycle .963, oracle .911; SPT est cycle .923, oracle .815
```

## Can the wait-cycle victim follow progress, and can a stuck wait raise an alarm, from facts ddflow already has, with no new event kind and no cost on a queue with no stuck wait?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DX-wait-cycle-followups`

- **Claim.** leasebreak.progress_at plus the live-gate registry and running jobs give a per-lease watermark, so leasewait stays pure (Held.progress_at), the victim is the least-progress holder, and an alarm is a wait older than a knob whose leases in the way all show no work for as long.
- **Mechanism.** Held carries the watermark; find() ranks ring members by it, falling back to the youngest wait on a tie. progress_of is lazy, so it reads the log and git only once a cycle or an aged wait exists.
- **Falsifier.** A holder with the older wait but the newer watermark still being chosen as the victim, or a working holder still raising an alarm, or a queue with no wait reading the log.
- **Budget.** 15 min, no GPU

## Do the control planes and ACP adapters do what R-control-planes assumed: Paseo hooks, .mcp.json and pre-made worktree adoption; the Harness Remote API; ACP adapters honoring an injected MCP server and cwd; adoption in AgentOS, Orca, Emdash?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `CP-verify-facts`

- **Claim.** An ACP agent honours an injected stdio MCP server and the session cwd (seen live on kilo 7.8.18; read in source for claude-agent-acp 0.100.0, codex-acp 2.5.0, opencode 2.2.5, gemini-cli), and the planes differ: Paseo reads no .mcp.json itself and adopts a worktree only as a plain directory, Harness Remote injects nothing, Emdash auto-adopts and can force-delete.
- **Mechanism.** ACP session/new carries cwd and mcpServers, which the spec requires agents to honour for stdio. Planes own their own workspace records, so adoption and deletion depend on each plane's ownership proof, read at pinned commits; only a tool on this machine could be run.
- **Falsifier.** The stub MCP server not starting, or starting in the spawn directory instead of the session cwd, when kilo acp receives session/new.
- **Budget.** Public docs and source only; no install; one live run of the kilo binary already on this machine, no model call

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 -I probes/probe_acp_mcp_inject.py 'kilo acp'; negative control: python3 -I probes/probe_acp_mcp_inject.py '/bin/true' 3
kilo: {"mcpCapabilities": {"http": true, "sse": true}} {"session_error": null} {"started": true, "env_passed": true, "initialized": true, "tools_listed": true, "cwd_is_session": true, "cwd_is_spawn": false} exit=0. /bin/true: {"mcpCapabilities": null} {"session_error": "no answer"} {"started": false, "env_passed": false, "initialized": false, "tools_listed": false, "cwd_is_session": false, "cwd_is_spawn": false} exit=1.
```

**Sources:** https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo, https://github.com/giuliastro/harness-remote, https://github.com/monperrus/harness-remote, https://github.com/saadnvd1/agent-os, https://github.com/stablyai/orca, https://github.com/generalaction/emdash, https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp, https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp, https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode, https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli, https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-setup, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp

## Can every Config() default and the default gates be written as one packaged TOML file and read as the lowest layer without changing a value or slowing the hook path materially?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `CE-defaults-file`

- **Claim.** The 541 knobs across 50 sections render as TOML literals that parse back equal, independent of host and hash seed, in about 16 KB; the 16 default gates add about 8.5 KB when fields equal to GateDef defaults are left out. Parsing once per process and comparing instead of re-coercing costs about 3 ms per process and nothing measurable per later load.
- **Mechanism.** tomlcfg.value renders plain values; no section default reads the environment, the host or a set; Config._apply costs 3.5 ms because it coerces each knob, so applying only the knobs that differ from the dataclass value skips it while the pin keeps the two equal.
- **Falsifier.** A default with no TOML form (None, tuple, set), a value that differs between PYTHONHASHSEED runs, or a parse above 15 ms.

**Probe:**

```console
$ scratch proto.py in the worktree at a9a8da595: render Config(), tomllib round trip each value, time parse and _apply over 20 runs, repeat under PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1, 7
knobs 541 sections 50 bytes 16299 none 0; bad 0; parse ms 3.27; apply ms 3.58; load none ms 0.39; sha ca7d5820a1ff5d1b for all three seeds; gates 8465 bytes
```

## Can one bound credential close the operator-only gap, or does each operator verb need its own role check?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `P-remote.auth`

- **Claim.** Every operator-only verb reaches identity.agent_marker or is_agent, and no caller yet feeds a paired credential into resolve_actor, so a credential bound once in services/identity and read by agent_marker, is_agent and resolve_actor applies one role check to all of them with no per-verb edit.
- **Mechanism.** agent_marker is the only person-or-agent test: 18 modules ask it (approval.grant, grants.add, chore, reviewer_trust, export select, complete, claim force, config set). Today it reads only --agent, DDFLOW_AGENT and CLAUDECODE, so with no marker it answers person: that is the convention. resolve_actor takes credential_role but only the harness attest path passes one.
- **Falsifier.** An operator-only verb that decides person-or-agent without agent_marker or is_agent.
- **Budget.** 15 min, greps only

**Probe:**

```console
$ git grep -c -E '\b(agent_marker|is_agent)\(' -- 'ddflow/*.py'; git grep -n 'credential_role=' -- 'ddflow/*.py'; env -u CLAUDECODE -u DDFLOW_AGENT python3 -c "from ddflow.services.identity import agent_marker as a; print(repr(a()))"; git grep -n -E 'DDFLOW_TOKEN|token\.issued' -- 'ddflow/*.py'
19 files carry the call (ddflow/api/chore.py:1, api/gates/_run.py:1, api/gates/_vet.py:1, api/lifecycle/claim.py:2, api/lifecycle/complete/approval.py:3, api/pin_files.py:1, api/setup/config.py:1, api/surf_setup.py:1, services/actors.py:1, services/approval.py:1, services/approvals/answer.py:1, services/approvals/relayed.py:1, services/export/select.py:1, services/gate_accept.py:1, services/grants.py:1, services/identity.py:3, services/phase_complete.py:1, services/repairs/accepted.py:1, services/reviewer_trust.py:1). credential_role=: only ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:450. agent_marker with no markers: ''. DDFLOW_TOKEN / token.issued: no hit.
```

## Can one HumanChannel port (notify, ask, relay) cover terminal, harness bridge, desktop, email, Slack, Teams, webhook, n8n and OpenClaw, keeping the digest and person-only checks in the ask engine alone, with no existing notifier to fold in?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `ADP-notify-ask`

- **Claim.** One port suffices: outbound adapters only post and report pending, the harness bridge couriers and reads through attest, the terminal collects; services/ask relays every collected answer through engine.answer, which already holds the digest and identity checks, so no adapter repeats them. No second notifier exists in ddflow today.
- **Mechanism.** adapters is the bottom layer and cannot import the engine, so a channel returns data (Answer) and a service above records it. engine.answer refuses an actor whose source is not terminal, credential or named, and compares the presented digest with the row's. attest already records harness answers at level 2, so the bridge calls it rather than repeating it.
- **Falsifier.** An existing notify-send, osascript or smtplib implementation in ddflow, or a wire format of a target that cannot be expressed as one JSON POST with an optional bearer header.
- **Budget.** 20 min, no network calls from code

**Probe:**

```console
$ grep -rnE 'notify-send|osascript|smtplib' ddflow; read services/ask/engine.py answer and _check_answerable, services/approvals/harness.py attest; opened the Slack, Teams and OpenClaw webhook docs
grep exit 1 (no match). engine.answer: 'if actor.source not in ANSWER_SOURCES: raise AskRefused', _check_answerable compares digest != row['digest']. Slack: POST {"text": ...}, 200 'ok'. Teams: Office 365 connectors retired May 2026; Workflows webhook takes {"type":"message","attachments":[{contentType adaptive card}]}. OpenClaw: POST /hooks/agent {"message", "name"}, Authorization: Bearer hook token, query tokens rejected, 200 admitted.
```

**Sources:** https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/sending-messages-using-incoming-webhooks, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/webhooks-and-connectors/how-to/connectors-using, https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/webhooks

## Can SE-workflow-template land as one item on today's main, and does landing it unblock SE-packs and CP-kits?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `SE-workflow-template`

- **Claim.** No to both. It is five separable deliverables, it rests on layers and a field type that do not exist, it needs undecided design answers, and SE-packs stays blocked after it lands because B-org-bundle and B-org-layers are open.
- **Mechanism.** Missing: (a) org layer and conf.d: CE-defaults-file -> CE-layer-stack -> CE-confd-loader / B-org-layers -> B-org-bundle are all open, no 'conf.d' in ddflow/*.py, services/overlay.py resolves only config/project/builtin, with no local or org, and the item has no edge to any of them. (b) FIELD_TYPES is string, integer, boolean, array of strings, so a nested stage list cannot be a record field; kinddata refuses code keys, so a data kind has no behavioural validator. Undecided: Q1 source of truth: log record (r-log-is-the-state), overlay files, or conf.d fragments plus a record kind (docs/ddflow/research/config-internal.md, a research line, no decision). Q2 land with the org seam empty, or wait for B-org-layers. Q3 generator: derive kind_pipelines at load, or write config.changed, and who wins against a hand-set [gates].kind_pipelines. Q4 verb home: `ddflow workflow` is taken by state/pipeline/gate/drop; `workflow template <verb>` or `workflow <name> <verb>` (B-rw-workflow text). Title order is stale: D-config-layer-order supersedes it and adds user, env, CLI, session and enforced layers. PROPOSED SPLIT: .1 format: pure parser and validator with file:line, core only, no dependency. .2 record kind: template as a record under RC1-RC12, after Q1 and the field-type answer. .3 layered loader on OverlayLoader with provenance, after Q1/Q2. .4 generator: stages to kind_pipelines and plan skeleton, after Q3. .5 verbs show/edit/reset/diff/explain on CLI and MCP, knobs, upgrade fragments and docs, after Q4. Plus one org-layer task needing B-org-layers. Only .1 can start now. Critical path for SE-packs and CP-kits is CE-defaults-file (no needs).
- **Falsifier.** An existing org or local layer in the overlay loader or Config.load, an object field type in FIELD_TYPES, a decision record settling template storage, or SE-packs having no open need besides SE-workflow-template.
- **Budget.** read-only survey, no worktree, no tests run

**Probe:**

```console
$ git grep 'conf\.d' -- 'ddflow/*.py'; sed services/overlay.py; grep FIELD_TYPES ddflow/api/records/_kind.py; ddflow --json show CE-defaults-file|CE-layer-stack|CE-confd-loader|B-org-layers|B-org-bundle; ddflow --json next; ddflow workflow --help
git grep conf.d: no hits. overlay.py: BUILTIN, PROJECT, CONFIG only. FIELD_TYPES = ("string", "integer", "boolean", "array"). CE-defaults-file open needs []; CE-layer-stack open needs [CE-defaults-file]; CE-confd-loader open needs [CE-layer-stack]; B-org-layers open needs [CE-layer-stack]; B-org-bundle open needs [CE-confd-loader]. next: SE-packs blocked 'B-org-bundle is open; B-org-layers is open; SE-workflow-template is open'; CP-kits blocked 'P-remote.gateways is open; CP-verify-facts is running; SE-packs is open'. workflow subcommands: state, pipeline, gate, drop.
```

**Sources:** ddflow/services/overlay.py, ddflow/api/records/_kind.py, ddflow/core/kinddata.py, docs/ddflow/research/config-internal.md

## Where must a reserved parallelism slot be enforced and reported, and can it be done without touching the files UX-output-caps holds?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DX-reserved-slot`

- **Claim.** The cap exists only in plan()'s cut (claim does not apply it to a named item), so the reservation belongs in the optimizer cut; and next, status and brief all print strings core owns (Plan.summary, Plan.parallel_line), so reporting needs no surface file.
- **Mechanism.** Ordinary work may hold at most cap minus reserved slots; a single walk in offer order with one extra per-class limit keeps priority order, and the total cap already covers bug fixes that overflow the reserved share.
- **Falsifier.** A cap check inside claim, or a next/status/brief renderer printing the limit from anything other than Plan.summary or Plan.parallel_line.

**Probe:**

```console
$ grep -n 'does not apply' ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py; grep -rn 'p\.summary()\|plan\.summary()\|plan\.parallel_line\|p\.parallel_line' ddflow --include='*.py'
wait.py:109: # LIST and `claim` does not apply it to a named item, so `_claim_blocker` never (pinned by tests/test_wait.py:599 test_a_cap_blocked_item_wait_agrees_with_claim). services/leases/claim.py has no cap reference. Readers: views/markdown/briefing.py:259 plan.parallel_line; surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:275 p.summary(); api/operations.py:195 plan.summary(); api/lifecycle/ready.py:97 p.summary(); api/lifecycle/wait.py:242,264 p.summary(); api/reporting/overview.py:190,289 p.parallel_line; set at core/schedule/_plan.py:236.
```

## Is a cold load with the marshal read snapshot on slower than with it off on a real-sized log, and what does a parsed event really cost in memory?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `PS-snapshot-calibrate`

- **Claim.** With the snapshot on, a cold load is slower than parsing the log, on the real log and at 200k to 1M synthetic events, so default-off is right. A parsed event costs 1.4 to 2.5 KB of retained memory, not the 736 bytes the knob doc says, so a 200,000-event ceiling holds about 300 to 500 MB rather than 147 MB.
- **Mechanism.** The snapshot does not avoid the expensive work: `_seed_from_snapshot` re-hashes every shard's real bytes (the hash is the trust check) and then unmarshals all objects, which costs more than C json parsing of the same lines, and the frames sit in memory beside the decoded objects, hence the higher peak. The 736-byte figure came from B86's bench, whose events are tiny `task.added` rows; real events carry gate evidence (880 bytes on disk per event here).
- **Falsifier.** Median cold read_all with the snapshot on is below off on the real log, measured in fresh processes with the snapshot verified in use (0 lines parsed, every shard seeded).
- **Budget.** about 40 min, read-only on the real log (copied to scratch), no installs. Not measured: a truly cold disk (the eviction is advisory and only the file pages), and R-scalability's 1.1 GB at 500k was with the fold in the process, which this read_all figure excludes.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Scratch scripts one.py/run.sh/seeded.py. Fresh process per run, EventLog.read_all, code at branch head 4e6272fe5, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. Log: copy of .ddflow/events (137,407 events, 915 files, 121 MB) and logfixture.generate(seed=7) at 200k/500k/1M; separate on and off copies because snapshot=false deletes the files. 7 interleaved off/on pairs for each of 2 cache states: 'keep' (page cache warm) and 'evict' (posix_fadvise DONTNEED on shards and snapshot). Snapshot written by a prior run, snapshot_max_mb raised so it is kept at every size. Memory: tracemalloc retained bytes after gc with the result list dropped, plus RSS from /proc/self/statm in an untraced run. seeded.py wraps _parse_lines and _seed_from_snapshot. R-scalability read in full first: its finding 3 is the same claim at 132k.
Median s, off vs on (min-max): real 137,407 keep 2.60 (2.22-2.75) vs 3.38 (3.00-3.72); evict 2.99 (2.60-3.65) vs 4.05 (3.57-4.30). fx 200,031 keep 1.99 vs 2.60; evict 2.07 vs 2.71. fx 500,026 keep 5.58 (5.42-6.13) vs 7.14 (4.55-7.48); evict 5.71 vs 7.26 (4.68-8.02). fx 1,000,013 keep 12.59 vs 14.74; evict 12.91 vs 15.11. On faster in adjacent pairs: real 0/14, 200k 0/14, 500k 2/14, 1M 0/14. Peak RSS MB off vs on: real 402 vs 602, 200k 365 vs 548, 500k 870 vs 1336, 1M 1679 vs 2596. Snapshot file MB: 113.3, 112.3, 281.7, 559.8. seeded.py on-run: real 137407 events, 0 lines parsed, 915 shards seeded, 0 not seeded, not rewritten, 3.05-3.07 s x4; 500k 0 lines parsed, 40 seeded, 7.39-7.94 s x4. Retained memory by tracemalloc: real 339.2 MB = 2469 B/event; fx200k 294.0 MB = 1470; fx500k 732.0 MB = 1464; fx1M 1388.5 MB = 1388. RSS after load, off, untraced: real 407 MB, 200k 375, 500k 892, 1M 1670 (27 MB before the load). Load average during the runs 16-78 on 192 cores.
```

**Sources:** ddflow/infra/log/_read.py, ddflow/infra/log/_guard.py, ddflow/infra/shardmeta.py, ddflow/services/logfixture.py, tests/bench_log_read.py

## How does the time to add and test one feature grow as the code grows, and which parts grow worse than linearly?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Change size is flat, selection is flat, and active item time grew about linearly with code (small items 38-50 min to about 120 min for code x2.6). Superlinear parts: suite CPU (tests x per-test start cost, about code^1.9), fold-based commands (brief exponent about 2.4 on log size, doctor about 5), and always-run's slowest test. The largest cost today is not growth in code: 68% of claim-to-merge hours since 10-26 are parked, and main has been red in every full run since 10-28, floor 281 failures, ci pass rate 1.5%, 88% of completions forced.
- **Mechanism.** Every run_cli test starts a subprocess that imports the whole CLI; start time is linear in code (0.15 s at 33k LOC, 0.87 s at 196k) and tests are linear in code, so the product is quadratic. Workers are capped at 48 on 192 cores with one slot, so CPU converts directly to wall and queue. Fold commands rescan a log linear in time. on_merge=fast runs no tests, so repo-wide guards go red unseen.
- **Falsifier.** A fixed test sample whose CPU does not rise across commits under equal load; or a per-test duration profile of a real run showing the suite's cost concentrated in a few tests rather than a flat per-process tax.
- **Budget.** about 1.5 h, no suite lock

**Probe:**

```console
$ Scripts over .ddflow/events and .ddflow/runs; git history per day; `python -m ddflow --version` at 7 commits; 24 fixed test files at 5 commits with BLAS capped, in throwaway clones; TR.reach for every module at 6 commits; select() replay of 23 merges; always-run list with --durations=0; ddflow command timings.
Tests 1,707 to 18,442; src LOC 33k to 196k. Best suite run 52 s to 1,896 s; full run about 72,000 CPU-s, n=48 on all 230 runs since 10-19. Fixed sample CPU 385, 652, 783, 850, 757 s at 76k..196k LOC (one run each, load 24 to 92). Claim-to-merge p50 45 to 255 min; files per merge p50 4 to 3. Selection 5.9-8.9% of suite files; small change replay median 4.5 files plus 22-24 always; import reach p50 12 to 2. Full fallback 18% to 25%. Always-run 118 s wall, two files 64%. brief 4.9 to 40 s, doctor 7.8 to 932 s. Full findings: session scratchpad cycle-time-findings.md. Unexplained: 72k CPU-s is above what the samples predict (28-50k); no per-test durations exist after 10-12.
```

**Sources:** R-test-duration-2026-10-12, R-perf-profile-2026-10-11, R-hot-split-queue-wide, Rc248888254, Rd8b97ba0c2

## Is tree_fingerprint blind to a re-edit of an already-dirty tracked binary file?

**Verdict: REFUTED** · item `B95`

- **Claim.** git diff renders a tracked binary as "Binary files ... differ" with no content, so a second edit of an already-modified tracked binary leaves tree_fingerprint unchanged (B95, docs/BACKLOG.md:1142).
- **Mechanism.** Claimed: the digest input is the text of `git diff HEAD`, and that text was assumed to hold nothing about binary content. Actual: git diff prints the header line `index <old>..<new>` for a binary too, and <new> is the blob id git computes from the working copy (diff_fill_oid_info hashes it), so the rendered text changes whenever the bytes do. tree_identity, which gates record since B-uni-tree-identity, names full blob ids and never relied on the diff text.
- **Falsifier.** tree_fingerprint returns the same value before and after a same-size second edit of a modified tracked binary.
- **Budget.** 20 min, local git only

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run python scratch probe_b95.py / probe_b95_matrix.py on main e234caf3c, git 2.43.0: real repo, commit a NUL-bearing asset.bin, edit it, fingerprint, edit again to the same size, fingerprint; matrix over staged, new staged, attr binary, attr -diff, same mtime, core.bigFileThreshold=1k, core.abbrev=4

edit 1    fp 432637c0812f+8c80e9462bfbbaa1 id 432637c0812f+st:40a821d2ce43dc8bc5f629f91f49683e
diff --git a/asset.bin b/asset.bin
index fa46a01..82232df 100644
Binary files a/asset.bin and b/asset.bin differ

edit 2    fp 432637c0812f+90edecc9c84979bc id 432637c0812f+st:b42cfb493488e1ebb92e5a46712ce285
fingerprint moved: True | tree_identity moved: True
worktree edit, default                     fingerprint_moved=True  identity_moved=True
staged first edit, then re-edit            fingerprint_moved=True  identity_moved=True

attr: *.bin binary                         fingerprint_moved=True  identity_moved=True
attr: *.bin -diff                          fingerprint_moved=True  identity_moved=True
```

## Can the shutil path operations live in adapters.fs with infra.fsio delegating, without a layer violation?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `ADP-fs`

- **Claim.** adapters is the bottom layer, so the implementation must sit in adapters.fs and infra.fsio (above) delegates; the fsio-home contract extended with shutil then keeps with the 29 current importers baselined.
- **Mechanism.** import-linter layers forbids adapters->infra but allows infra->adapters; a forbidden-module contract with per-module ignore files ratchets.
- **Falsifier.** test_import_contracts reports the layers or fsio-home contract BROKEN or an unmatched ignore.

## Does a hedge copy of a chunk whose first copy returned DID NOT CONVERGE ever converge, or is it a deterministic repeat of the same timeout?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-review-chunk-timeout-not-enforced`

- **Claim.** A reviewer chunk whose first copy returns DID NOT CONVERGE (or TRUNCATED) is deterministically doomed: a hedge copy is the same chunk with the same budget and timeout, so it must fail identically. Cancelling the hedge twin and settling the chunk at once stops a lost chunk waiting hedge x timeout_s.
- **Mechanism.** In review._race, a queued hedge copy started only after the first timed out (max_concurrency=1 queues it), so a non-converging chunk burned hedge x timeout_s before reporting DID NOT CONVERGE, while the progress tick claimed each request is cut at timeout_s.
- **Falsifier.** The hedge copy succeeds where the first copy DID NOT CONVERGE (an identical request converging on retry under identical budget/timeout).

**Probe:**

```console
$ Reviewer(kind=command, hedge=2, timeout_s=2, max_concurrency=1) over one non-splitting chunk that sleeps 20s: with the twin cancelled the review runs the command ONCE (seen.txt==1); without it, twice (seen.txt==2).
test_a_chunk_lost_to_time_settles_at_the_bound_not_after_a_hedge_copy FAILS pre-fix (assert 2 == 1: seen.txt had 2 invocations) and PASSES post-fix (1 invocation).
```

## Why does a held lease lapse during long detached review rounds?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-lease-ttl-expires-during-review`

- **Claim.** A ddflow review --detach relaunches the review WITHOUT the resolved agent identity, so the detached process runs as a freshly derived id that holds no lease; the lease keeper finds the holder does not match and never renews, so the lease lapses over the TTL.
- **Mechanism.** review._detach relaunches the review via _relaunch_argv, which strips only --detach and does not re-declare the resolved --agent id, so the detached process re-derives its id; api/review/run.py wires on_tick=keep_lease but leasekeep.keeper returns None when the holder does not match log.agent_id, so no lease.renewed lands.
- **Falsifier.** The relaunched argv already carries --agent <resolved>, or the lease is renewed despite a different derived id.

**Probe:**

```console
$ assert _detach_argv(['--detach','T1','--delta'],'role') == ['--agent','role','T1','--delta'] on unfixed code
```

## Does ddflow review run from a claimed worktree attribute the review to the as_agent role passed, or the derived worktree identity?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-review-identity-from-worktree-ignores-as-agent`

- **Claim.** ddflow review --detach relaunches itself from raw argv (stripping only --detach), so a non-argv identity (as_agent/DDFLOW_AGENT/harness) is lost and the detached process records the derived worktree holder.
- **Mechanism.** review._detach rebuffs argv then reruns python -m ddflow <argv>; identity.resolve reads only --agent from argv and falls to the tree-derived default, so a non-argv identity never reaches the relaunched log.
- **Falsifier.** If the relaunched argv already re-declared the identity, by would name the role, not a derived id.

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run pytest tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py -q
3 passed; on unfixed code the relaunch argv holds no --agent, so test_detach_launches_with_the_resolved_identity fails.
```

## Can tiny, safe fixes be bundled or gate-lightened on a fast track, and what does the real log say about how many, how costly and how safe?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `P-batch-gates`

- **Claim.** Tiny fixes (src+other <=10 changed lines, <=6 files, no hot engine path) are ~11% of completed items (169 of 1510, 2026-09-28..11-03) but only ~5% of gate-hours (70 of 1415 h); skipping their reviews would miss a confirmed MEDIUM+ finding in ~12-20% of them, so the safe win is bundling the shared gates (ci/unit_tests/standards) plus ONE combined review per bundle, not review skipping; a text predictor is no better than base rate, so a post-hoc diff guard must decide.
- **Mechanism.** Per-item fixed gate cost (ci 475 s, unit_tests 560 s, rubber_duck 272 s, critic 195 s median for tiny) dominates a 10-line change; same-day tiny pairs overlap on paths in only 12 of 535 pairs, so path-disjoint bundles of 4-6 are common. Existing: doc_pipeline by actual diff (services/docsonly.py), [chore], [review].combined_under_lines, P-batch-gates (D-BG-Q4: reviewer never skipped), TA-fastlane (queue cap only).
- **Falsifier.** A replay of the 169 tiny-cold fixes through a bundler (N<=10, path-disjoint) that shows <20% gate wall-time saved, or >1 culprit-attributed red bundle in 10, or a post-hoc guard that demotes >40% of bundled items.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python over .ddflow/events (133458 events): item gates/triage/bug events joined to git diff --numstat landed_before..landed_after excluding .ddflow and docs/ddflow
fix tasks 631/1510; tiny-cold fixes 169; findings confirmed MEDIUM+ tiny 30/149 (src>0 only 7/37); gate-hours tiny 70/1415; median lead 37 vs 87 min; text predictor precision 0.17-0.24 vs base 0.15
```

**Sources:** https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue, https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/5.2.2/config/pipeline.html, https://docs.openstack.org/infra/zuul/gating.html, https://research.google/pubs/what-breaks-google/, https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git/+/dc7f5252145dbef0c1663176a90e86285d5e0e3b/docs/code_reviews.md, https://cmcrossroads.com/article/largest-case-study-code-reviews-ever

## Where does ddflow time go on the 132k-event, 116 MB, 834-shard log, how does it scale to 1M and 10M events, and which upgrade-safe, derived-data-only changes fix it?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Every read verb pays O(total log): parse+merge+fold = about 4.4 s cold at 132k (33 us/event; 15-30 s and 2.2 GB RSS at 1M synthetic), repeated 2-5 times per command, plus a restamp that fires whenever ANY agent appended. A State checkpoint plus tail fold, single load per command, no restamp on foreign appends, lazy numpy import and one-pass doctor remove about 85-95 percent without touching the log or adding a database.
- **Mechanism.** The log is append-only per agent shard and fold is pure and deterministic, so State at a verified shard-prefix mark plus the appended tail equals a full fold unless a merged clone brings an event sorting before the mark (detected, falls back to an older rung). Waste is elsewhere: keep_stamped compares the global log.mark so a busy log restamps after read verbs; _load_fresh runs 2-5 times; embed.py imports numpy at startup; doctor re-scans 1.3 GB of transcripts per consumed ask; the marshal read snapshot costs more than json parsing.
- **Falsifier.** Prototype State-pickle checkpoint plus tail fold: if show on the real log is not under 1.5 s idle with State byte-identical to a full fold, or if a second process appending in a loop does not stop read verbs from calling batch.apply after the restamp fix, the claim is false.
- **Budget.** about 90 min, read-only, no installs; orjson speedup not measured (THEORETICAL)

**Probe:**

```console
$ cProfile and wall timers per phase (scratch/phases.py), py-spy 150 s on doctor, python -X importtime, DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT=0/1 A/B, DDFLOW_WAVES_AUTO_STAMP=false A/B on show, logfixture.generate at 250k/500k/1M, State pickle dump/load, git/count scans of the event log; load average 13-66 on 192 cores, each timing repeated 2-3 times
version 0.99 s wall but user 8.2 s (user 0.86 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; numpy via ddflow.services.embed). Cold _load_fresh phases: read_all 3.4 s, fold 0.9 s, warm read_all 0.8 s. Command wall at 132k: next 6-11, show 6-18 (bimodal: restamp 4-16 s when another agent appended), board 9-18, recall 15.5, status 22.5 (622 git subprocesses 9.8 s), brief 40-43, doctor ~870 s (76 percent in harness.verify rescanning 1264 transcripts, 228 consumed asks). show with auto_stamp off: 22.8 s to 8.0 s under cProfile. Snapshot ON 3.6 s vs OFF 2.8 s cold at 132k; 27 vs 15 s at 1M. Synthetic cold load 32k 0.8 s, 66k 1.5-2.1 s, 132k 2.8 s, 250k 3.3 s, 500k 7-8 s (1.1 GB), 1M 15-30 s (2.2 GB). State pickle 85 MB (items 74 MB), load 0.47 s vs fold 0.9 s. index.db: 46 fingerprint files, 5.0 GB. In-process parse cache holds 100000 of 132555 events (max_cached_events ceiling already crossed). Event mix: lease.renewed 29.8 percent, gate.passed+failed 53 percent of bytes.
```

**Sources:** ddflow/infra/log/_read.py, ddflow/api/_base.py, ddflow/api/waves_auto.py, ddflow/infra/store/_fingerprint.py, ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py, docs/ddflow/research/snapshot-open-speed.md

## Where is ddflow differentiated, which scope is speculative, and what should it not build because vendors will ship it?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Differentiated and defensible: file-glob leases with conflict control (vendor agent teams doc still says avoid same-file edits by splitting ownership by hand), cross-family review independence plus unavailable-not-passed gate semantics, bug-needs-failing-regression-test, event-sourced replayable audit log, no-shell MCP operation. Redundant or at risk from vendors in 12 months: native worktrees, shared task lists with dependencies and TaskCompleted hooks (already in Claude Code agent teams, experimental), managed PR review (Claude Code Review, Mar 2026), scheduled automations (Codex app), agent control planes (GitHub Agent HQ). Speculative: product/test/architecture/change/constellation ops, lifecycle profiles, 24+ harness descriptors, ETA/optimizer; filed in the last 3 days with zero usage evidence. Minimal kernel: queue+DAG, leases+worktrees, gates, review independence, event log, approvals, MCP.
- **Mechanism.** Comparison of ddflow's queue and decisions with fetched vendor docs; judgement

## Does ddflow need a QA agent as a gate that verifies the changes produce trustworthy test evidence and are correct and resilient?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** PARTLY. ddflow already runs a real fail-before/pass-after check for bug fixes (verify_regression_test); the gaps are (a) 40 percent of bug fixes closed without a machine-run F2P, (b) no F2P/weakening/flake check for ordinary tasks, (c) hand-recorded gates (research, rules, implement, bug_hunt, dedupe) pass on a note, (d) reviewers see only the diff and are not prompted for test quality. A deterministic evidence gate (F2P of new tests on the pre-change tree, weakening detector, skip-is-not-pass, flake rerun, bounded mutation on risk globs) covers most of it; an LLM QA reviewer should be an advisory lens fed those results, never a separate blocking round. DESIGN PART IS THEORETICAL; the measurements are CONFIRMED.
- **Mechanism.** Reuse services/gates/mutation.verify_regression_test + regression_run.not_a_pass/not_a_failure on the item's own base with the new test files overlaid; AST diff of tests for weakening; flakes.py for rerun; mutation {file,old,new} registry format for bounded mutants; LLM only proposes mutants or triages anomalies, ddflow runs them.
- **Falsifier.** On the 25-bug F2P sample and 19-merge revert sample, the proposed checks classify fewer than 80 percent the way a manual run did, or the seeded bad-test set (QA-eval) is caught below 90 percent, or per-item cost exceeds 5 percent of current gate wall time.
- **Budget.** about 3 hours, read-only, scratch worktrees in a temp dir

**Probe:**

```console
$ event-log analysis (131306 events, 2026-09-28..2026-11-03, window 2026-10-04..): bug.fixed regression_verified counts; gate.failed rates; ci.result stages; git worktree checkout of landed_before with test files overlaid from landed_after, python -m pytest <node ids>; AST scan of 1126 merges / 8811 new test functions; revert of source files for 19 merges
```

- **Mechanism.** The heartbeat (the periodic call an agent already makes during long gates) re-scores the live lessons against the item with services.similar, records cadence.ran, and stops until the interval passes again; matched_lessons filters to [dedupe].show_floor.
- **Falsifier.** RC.due(st, item, cfg, at + recall_recheck_s) is False


## Does ddflow merge clear a stale MERGE_HEAD that blocks every merge?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B1b8d31b8c6`

- **Claim.** A concluded merge can leave MERGE_HEAD pointing at an ancestor of HEAD with nothing staged; ddflow merge then fails with 'You have not concluded your merge (MERGE_HEAD exists)' instead of clearing the stale state.
- **Mechanism.** _merge_here calls git merge with MERGE_HEAD still set; git refuses before merging; merging() reports True (MERGE_HEAD set) but nothing distinguishes a stale ancestor from a real in-progress merge.
- **Falsifier.** Detect MERGE_HEAD that is already an ancestor of HEAD with an empty index, clear it with git merge --quit, and the merge proceeds.

**Probe:**


## Does `decision add --extends ID` currently append the new decision text to ID and union the new globs onto it (no new record), instead of filing a new decision linked to ID?


## Can near-duplicate OPEN bugs filed under differently-worded titles describing one root cause be clustered by symptom + root cause, so a sweep finds them and linking settles them?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `dx-bug-dedupe-sweep`

- **Claim.** A two-signal matcher -- TF-IDF content-word overlap (services.similar) plus embedding cosine (services.embed) -- clusters two reports of one defect that share no whole sentence, while two genuinely distinct defects stay apart.
- **Mechanism.** Root-cause content words recur under word-variation (file, lease, deadlock, queue), which overlap captures; paraphrase that shares no word is caught by the embedder. A pair clusters when either signal reaches the floor.
- **Falsifier.** An overlap score below the floor between two known duplicates, or a distinct defect scoring above it, would cluster or part wrongly.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python: bugsim.cluster() over paraphrase fixtures in the worktree
groups: [['B1','B2']] (paraphrases merged); distinct cause B3 not grouped
```

## Which sections of a task's workflow path (gates and steps) could have been merged or overlapped, how many hours would that save, and how should the DAG optimizer and a running agent be told?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** MEASURED 2026-10-03..11-02 (1,322 claimed+completed items, 1,182 with gate processes): only 4 gates are real processes with elapsed_s (rubber_duck 406 h, critic 346 h, ci 322 h, unit_tests 174 h, combined reviews counted once); they are 27% of claim-to-merge time (992 h union of 3,702 h). Judgement gates (research, rules, implement, standards, bug_hunt, dedupe) fail <=0.7% and are recorded in bursts (implement 77%, dedupe 80%, rules 68% within 10 s of the previous record). Of 2,499 rubber_duck/critic round pairs 55% ran sequentially (upper bound 142 h if concurrent), 30% concurrent, 15% one combined request. Final-pass review || suite potential is 109 h (suite-lock aware) to 152 h (no lock) = 2-3% of cycle; 75% of items change tree after review so speculative ci||review is wasted in 3 of 4 items (51 h of ci/unit_tests passes were invalidated by a later tree change). Task merging, size-capped (combined <300/<400 lines), saves only 6-22 h / 14-54 h per 30 days (46/101 pairs). THEORETICAL: the WP-* design (gate stages, plan record, in-flight notice, optimizer group decisions) is not built or measured.
- **Mechanism.** Folded .ddflow/events (129,073 events): gate.started/gate.* outcomes with evidence.elapsed_s, tree_sha, review_id, combined_gates; worktree.merged landed_before..landed_after for git diff --numstat; paired rubber_duck/critic outcomes within 40 min; same-tree groups by evidence.tree_sha; union of [t-elapsed, t] intervals per item. Code read: services/gates/defs.py (pipeline is an ordered list, enforce_order warn, no gate dependencies), api/review/run.py (_review_each runs gates one after the other; combined_under_lines=150), api/gates/_run.py (_covered_by_ci), adapters/optimizer.py (Candidate/Verdict, no group concept), services/inbox.py (REASONS ready, merge_offer, yield, message).
- **Falsifier.** A recount on a different 30-day window or a second reading of gate.started->outcome pairs (instead of elapsed_s) that puts the remaining fork-join potential above 400 h or below 40 h; or a pilot of review||suite at the final tree that does not shorten claim-to-merge p50.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python folds in the session scratchpad (a1..a14.py); ddflow metrics stages --since 2026-10-03 as cross-check (claim_to_merge p50 4447 s vs 4740 s here)
items 1322; cycle p50 1.33 h p90 9.7 h; process union 992 h of 3702 h claim-to-merge; rd/critic pairs sequential 1378 concurrent 750 combined 371; same-tree groups 1649: sum 601 h union 491 h ideal 376 h; final-pass review||suite 389 h -> 280 h; superseded ci passes 235 (27.8 h) unit_tests 131 (23.4 h); task pairs combined<400 lines 101 pairs 13.6/53.8 h; Pegasus clustering Montage -53.3% makespan jobs 3461->104 (scitech.group/files/publications/chen2011overhead.pdf); Google median change 24 lines, review latency <4 h (sback.it/publications/icse2018seip.pdf)
```

**Sources:** https://scitech.group/files/publications/chen2011overhead.pdf, https://sback.it/publications/icse2018seip.pdf, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-jobs-in-a-workflow, https://smartbear.com/learn/code-review/best-practices-for-peer-code-review/

## Should 'every task add considers duplicates, merges, needs, phase and wave' be a rule (default for all projects) or a feature?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** A built-in compute-and-propose step inside task add ([tasks].add_check) plus a 4-line shipped rule that points at it beats a rule alone: the existing forced duplicate flag is answered --new 95% of the time (529 of 555 asks, 2026-10-03..11-02), duplicates that slipped through (68 dup-abandoned, 1.9%) mostly scored below the 0.55 ask threshold, DX tasks are 7x likelier to be dup-abandoned (6.6% vs 0.9%) than phased ones, and only 6 of 373 lease-wait pairs had a needs edge.
- **Mechanism.** check_add (ddflow/api/_dedupe.py) compares title+body only and asks at cosine>=0.55; add-time sees no globs, no needs, no phase, no wave; ddflow plan lint (services/planlint.py) sees them but only whole-queue and on request; waves auto-stamp landed 2026-10-29. Joining globs/needs/phase signals to the existing add transaction costs no extra call.
- **Falsifier.** After the feature ships, dup-abandon share of new tasks (excl. fix-) does not fall below 1% in 30 days, or lease.waiting pairs without a needs edge stay above 90%, or median add latency rises more than 2 s.
- **Budget.** read-only, about 1 h

**Probe:**

## Why is the constants ratchet red on main, and is it register drift or unregistered work?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-ci-main-constants-ratchet`

- **Claim.** The red is register drift: the package splits moved constants to new module paths (register keys went stale) and new constants landed unclassified; re-pinning the register keys at the current homes and classifying the new constants settles it.

## Which module pair trips test_no_mutually_importing_pair_has_a_module_level_edge on main, and what breaks its eager edge?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-ci-main-layering`

- **Claim.** The mutual pair is services.importer._tables <-> services.importer._titles: _tables imports 21 title primitives from _titles at module level, and _titles imports Found from _tables (TYPE_CHECKING only). The eager edge is the _tables -> _titles module-level import.
- **Mechanism.** The detector flags a mutual pair whenever EITHER edge is module level. _titles's Found import is a compile-time-only TYPE_CHECKING edge (mutual, lazy), so the module-level _tables->_titles import is the eager edge to break. Removing the reverse edge (move _add_prose_needs, the sole _titles consumer of Found, into _todo and delete the TYPE_CHECKING import) makes the pair non-mutual, so no eager edge remains flagged.
- **Falsifier.** Running the detector over the package still reports a mutual pair with a module-level edge after the move, or a relative import resolves to nothing.

**Probe:**

```console
$ walk every ddflow module, build (at_module, everywhere) import edges, and list mutual pairs with a module-level edge
BEFORE: services.importer._tables imports services.importer._titles at MODULE level, and services.importer._titles imports services.importer._tables. AFTER: NO MUTUAL PAIR WITH EAGER EDGE
```

## Which claims of R-lock-landscape survive primary-source and local-log verification, and what changes in the lock design?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** PARTIAL (verdict field only allows CONFIRMED/REFUTED/THEORETICAL; filed THEORETICAL because unverified items remain). VERIFIED (primary quote or measured): Brun TSE2013 16% textual/1% build/6% test conflicts over 5355 merges, 33% of clean merges later fail build/test, textual conflicts persist mean 3.2d (median 0.7d); Cursor: lock-based coordination made 20 agents run at 1-3 agents throughput, OCC simpler, integrator role dropped as bottleneck; Anthropic C-compiler: task lock = text file in git, merge conflicts frequent; Zuul/GitHub queue/GitLab train/bors semantics; Perforce p4 unlock -f admin only; SVN steal/break; git-lfs unlock --force and --lockable read-only; git merge-tree --write-tree exit 0/1/other (git 2.43.0 lacks --quiet: rc129; honors .gitattributes merge=union); merge-tree median 16ms on 27 ddflow branches (p90 1.3s only for branches 11k+ commits stale); Mergiraf supports Python + 30 others, Linux kernel only 428/7415 (5.8%) conflicts fully solved; AgenticFlict 27.67% of 107k agent PRs conflict. LOCAL (14d, 490 completed tasks): lease hold p50 2.3h p90 21.4h; claim->merge p50 106min p90 682min; 33.5% of lease-hours are AFTER merge; 84% of tasks still commit after first review starts so release-at-review is unsafe; 144 wait spans = 495h, p50 1.5h, p90 11h; of 108 classifiable spans 38 (145h, 32%) were between tasks whose ACTUAL changed files were disjoint; declared globs: 50% of declared files untouched, 45% of actual files outside declared globs, 54/100 tasks wrote undeclared files; pairwise conflict: 1 of 68 evaluable concurrent-overlap pairs conflicted, 0/60 sampled in-branch main-merges needed manual resolution, but 41 of 487 merges (8.4%) produced a red-main bug (mostly lint/secrets/ratchet, split unmeasured). STILL UNVERIFIED: Uber SubmitQueue 2019 paper itself (only secondary summary + 2025 Uber arXiv 2501.03440 numbers); Accioly 2018 and Ghiotto per-merge conflict rate beyond the quoted 10-20% (PDF not fetched); relation of conflict probability to branch lifetime/developer count (no source found); Perforce +l and p4 opened -a text; Crystal/Palantir effect sizes; Meta PTS full-paper test share; Google TAP skip fraction; pytest-testmon miss rate; Sapling/Graphite/ghstack; OpenAI Codex/Devin/OpenHands conflict handling; hunk-level overlap (e) not computed, only textual merge-tree conflict on non-synced branches.
- **Mechanism.** Locks block throughput (Cursor; own log: 32% of wait-hours are false serialization); textual conflicts are rare in this repo (<3%) so optimistic merge with a merge-tree probe at claim/review/merge is cheap (16ms) and the arbiter; leases should shrink to a scheduling hint on declared-and-observed files and release at merge, not at review start.
- **Falsifier.** If after switching to observed-file leases released at merge, red-main bugs or textual merge-tree conflicts exceed ~5% of merges, or rebase churn exceeds waiting saved, revert.
- **Budget.** one session, web+local read-only

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 -I log analysis of .ddflow/events (51k events, 2026-10-19..11-02) + git merge-tree timing on 27 branches/60 merges/10+10 pairs, git 2.43.0
hold p50 8217s p90 76918s; wait spans 144 total 495h; disjoint-actual waits 38 spans 145h; merge-tree median 0.016s p90 1.29s; 1/68 pair conflicts; 0/60 in-branch merges manual; 84% tasks commit after first review
```

## How can agents hand changes and information to each other (suggest a patch to a file's owner, get accept/reject, sync on main/peer progress) on ddflow's event log, git, and harness doors, so long file locks can be broken safely?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Git already provides every transport needed (shared object store makes a contributor commit visible by branch name at once; cherry-pick -x, am -3, bundle, a hidden refs/ddflow/suggest/<item>/<id> namespace, patch-id/range-diff, merge-tree --write-tree as a ~8 ms applicability probe, rerere); ddflow already has the carrier (per-agent local inbox with wake reasons delivered at wait/watch/heartbeat, the ask/approvals engine pattern, drift/sync, merge queue). Missing: a suggestion record + lifecycle, a cheap inbox door at PostToolUse/plugin hooks, drift.relevant/peer notices (DX-merge-fanout-notify, DX-drift-notice open), and an amendment to D-context-sync (an agent may tell only its master). A staged rollout of about 10 task-sized items is possible.
- **Mechanism.** Event log is the blackboard (swarm-orchestration.md); a suggestion is a record pointing at a git ref, delivery is a pointer message in the existing inbox; the owner applies by cherry-pick -x (authorship kept, owner's gates cover the tree-keyed result); applied/duplicate state detected by patch-id; staleness by merge-base drift; expiry files an ordinary task via a trigger-style action.
- **Falsifier.** If more than a few percent of probe-clean suggestions give a red ci on the owner's merge result (semantic conflicts are proven possible in the experiment), or owners do not answer within the TTL for most suggestions, or a suggestion costs the owner more tokens than a lease wait, the protocol is not worth building beyond notify-only.
- **Budget.** one session, throwaway git repos, read-only on the ddflow repo

**Probe:**

```console
$ git 2.43.0 throwaway repos in the session scratchpad (e1..e10): cherry-pick -x clean/conflict/idempotent, rerere across worktrees, merge --no-ff, format-patch|am -3 in an independent clone, update-ref refs/ddflow namespace + push/fetch refspec, bundle, notes/trailers, patch-id/range-diff/git cherry, merge-tree --write-tree (clean, conflict, timing 5000 files), sync strategies, post-merge rebase (ff, squash, tweaked), semantic clean-merge failure, commit-tree plumbing re-cut, dirty-tree apply; ddflow code read on main 44cc12426: services/inbox.py, api/lifecycle/wait.py+heartbeat.py, api/knowledge/sessions.py, services/lanerelease.py, leasebreak.py, drift.py, ask/engine.py, triggers.py
merge-tree 6-9 ms clean and conflicting on 5000 files vs 0.92 s scratch-worktree trial merge. am -3 across clones: 'No changes -- Patch already applied', patch-id equal in both repos; fresh empty repo: 'sha1 information is lacking'. git cherry: '-' when applied unchanged, '+' when owner tweaked or squashed; contributor rebase onto main after owner merge: ff -> skipped previously applied; squash -> dropping, patch contents already upstream; tweaked -> conflict. merge-tree CLEAN yet NameError after merge (rename vs new call). Plain clone fetches 0 refs/ddflow; branch -a hides them; git merge S1 'not something we can merge'. Notes do not follow cherry-pick. Stays THEORETICAL: protocol design, token cost, owner response rates, per-harness door behaviour (taken from agent-token-features.md, not re-probed).
```

## How can ddflow avoid long blocking file/glob leases while keeping risk low?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Hold edit leases only while editing (lazy per-file at first write, released at merge-ready); run expensive gates on snapshots via a speculative merge queue with a conflict probe; leases are a scheduling hint, merge-tree is the arbiter.
- **Mechanism.** Merge queues (GitHub, GitLab trains, Zuul) test change on top of predicted main so gates need no edit exclusivity; git merge-tree --write-tree probes conflicts without touching trees; shorter lock hold time cuts waiting by Little's law; conflicts concentrate in overlapping hot files.
- **Falsifier.** If in ddflow's own event history, tasks whose lease was released at merge-ready still produced semantic or textual conflicts at a rate over a few percent of merges, or rebase churn cost exceeds waiting cost, the design is wrong.
- **Budget.** one session, web only

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebFetch of 8 primary docs 2026-11-02
merge queue/zuul/gitlab/merge-tree/jj/PTS/Crystal/agent-teams verified; Uber SubmitQueue, Perforce, Accioly rates, Palantir not fetched (K)
```

**Sources:** https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue, https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html, https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/pipelines/merge_trains/, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-tree, http://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/conflicts/, https://mergiraf.org/, https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05286, https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~mernst/pubs/vc-conflicts-tse2013-abstract.html, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams

## Does a Popen subclass reaping via os.wait4 give each shell line its own rusage at negligible overhead?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `PM-resource-capture`

- **Claim.** Overriding Popen._try_wait to call os.wait4 yields the child's own cpu, maxrss and block io; a 150 MB allocating child is reported >=140 MB and a following trivial child reports its own small numbers.
- **Mechanism.** wait4 returns the rusage of exactly the reaped pid (and its waited descendants); RUSAGE_CHILDREN is a cumulative process-wide total with maxrss a high-water mark, so only wait4 is per-command.
- **Falsifier.** A trivial command after the heavy one reporting the heavy one's maxrss, or metered reap costing more than 5 ms over a plain Popen.

## What does ddflow already measure or plan about performance, and what is missing for a metrics-collection and periodic-analysis phase?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Wall-time metrics for gates, ci, review, queue wait, cycle time and rework exist and are log-derived (ddflow metrics); per-process CPU/rss/io/network, per-test time, tool-call counts, token cost per task and flaky rate are not measured anywhere; phase id P-perf already exists (log read path, hook latency, import time).
- **Mechanism.** Gate/ci/review events carry evidence.elapsed_s and waited_s (services/gates/runner.py, ci.py, infra/proc.py run_shell monotonic); services/metrics/* folds them; flowsignals and infra/signals.py sample load, memory, disk to .ddflow/local/flow/samples.jsonl via ticks.py. No getrusage/psutil anywhere in ddflow/ or tests/ (grep). Cadence passes are a fixed table COUNT_PASSES in services/schedule.py plus [cadence] knobs and prompts in templates/prompts/commands; P-observe.telemetry/.detectors/.experiments, B-perf-bench, B-gap-spend, ETA-data, SCH-review-inbox already plan much of the rest.
- **Falsifier.** A grep finding resource.getrusage, psutil or per-test duration capture in ddflow/, or an event kind recording cpu/rss/io, would refute the gap claim; ddflow metrics showing per-test times would too.

## External landscape for ddflow performance telemetry + self-optimizing workflow loop

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Stdlib-only collection (event timestamps, getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN), cgroup v2 files, pytest --durations/junit) covers most value; OTel GenAI names + Claude Code OTel names are the vocabulary; robust-stat alerts with min-sample guards avoid noise; test impact selection (testmon, Meta PTS) is the main lever against suite growth.
- **Mechanism.** Surveyed raw docs: Claude Code OTel (metrics claude_code.token.usage/cost.usage/active_time.total/lines_of_code.count; events api_request, tool_result duration_ms; prompt text opt-in only; metrics 60s export); OTel GenAI semconv moved to open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai (old page unmaintained); Python resource docs: RUSAGE_CHILDREN counts only waited-for children, ru_maxrss KB Linux / bytes macOS; cgroup v2 cpu.stat usage_usec, memory.peak resettable, io.stat rbytes/wbytes, pids.peak, needs delegation; Meta predictive test selection: >95% failures and >99.9% faulty changes caught at 2x lower infra cost; testmon uses coverage deps, not VCS; DORA now 5 metrics (change lead time, deploy freq, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate, deployment rework rate; updated 2026-01-05); GitHub Actions has usage metrics per workflow/job/runner. Not read in depth (training knowledge only, unverified): Langfuse/LangSmith/Helicone/Phoenix, Perfherder (URL 404), Bazel BEP, CodeScene, asv, SWE-bench cost metrics.
- **Falsifier.** A 4-week local pilot showing getrusage+event-timing attribution misses >30% of gate wall time or CPU, or alerts firing >1 false positive per week at min-sample 8.
- **Budget.** read-only, ~12 fetches

**Sources:** https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage, https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai, https://docs.python.org/3/library/resource.html, https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html, https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05286, https://testmon.org/, https://dora.dev/guides/dora-metrics/, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/metrics

## Why does a SIGTERMed checkout review leave its command reviewer running?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-push-review-terminated`

- **Claim.** The @_ends_on_signal signal guard was dropped from ddflow.api.review.review when ddflow/api/review.py was split into a package (commit 24a3e4434), so SIGTERM is no longer turned into RunTerminated and the detached reviewer child is never cancelled.
- **Mechanism.** _ends_on_signal installs RUN.terminating() (SIGTERM -> RunTerminated). Removing it means the default SIGTERM handler kills the review before _cancel_on_error cancels the hedged tokens, whose _abort kill_group()s the reviewer process.
- **Falsifier.** If review() were still decorated, test_review_terminated.py would not fail with 'the reviewer pid outlived the terminated review', and hasattr(ddflow.api.review.review, '__wrapped__') would be True.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow/api/review/run.py -- grep shows def review( has no @_ends_on_signal decorator; git show 24a3e4434 -- ddflow/api/review/run.py shows the decorator absent on the moved function
git log -S '@_ends_on_signal' -> 4c2ceb6f6 added it as a decorator; 24a3e4434 split the package and the @_ends_on_signal line is gone from run.py (def review( follows the import directly). Bug B-push-review-terminated repro: tests/test_review_terminated.py two cases fail in the pre-push run.
```

## Does capture_prompt drop a legitimately-second prompt as duplicate when an earlier slow hook wrote after a later hook's fired_at?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B7b632b294c`

- **Claim.** Yes: _recorded_recently only rejects events OLDER than the window (age>window), so a record in the future (negative age) is not skipped and counts as recent
- **Mechanism.** capture_prompt passes now=fired_at, which can precede an earlier hook's record ts; _age_s(record,now)=now-record_ts is negative, and negative>window is False, so the future record is treated as recent and the second prompt is dropped


## Does classify_exit read a signal-killed command as a failure, leaving a cut-off ci run stuck as 'queued ... elapsed'?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B8664a1e0c6`

- **Claim.** classify_exit maps a process killed by a signal (python exit -N, or the shell's 128+N) to FAILED, so a ci run that queued for the suite lock and was then killed records evidence waited_s/elapsed_s and gate status reports 'queued 11m of 15m elapsed' forever.
- **Mechanism.** classify_exit's order is: declared unavailable_exits, declared partial_exits, then code!=0 -> FAILED. SIGKILL is -9/137 and is in neither declared set, so it is FAILED; _queued_notes then derives the queued note from waited_s>0 because the outcome is not unavailable/partial.
- **Falsifier.** classify_exit(gate, -9, '') returns 'failed', not 'unavailable'.

**Probe:**

```console
$ classify_exit(ci-gate, -9, '')
before fix: ('failed',''); classify_exit returned FAILED for -9/137/143.
```
