## Why does star-import of a lazily re-exported package drop its lazy names, and does installing __all__ fix it?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-upgrade-apply-star-import`

- **Claim.** A package that re-exports names via ddflow/core/_reexport.py lazy __getattr__/__dir__ is invisible to star-import, because star-import reads the module __dict__ (or __all__ when defined), never __dir__.
- **Mechanism.** With no __all__, `import *` copies exactly the public names present in the module dict; lazy names resolve only on attribute access and are silently omitted. Setting __all__ to the public surface makes star-import resolve them through __getattr__.
- **Falsifier.** If the star-import had already bound apply and Watch before the fix, the claim is false.

**Probe:**

```console
$ PYTHONPATH=. python -c "ns={}; exec(stmt,ns); print(...)" where stmt is the star import
```


## Which guard ratchets did the infra.worktree / api.setup / services splits break, and does routing through infra.fsio plus re-keying agent-literal sites restore them without raising baselines?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `dx-split-guard-fsio-literals`

- **Claim.** The archdeps shutil family ratchet grew by exactly ddflow.infra.worktree._local/_locate/_merge (26 baseline -> 29 importers) after the infra.worktree split, and test_no_agent_literals failed only on the split-submodule moved sites plus one grok vendor<->descriptor overlap.
- **Mechanism.** archdeps shutil has no declared home, so every importer is a violation; the 3 new worktree submodules import shutil directly. test_no_agent_literals re-keys BASELINE by file path, so a moved site lands in a new file (baseline 0) and the old path goes stale.
- **Falsifier.** routing copy2/rmtree through infra.fsio makes archdeps shutil violations equal 26 again, and re-keying the moved BASELINE entries makes both test assertions pass, with shutil importers outside the declared home still 26 (not raised).

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow archdeps --json (shutil importer list) before/after; invoke tests.test_no_agent_literals test functions; assert shutil violations == BASELINE 26.
before: shutil 29 importers (grew _local,_locate,_merge); after: shutil home=infra.fsio, 27 importers, 26 violations == baseline. test_no_new_agent_literal OK, test_the_baseline_only_shrinks OK.
```

## Does each listed split submodule carry an import statement inside a function body (a deferred import) that test_ratchet[deferred_imports] flags against a baseline-0 file, and does rerouting each to a call-time sys.modules[__package__]/importlib accessor drive the per-module count to 0 without raising any baseline?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `dx-deferred-imports-reroute`

- **Claim.** Yes: the split moved defensive late-bound sibling reads into functions as // inside function bodies; none of the new submodules has a deferred_imports baseline file, so the ratchet is non-zero over a 0 baseline. Rerouting each to a call-time accessor removes the import STATEMENT (the guard counts AST Import/ImportFrom nodes at depth>0), leaving count 0 = baseline 0.
- **Mechanism.** tests/test_architecture_guards.py _Sites counts an ast.Import/ImportFrom node when visited at function depth>0 ('deferred_imports'). An assignment like  is an Attribute load, not an Import node, so it is not counted; semantics are unchanged because the package __init__ re-exports x lazily (__getattr__/reexport) and sys.modules lookup is equivalent to .
- **Falsifier.** The AST census of the 10 in-scope modules still reports >=1 Import/ImportFrom node at depth>0 after the change (i.e. the per-module deferred_imports count is non-zero), or the guard path no longer resolves the same names at call time.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python AST visitor over the 10 modules counting Import/ImportFrom at function depth, plus a venv import shim resolving each rerouted name
before: 18 sites (config/_compat 1, _tree 1, flow/_cut 4, importer/_plan 1, _scan 1, upgrade_apply/_apply 6, upgrade_dryrun/_read 1, cleanup dispose/plan/actions 4). after: 0 deferred_imports sites. import shim: ddflow.config, cleanup.dispose_tree/Path/proved_leftover_tip, importer _dedupe_found/_claims_done, upgrade_apply _save/make_snapshot/make_backup/_run_repairs/_run, importlib version_files/changelog_cut, source_root() all resolve.
```

## why can ddflow complete an item with unmerged commits

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Bd59dded6a4`

- **Claim.** ddflow complete lands/reports done on a released item whose branch still has commits its base lacks, dropping them without notice
- **Mechanism.** complete reads the fold's merged_sha (empty when merge never ran) and judges gates; the merge gate 'not run' is overridable by --force/approval, so an unmerged branch does not forbid completion
- **Falsifier.** force-completing a task whose branch has commits main lacks succeeds (exit 0) instead of refusing

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow task add/claim/commit then complete --force with merge gate omitted
exit 0 before the fix; the guard added in this change makes it exit 3 'branch ... not merged'
```

## Can the task selector and orderer prefer tasks that share files, overlap in globs or read alike (and affinity tags) in the same lane, keep averse tasks parallel, and sit behind one swappable optimizer adapter?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes, with no model call. TODAY (code audit, verified by reading): order is [bugs_first, priority, id] built in ddflow/core/schedule/_plan.py and _filters.py; phase, wave, critical path, tags and similarity do not enter it; overlapping globs are only HARD-blocked (one of two overlapping items is never offered together, glob_conflict in core/admission.py), never grouped; a register_key/register_filter seam exists for per-item keys but the greedy slot cut (_cut_ready) is hard-wired; several callers bypass plan_for and call core.schedule.plan directly; the swarm scorer (services/swarm/score.py: refusals, evaluate, rank, choose, pull with weights for critical, fit, cost, rework, queue) is built and tested but production calls only refusals and est_cost, and keeps its own copy of the overlap check; services/similar.py already offers TF-IDF similarity behind a Matcher protocol but nothing feeds it into ordering; Item.critical is never filled. PRIOR ART (UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory, no source opened): deterministic list scheduling with critical-path priority (HLFET/HEFT) plus a weighted soft-constraint score is the right shape; Kubernetes preferred affinity with weights 1-100 is the model for tag syntax; risks are over-clustering lengthening the critical path, starvation, non-determinism.
- **Mechanism.** One OptimizerPort in ddflow/adapters (order, cut, explain) whose default adapter v1 is today's algorithm moved unchanged; a v2 adapter adds lane-aware scoring: cost = earliest finish minus capped affinity bonuses (glob/file overlap through an inverted file-to-task index, text similarity from the existing Matcher, co-change coupling from git history, declared affinity tags) plus aversion penalties, with a critical-path floor, an age bonus and a makespan guard that falls back to v1. Tags: affinity:<key>[@weight] and aversion:<key>[@weight] as plain strings, weight 1-100 default 50, preferred only.
- **Falsifier.** A replay of the real event log in which v2 does not reduce lease wait or merge conflicts against v1, or lengthens makespan beyond the guard, or two runs on the same input differ.

**Sources:** code: ddflow/core/schedule/_plan.py, _filters.py, core/admission.py, services/swarm/score.py, services/similar.py; prior art unverified (HEFT 2002, Kubernetes affinity docs, code-maat)

## Which checks and companions should ddflow propose by default for every project, per software stack, and how does it detect the stack and ask the user and an agent?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** A universal baseline (pre-commit hygiene hooks, gitleaks pinned equal in hook and CI, detect-private-key, large files) plus per-stack tools chosen from detected lockfiles, manifests and existing tool configs. Fast fixers at commit, type checks and audits at push or CI; one entry point (pre-commit or prek run --all-files) shared by hook and CI because --no-verify bypasses hooks. Proposals need evidence, a dry run and an individual accept or reject; rejections are remembered. Categories ddflow cannot know (domain tools, build-tool-specific analysis, compliance, monorepo scoping, newly released tools) go to an agent research task with a fixed return contract.
- **Mechanism.** Detection by git ls-files (never node_modules, .venv, vendor), lockfile first, then manifest, then existing tool config; per-subdirectory roots in a monorepo. Catalogue data: tool, stack, stage, speed class, install, overlap, maturity, false-positive risk, default class (on, offer, research), pinned version and check date. Agent hazards worth a check: unpinned actions and workflow permissions (actionlint, zizmor, pinact), secrets in agent transcripts and config, MCP config risk, hidden characters and instruction-like text in agent-readable files, committed agent permission settings, hallucinated package names.
- **Falsifier.** A detected stack for which the proposed set fails to run on a clean checkout, or a default-on tool whose false-positive rate on a fixture repo blocks a normal commit.

**Sources:** prek releases (v0.5.9 on 2026-10-30), ty releases (0.0.95), zizmor; the rest from background knowledge, to be re-checked by TK-catalog

## How does ddflow compare with the other AI coding, test, project-management, research and documentation workflow tools (Claude Code, Codex, Kilo/Roo/Cline, Cursor, Copilot + Spec Kit, Aider, OpenHands/Devin/Amp, Taskmaster/Backlog.md/OpenSpec/BMAD, worktree managers, review bots, Renovate/Dependabot, Sonar/Semgrep/CodeQL), and which gaps are worth closing?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** ddflow is alone in combining file-glob leases, mandatory cross-family review, bug-to-regression-test enforcement and an append-only replayable event log. Gaps seen in several other tools: durable scheduled and event-triggered runs (Claude Code Routines, Codex Automations, Devin, Actions), PR-native integration (check runs, review bot), native AGENTS.md/SKILL.md read and write, a spec stage before tasks (Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Taskmaster), per-role tool and model modes (Kilo, Roo), SARIF and dependency-bot feeds, learning from review feedback, packaged installable setups (plugins, recipes). Most scheduling and pass work is already queued in P-schedule and P-continuous-improvement but nothing runs yet.
- **Mechanism.** Survey of public docs and vendor pages by a read-only researcher, then a check of the ddflow queue for what is planned. CAVEAT: the survey made only two web searches; most cells come from model knowledge (cutoff June 2026), so every non-obvious cell is unverified until GC-verify-matrix re-checks it with a source URL and date.
- **Falsifier.** A cell in the matrix that a vendor's own documentation contradicts, or a gap that the queue already covers under another id.

**Sources:** docs.claude.com; developers.openai.com/codex; kilo.ai; github.com/github/spec-kit; github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec; makerkit.dev routines guide; aicodereview.cc codex

## Why does ddflow review --delta raise ValueError 'outcome failed must carry a --reason' on a findings round?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B0419c114ef`

- **Claim.** The gate-failed reason is derived from the single 'best' reviewer only, so a blocking finding raised by a different reviewer leaves the reason empty and record() raises.
- **Mechanism.** _gate_outcome blocks on found aggregated across every REVIEWED reviewer, but _record_review builds the reason from _reason_of(best); best=min(status) picks the first fully-reviewed reviewer, which may have no findings while another reviewer raised one.
- **Falsifier.** A single reviewer raising a finding would crash the same way (it does not: _reason_of(best) then returns 'N finding(s)').

**Probe:**

```console
$ Repro with two command reviewers (clean + finder): first round clean (pass), a fix commit adds a FINDME line the 'finder' reviewer flags; the delta re-review records best=clean with no findings but blocks on finder's finding.
ValueError outcome 'failed' must carry a --reason (ddflow/services/gates/hand_approve.py:91-92)
```

## split config.py into a <30k package?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** ddflow/config.py (985 lines, 47.6k chars) can become ddflow/config/ with each submodule <30k chars and the full public API re-exported from __init__, with unchanged call sites and no behavior change.

## How do we make every external dependency (third-party packages and OS-level stdlib families such as http, sqlite, toml, shell, filesystem, clock) reachable only through our own adapters, with one implementation per function?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Mostly already in place as ratchets, with named gaps. The layer model and four 'home' contracts exist (import-linter); third-party use is small and near single-home. Missing: home contracts for http, sqlite, toml reading, shutil, templates and the clock/env; Protocol ports with fakes; one reconciled layer contract; a clone ratchet so one function has one implementation.
- **Mechanism.** A dependency census report (module, importing files, home, violations) drives one home contract per family, each with a port (Protocol), a default implementation in the home and a fake for tests; the baseline ignore lists only shrink (strangler with ratchets, D-unify); a clone detector with a ratchet (SE-reuse-guard) plus an extraction pass per cluster enforces one implementation per function.
- **Falsifier.** If a family cannot be put behind a port without changing observable behaviour (for example sqlite query semantics leaking into callers), that family stays a documented home module without a port and the ratchet only forbids new importers.

**Probe:**

```console
$ AST census of ddflow/**/*.py and read of .importlinter, B-uni-* and B109, B-architecture-pass, B-arch-layer-contracts, SE-reuse-guard (2026-10-31)
Third-party imports: jinja2 in 3 files, rapidfuzz 1 (core/fuzzy.py), tomlkit 1 (infra/tomlcfg.py), radon 1 (services/complexity_budget.py), model2vec 1 (services/embed.py); the mcp SDK is not used (own JSON-RPC). Stdlib family importers: tomllib 30 files, shutil 27, sqlite3 5, urllib.request 5, http.client 4, socket 2, subprocess 1. Existing import-linter contracts: layers (surfaces > api > views > services > infra > config > core), surfaces-through-api, subprocess-home (infra.proc, infra.git), fsio-home (tempfile and fcntl), hashlib-home (core.digest), optional extras only in their one adapter module. Open: B109 storage seam (no Protocol for EventLog or tomlcfg), B-arch-layer-contracts (two disagreeing layer models, 9 core->config, 2 services->views, 9 surfaces->infra baseline entries), B-architecture-pass (periodic assessment, default hexagonal), SE-reuse-guard (clone detector with ratchet, nothing enforces one implementation per function today), P-change-surface.smaller-code (clone and dead-code report). Done: B-uni-cmd-migrate (commands on a registry), B-uni-proc.4-leftovers (one process layer), B-uni-guards, B-uni-decide, Registry[T] seams, drivers as data.
```

**Sources:** B-uni-guards, B-uni-decide, B109, B-architecture-pass, B-arch-layer-contracts, SE-reuse-guard, .importlinter

## Can one contract make every supported agent reach function parity, in both directions (ddflow as a tool inside the agent, ddflow orchestrating the agent as a lane), with drivers and adapters reused across agents?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes. The driver architecture already separates a common core from per-harness data (descriptor v2, named engines fieldmap/emit/mcp_shape/render_argv/stream_map/limit_detect/transcript_map, the Lane contract, three-valued facts, harness x model x route combination, the offline conformance suite with its gap ratchet). What is missing is one canonical feature catalog with two axes that every descriptor must answer row by row, and a gate that makes 'supported' mean 'every row answered' so a new agent, or a new ddflow function, produces its parity tasks automatically.
- **Mechanism.** A data catalog lists features on two axes. In-agent (ddflow as a tool): instruction file, MCP config, lean tool profile, session-start brief path, pre-tool enforcement hook, post-tool recording, stop/gate reminder, skills and commands, agent and session identity, approvals relay, session ingest, trust handling, version detection. Orchestrator (ddflow drives the agent): headless launch, state-dir isolation, key by env name, permission mode, budget limits, stream mapping, usage and cost, limit detection, stop on lease revocation, steer, resume, hook injection in lanes, conformance levels 1-7. Each descriptor answers every row: supported (verified or declared), documented absent, unverified, or not applicable with a reason. ddflow harness parity prints the matrix; a ratchet fails when a descriptor leaves a row unanswered or a new catalog row appears without an answer; adding a row files one parity task per supported agent and gap; the share of agent-specific Python versus data is measured and ratcheted so new agents are data-first.
- **Falsifier.** If a feature cannot be expressed as a catalog row with a testable offline check (it needs per-agent bespoke code to even state), the row stays unverified for that agent and the matrix says so; if the gap ratchet makes adding an agent so costly that operators bypass it, the answer states must allow 'unverified' to count as listed but not as supported.

**Probe:**

```console
$ read docs/ddflow/decisions/driver-architecture.md, docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md, docs/ddflow/lane-conformance.md and the P-drivers task list, 2026-10-31
Already done in P-drivers: DRV-engines (named reusable engines), DRV-lane-interface (LaunchSpec, observe, steer, cleanup), DRV-facts, DRV-combine, DRV-model-catalog, DRV-conformance (106 declared checks, 19 synthetic, 87 unverified gaps, 16 of 24 agents zero-Python by proxy, ratchet in tests/harness_conformance/gaps.json), DRV-cli (harness add, lint, test, probe). Open: DRV-migrate (remaining code switches to data), DRV-packs, DRV-plugin-sdk, DRV-docs, DX-harness-test-wire-conformance. Lane conformance levels 1-7 exist (launch, claim, heartbeat, gate_record, hook, lease_stop, tool_accuracy). No single catalog covers both directions and nothing files parity tasks when a feature or an agent is added.
```

**Sources:** R-mistral-vibe, driver-architecture.md, adding-a-harness.md, lane-conformance.md

## Is Mistral Vibe 2.0 (the Devstral-powered terminal coding agent) a good fit as a supported ddflow agent, and what does the integration need?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes. Vibe is Apache-2.0, terminal-native, and exposes almost everything ddflow needs from a harness: project and user hooks (pre_tool can deny or rewrite, post_tool, post_agent), MCP servers in config.toml, AGENTS.md instructions, Agent Skills (SKILL.md), subagents, a headless mode with streaming NDJSON, budget limits and documented exit codes, ACP via vibe-acp, and a full state-directory override (VIBE_HOME) that makes per-lane isolation easy. Gaps: no session-start or session-end hook, project hooks and config load only from trusted folders, no documented custom OpenAI-compatible provider, no documented session storage path.
- **Mechanism.** Descriptor and facts from the public README and the 2026-01-27 announcement; hook installer writes [REDACTED:path] (user) or <project>/.vibe/hooks.toml after the trust step; the session brief reaches the agent through an AGENTS.md managed region and MCP server instructions because there is no session-start hook; lease enforcement is a pre_tool hook returning decision=deny; lane driver runs vibe -p with --output streaming, --max-turns/--max-price/--time-limit and a lane VIBE_HOME, mapping exit codes 0-4 to the Lane contract; telemetry, update checks and notifications are switched off in the lane home; Devstral 2 pricing becomes model facts.
- **Falsifier.** If a live probe shows the hook payload lacks a stable session id or tool name, or hooks do not fire in --prompt mode, or pre_tool deny does not block the tool, lease enforcement needs the MCP path only; if streaming output has no usage or session id, lane accounting falls back to export.json; if project config is ignored without the trust step in headless runs, the lane home must pre-trust the worktree.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebFetch of github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe README and mistral.ai/news/mistral-vibe-2-0, 2026-10-31; no install, no live run
Documented: install via uv tool install mistral-vibe or the mistral.ai/vibe/install.sh script (GIL-enabled Python 3.12+); config.toml in ./.vibe then [REDACTED:path], VIBE_HOME moves everything, trusted_folders.toml gates project .vibe; [[mcp_servers]] (stdio, http, streamable-http, oauth/static auth, timeouts) and vibe mcp add; hooks.toml with exactly three events pre_tool, post_tool, post_agent, JSON on stdin, decision allow/deny, project entry wins by name, subagents inherit hooks, no session hooks; headless vibe -p/--prompt/--prompt-file, --output text|json|streaming, --max-turns, --max-price, --max-tokens, --time-limit, --output-dir, --resume, -c, --agent, --auto-approve/--yolo; exit codes 0 finished, 1 usage/config error, 2 infrastructure failure, 3 limit stops, 4 aborted; built-in agents ask, accept-edits (default), auto-approve, plus custom agents in agents/*.toml; subagents via the task tool (explore built in); skills per the Agent Skills spec in .agents/skills, .vibe/skills and [REDACTED:path]; AGENTS.md from [REDACTED:path] and project dirs up to the trust root; vibe-acp for editors; MISTRAL_API_KEY; telemetry off with enable_telemetry=false; license Apache-2.0; the project accepts no pull requests. ## Can ddflow predict when a task, a phase and an agent's current work will finish, and give a useful range when the operator asks?
```

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes, as a range and not a single date: per-item remaining time from the typical duration of the gates still to run plus expected review rounds and lease/glob contention, combined over the dependency DAG with lane capacity by simulation, with the critical-path chain named as the reason, scored continuously against what actually happened.
- **Mechanism.** The event log already holds the signals: lease.acquired, gate.started/passed/failed, item.completed, lease waits, review rounds and lamport-ordered timestamps. A derived read model folds cycle times and per-gate durations; an estimator turns the item state (gates done, rounds so far, glob count, class) into a quantile distribution shrunk toward the global one; a Monte Carlo over the needs graph with N lanes gives phase and queue P50/P80/P95 and the bottleneck chain; every prediction is recorded and later scored so the model recalibrates.
- **Falsifier.** If backtesting on the log shows the 10-90 percent interval covers well under 70 percent of actual completions, or the model does not beat the naive per-prefix median by a clear margin, or contention and operator waiting dominate so much that no stable distribution exists, ETAs must be shown only as order-of-magnitude bands or not at all.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python fold of .ddflow/events/*.jsonl: claim-to-complete cycle times, per-gate durations, and a naive per-prefix-median backtest (2026-10-31)
1406 items with a claim-to-complete time: p25 36 min, p50 70 min, p75 136 min, p90 356 min (heavy tail). Gate durations p50/p90 seconds: rubber_duck 408/1088, critic 424/1081, ci 444/916, unit_tests 618/1418. Naive backtest, median by id prefix with global fallback over 1376 items: only 51 percent land within 2x of the actual, median relative error 0.58. About 62 completions in the last 24 hours. Conclusion: point estimates from item class alone are poor; the tail is heavy; a state-aware, interval-valued model is needed and the data to build and score it exists.
```

**Sources:** events log, D-roadmap, DX-parallel-width-report, SW-digest, SW-lead-link, B-rm-changes

## Which protections must ddflow enforce by default, for every project, before a commit, a push and an approval, given the failures seen in this project (key leaked into the committed event log, force-complete bypass over MCP, red main, stale claim bases, duplicate identities)?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** The failures share three causes: protection that lives in a hook but not in the API layer, protection that depends on an external tool being installed, and checks that run at push time when the damage happens at write time. The defaults must be built in, enforced in the API layer, fail closed when a checker is unavailable, and run at write, commit and push.
- **Mechanism.** Write-time: redact secret shapes and exact secret values before any event or prompt is persisted. Commit-time: a built-in staged-content scanner (no external tool), size and conflict-marker and forbidden-file checks, local-layer isolation. Push-time: the existing scratch-worktree CI plus scanner; an unavailable scanner blocks, never passes. API-layer: every person-only act refuses an agent identity on every surface, proven by a surface-parity test. Baseline-aware unit_tests so a red main does not force every completion.
- **Falsifier.** If a built-in shape scanner has a false-positive rate that makes agents bypass it, or if an API-layer check cannot see the caller identity on some surface, the default has to be a warning plus the push-time block instead.

**Sources:** bug Bsecbug-redact-google-api-key, bug B49fa10bbb1, bug B3c1a2491a3, bug B6b7e47955e, R-security-gate-design, R-secrets-management

## Can ddflow resolve keys from local files and from trusted vaults (Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, pass, HashiCorp Vault, 1Password) on a remote host it cannot reach, without ever transporting or storing the value?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** A provider interface in the machine-local secrets table, resolved on the host where the consuming process runs using that host's own identity (az/aws/gcloud/pass/vault/op CLI already installed and logged in, managed identity or service principal), covers local and remote agents; ddflow stores only secret NAMES, provider kinds and references, never values.
- **Mechanism.** Each secret entry: name -> ordered list of sources (env, file, or provider {kind, ref}). Providers run a fixed argv with no shell (az keyvault secret show, aws secretsmanager get-secret-value, gcloud secrets versions access, pass show, vault kv get, op read) with a timeout; stdout is the value, captured in memory only, cached for a short TTL knob, never logged, never in argv of children, injected into a launched child's environment only. A remote lane resolves on the remote host, so ddflow never ships values and the remote's managed identity decides access. Failure or missing CLI is unavailable, never passed. Adding a command-style provider is a person-only act (T3, like command-kind reviewers). Events record name, provider kind, outcome and timing, never the value.
- **Falsifier.** If a vault CLI cannot return the value on stdout without writing it to disk or its own cache, or if its argv or env leaks the value to other processes, that provider needs a different carrier; if remote hosts have no CLI or identity, the entry must fall back to file/env and report unavailable.

**Sources:** R-secrets-management, ddflow/services/review_keys.py, D-no-own-services-local-dir

## Can ddflow manage API keys (gemini.key, kimi.key) so reviewers, lanes and launched tools get them without an agent or the shell handling the value?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** A named secrets table in .ddflow/local (name -> env var + key file PATH, never a value), resolved by the existing review_keys.resolve_key and injected into a launched child's environment only, removes manual export and gives redaction the exact values to match.
- **Mechanism.** review_keys.resolve_key(env, file) already reads env first then a mode-600 owner-only file via fstat, never printing the value; reviewers and lane endpoints already carry api_key_file. Gap: no table shared by other launched tools, no launch-time injection, no check command, brief does not say where a key comes from. Add a secrets table, make the lane launcher and review runner resolve by name, add ddflow secrets check, feed exact values to the redactor.
- **Falsifier.** If a launched tool cannot be given the key through its child environment alone (needs a config file with the value), or if exact-value redaction false-positives on short keys, the design needs a different carrier.

**Sources:** ddflow/services/review_keys.py, ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py, R121b9a81b3, bug Bsecbug-redact-google-api-key

## Why does the qwen reviewer hit its 64k-token reasoning cap on a ledger.py-sized chunk, and does review-dispatch chunking ignore the reviewer's declared output cap (max_tokens)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B9a2279db22`

- **Claim.** review size() splits a diff only on max_chunk_chars and ignores the reviewer's max_tokens (output cap), so a reviewer whose max_tokens < max_chunk_chars is sent a single chunk larger than it can reason about, which a reasoning model exhausts mid-thought (TRUNCATED -> UNAVAILABLE) and a review round is wasted
- **Mechanism.** a reasoning model spends its max_tokens OUTPUT budget thinking before answering, and the thinking grows with the input (measured 28 381 reasoning tokens for a 30 KB chunk, ~1 token/char); a chunk > max_tokens chars cannot be answered within the cap
- **Falsifier.** review(Reviewer(max_tokens=120, max_chunk_chars=30000), 12-file-diff) returns res.max_chunk_chars==30000 and chunks_total==1 (one over-cap chunk) on the unfixed code, vs res.max_chunk_chars==120 and chunks_total>1 on the fixed code

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run python -c 'review() with max_tokens=120 vs max_chunk_chars=30000 over a 12-file diff, monkeypatched _race returning STATUS: NO FINDINGS'
chunks_total=12 max_chunk_chars=120 status=0 (REVIEWED) -- the diff that used to go out as one 816-char chunk is now split to fit the 120-token output cap
```

## Does it make sense for ddflow to use the Agent Host Protocol (AHP) to integrate with VS Code and other tools that support it, and in which role?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Not as a core feature now. AHP (Microsoft, open, draft v1.1.0 over v1.0.0, JSON-RPC over message port locally and WebSocket remotely) is a coordination layer between several CLIENTS and an agent HOST: the host owns authoritative session state, sequences actions with a serverSeq, lets clients reconnect with lastSeenServerSeq and replay, arbitrates conflicts such as competing tool-call confirmations (first wins), and speaks ACP or another protocol to the agents behind it. It deliberately does not cover how agents reason, tools or models. ddflow's job is the queue, leases, gates and records over MCP, and its planned lane transport is ACP (R-acp, D-acp-r2, P-acp): AHP sits above that layer and solves multi-client viewing and persistence of one live agent session, which ddflow's deterministic lanes (D-swarm-answers) do not need. ddflow already integrates with VS Code with no AHP: the vscode harness descriptor (.vscode/mcp.json under the 'servers' key, .github/hooks/ddflow.json, copilot instructions), and VS Code's extensions can contribute tools, MCP servers and custom agents to the Agent Host. Three roles considered: (A) ddflow as an AHP CLIENT of a VS Code Agent Host (drive or observe Copilot, Claude and Codex sessions hosted by 'code agent host'): plausible later as one more lane backend, value moderate, blocked by an unconfirmed ability of a third-party client to create sessions and by the draft status; (B) ddflow as an AHP HOST exposing its lanes to VS Code's Agents window: attractive for operator visibility and approvals, but a large build (ACP-to-AHP event mapping, authoritative state beside the event log, auth) on a moving draft and with no documented support for third-party hosts in VS Code; (C) nothing now, keep MCP plus hooks for VS Code and add a read-only VS Code view only if wanted. Recommendation: C now, a small watch-and-probe task under P-acp for A, and revisit B when the spec is stable and VS Code documents third-party hosts.
- **Mechanism.** Sources read: VS Code docs agent-host concept page, the AHP doctrine and AHP-and-ACP pages, the AHP site index. Facts: standalone host 'code agent host' (localhost, connection token on by default, --tunnel to expose); adapters named for Copilot, Claude and Codex; third-party agent support not documented; client actions named in the pages: chat/turnStarted (send a turn), chat/toolCallConfirmed, chat/turnCancelled, sessions as URI channels with replay; session creation by a client is not described except that any client can start an automation run; SDKs in TypeScript, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, Go and .NET; the protocol says breaking changes may still be necessary while it is under active development. ddflow facts: ddflow/harnesses/vscode.toml (MCP path .vscode/mcp.json key servers, hooks style claude file .github/hooks/ddflow.json, injects session_start); P-acp has 21 open tasks (AC-spike wave 2 drives claude-agent-acp, codex-acp and opencode acp headlessly, AC-events maps session/update to ddflow events, AC-backend plugs the lane backend interface); lane decisions are D-swarm-answers (deterministic scheduler, pull lanes); operator approvals today go through the chat route.
- **Falsifier.** If a third-party client can create sessions on 'code agent host', attach to a running Copilot, Claude or Codex session and receive its events, and if VS Code's Agents window accepts a foreign host, role A becomes a cheap lane backend for hosted agents and role B an inexpensive visibility feature, and the recommendation changes to schedule them. If AHP reaches a stable 1.x with third-party hosts documented, revisit B.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebSearch AHP; WebFetch of the VS Code agent-host page, microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol guide pages doctrine and ahp-and-acp, and the site index; sed ddflow/harnesses/vscode.toml; ddflow recall ACP; ddflow search 'Agent Host Protocol' (no prior record). NOT probed: a running 'code agent host' or any AHP client.
```

**Sources:** https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/concepts/agent-host.md; https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/guide/doctrine.html; https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/guide/ahp-and-acp.html; https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol; R-acp; D-acp-r2

## Can descriptor-supplied regexes be made ReDoS-safe in Python re without a timeout?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DRV-engines`

- **Claim.** Auditing the parsed pattern (no repeat of repeat/branch, no backrefs) plus a head-length cap bounds match time
- **Mechanism.** Exponential backtracking needs nested ambiguous repeats; the sre parse tree exposes them before compile
- **Falsifier.** A refused-class pattern that is fast, or an accepted pattern slow on a 10MB input

**Probe:**

```console
$ raw re (a+)+$ on 26 chars vs safety.safe_regex
raw (a+)+$ on 26 chars: 7.27 s; engine: unsafe pattern '(a+)+$': a repeat of a repeat or branch can backtrack exponentially; tests: 10MB input searched <1s
```

## Can the planned security phase run Claude-Mythos-style code audits (an LLM agent hunting security flaws in source, with hypotheses, execution and proof-of-concept) so security issues are prevented in advance, and what must be added to P-security-gate?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Not as planned. P-security-gate (SEC-gatedef, SEC-scanners, SEC-deps, SEC-policy, SEC-findings, SEC-cadence, SEC-e2e) covers known-pattern scanners (bandit or semgrep, gitleaks, pip-audit), dependency advisories, a policy checklist with a cross-family review lens, and filing findings as bugs. None of it is an agentic vulnerability hunt, so it would catch known classes but not the logic and design flaws a Mythos-style audit finds. The method can be reproduced with whatever strong models are available, because the method is the agent loop, not one model: threat-model the code, partition it into audit units, let the agent read, hypothesise (source, sink, preconditions, CWE class), run the code in an isolated sandbox with a reproducer, and report only what reproduces, with exploitation steps, a failing test and a suggested fix. ddflow already has the pieces to host this (review machinery with FINDING lines and triage, a sensitivity vocabulary done as SE-sensitivity, a per-item scratch worktree, the declared surface registry as an entry-point inventory, a cross-family reviewer rule, regression-test-or-not-closed bug rule). Added tasks: SEC-hunt-decide, SEC-threatmodel, SEC-sandbox, SEC-embargo, SEC-hunt-engine, SEC-verify-triage, SEC-variant, SEC-fix-assist, SEC-prevent, SEC-hunt-eval; SEC-cadence and SEC-e2e now depend on them.
- **Mechanism.** Secondary press coverage of Claude Mythos Preview (not Anthropic's primary write-up, which I did not retrieve; the model itself is not publicly available): the workflow launches an isolated container with the target codebase, the model reads source, forms hypotheses, runs the software, uses debuggers, and writes a bug report with a proof-of-concept; reports include exploitation steps, a reproducer and a suggested fix; its strength is keeping context across long sessions and trying several approaches. Reported results: the Symfony team reviewed 19 reports and found all real; of 1,900 candidates sent for review 1,726 (90.8%) held up, but 21,119 of 23,019 candidates were unreviewed; model-assigned severity was wrong in 14 of 27 checked (13 overstated). Lessons for the design: reproduction is the false-positive filter; severity must come from a rubric or a human, not from the model; candidate volume outruns human triage, so budgets and dedupe are first-class; unfixed vulnerabilities are secrets, and ddflow's event log is committed, so a finding must not land in clear text in a committed log, export, brief or changelog before the fix (SE-sensitivity's restricted or confidential classes; R-Re6e4a3668e already found private text in bug summaries). Timing conflict: D-security-gate-scope (operator, 2026-10-29) put the gate at PHASE level only, but 'prevent in advance' also needs diff-scoped checks on risky changes and design-time checks at claim; SEC-prevent makes these opt-in and SEC-hunt-decide asks the operator. Cost and model: deep audits need the strongest available model, long sessions (governor and context meters), a model family different from the code's author (cross-family rule) and a sensitivity check before code leaves the machine.
- **Falsifier.** If the models available here cannot reproduce even the seeded fixtures (SEC-hunt-eval: injection, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, authorization bypass, race) at a useful precision and recall and at an affordable cost, the engine ships as a prompt-assisted review (advisory, static-only findings marked unverified) rather than an autonomous hunt, and the gate stays on scanners and the policy checklist. If no sandbox exists on the machine, hunts run static-only and every finding is labelled unverified, never verified.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebSearch Claude Mythos (secondary sources: Symfony blog, Endor Labs, Help Net Security); ddflow show SE-sensitivity; ddflow recall vulnerability disclosure embargo; list of P-security-gate tasks and the EXT-oh-sandbox task; D-security-gate-scope. NOT probed: running any model as an auditor.
```

**Sources:** https://symfony.com/blog/claude-mythos-audited-symfony-and-found-19-vulnerabilities; https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/?p=383552; https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/what-is-mythos-and-why-it-matters-for-software-security; P-security-gate; D-security-gate-scope; SE-sensitivity

## Does the queue already plan for a lead agent (e.g. Claude Code) managing the main task and communication while the lanes run other coding agents (e.g. opencode) on other models (DeepSeek, local endpoints), is it set up properly (phase, tasks, dependencies, waves, ACP), and what is missing?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Mostly planned and decided, with five gaps on the path to a real heterogeneous pilot. P-swarm (18 open tasks, waves 0-13) is the home; D-swarm-answers (operator, 2026-10-24) already decides: deterministic scheduler with pull lanes (an LLM orchestrator only for read-only research items), the scheduler MAY launch lanes from approved templates, pilot families Claude plus opencode or kilo with DeepSeek plus Qwen or Kimi, quality ledger per family and model, capped hedging, one remote lane at the end, lane-private hooks. ACP (P-acp, 21 open, AC-client wave 3, AC-backend wave 23) is NOT on the critical path: SW-pilot-local needs 16 open prerequisites, deepest wave 5, mostly P-swarm (7), P-drivers (5), P-agent-parity (2), through the process-headless Lane driver in DRV-lane-interface; ACP plugs in later as a transport. Roots that can start now: SW-git-fallback, SW-baseline, DRV-inventory, P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2, DX-fleet-registry, CC-inventory. Gaps: (1) nothing provisions a local or OpenAI-compatible model endpoint for an opencode/kilo lane (base URL, model id, key by env name, context window, tool-call support, lane-private provider block); (2) no capacity model for local endpoints or GPUs so the scheduler could oversubscribe them; (3) no task that actually launches lanes from approved templates although Q2 allows it (SW-pull only answers an idle lane); (4) no concrete opencode lane driver on top of the generic Lane contract; (5) the lead-to-lane channel (status, steer, ask, wake) only arrives late (P-spawn.steer wave 22, AC-steer wave 24), so a lead Claude Code session cannot talk to lanes in the pilot. SW-decide is still open although D-swarm-answers recorded its answers.
- **Mechanism.** ddflow show P-swarm, P-drivers, P-acp; ddflow decision show D-swarm-answers; task graph from ddflow list (needs, wave tags, phase): P-swarm tasks SW-baseline, SW-decide, SW-git-fallback (w0), SW-ledger (w1), SW-conformance (w3, needs DRV-lane-interface), SW-lane-hooks, SW-score (needs DRV-model-catalog), SW-seed-pack (w4), SW-headroom, SW-pull, SW-remote-bundle (w5), SW-digest, SW-hedge, SW-pilot-local, SW-remote-trust (w6), SW-docs, SW-pilot-remote (w7), SW-reassign (w13). P-drivers: DRV-lane-interface w2 (Lane contract and process-headless driver; ACP, Pi RPC, OpenCode HTTP and tmux plug in as transports), DRV-model-catalog w3 (families, windows, prices, limits as data), DRV-combine w4. The opencode descriptor (ddflow/harnesses/opencode.toml) exists: opencode.json MCP, plugin hooks, AGENTS.md, .opencode/ commands, skills, agents; it states nothing about provider or model endpoints. A keyword scan of open tasks for vllm, ollama, local model, base url, openai-compatible, gpu, litellm finds no task. ddflow task add already has --resources (physical resources a task runs on, e.g. gpu:4) and services/slots.py limits concurrent suites: reuse for endpoint capacity. services/launchers.py and services/lanes/* exist (state, brief, advise) but no scheduler launch. LC-wake (P-lane-consolidation) gives a lane inbox and wake reasons that the lead channel can reuse.
- **Falsifier.** opencode's own support for a custom OpenAI-compatible provider in opencode.json (provider block with baseURL) and for tool calls on the chosen local model is NOT verified here: SW-local-endpoint must probe it with the installed opencode and the LAN endpoint before anything else is built; if a model cannot do tool calls reliably the family goes into the ledger as unqualified, not into the pilot.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow show P-swarm P-drivers P-acp DRV-lane-interface DRV-model-catalog SW-conformance SW-headroom; ddflow decision show D-swarm-answers; ddflow list task (3 pages) transitive closure of SW-pilot-local; sed ddflow/harnesses/opencode.toml; ls ddflow/services/lanes; keyword scan of open tasks; sed docs/ddflow/research/swarm-orchestration.md headings. NOT probed: a running opencode with a local endpoint.
```

**Sources:** D-swarm-answers; docs/ddflow/research/swarm-orchestration.md; docs/ddflow/decisions/swarm-orchestration.md; P-swarm; P-drivers; P-acp; ddflow/harnesses/opencode.toml

- **Mechanism.** step() compares against marks[level] on the way up and marks[level-1]-hysteresis on the way down, and holds when None
- **Falsifier.** A hypothesis counterexample where a higher reading yields a higher cap or a wobble inside the band lowers the level


## How can ddflow maintain docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CHANGELOG.md so the requirements alone can regenerate the code and let an AI see how features correlate and where the gaps are, and what already exists to build on?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Most machinery exists; the regenerable user-requirements document and its gap analysis do not. ddflow can already generate documents from the event log (ddflow export: bugs, changelog, decisions, roadmap, rules, sessions, status, worklog), keeps operator prompts verbatim (ddflow session prompt), accepted decisions, research, done tasks and a declared surface registry, and has queued document-type work (B-dt-*). Missing: (a) a requirements document kind built from USER requirements (operator prompts, decisions, stories) in a regeneration-oriented structure: IDs, use cases, feature relations, interfaces, constraints, build order, traceability to modules/tests/tasks; (b) a deterministic gap finder (requirement with no code/test/task, shipped surface/knob/event with no requirement, conflicts, stale entries) plus an AI-assisted use-case gap pass; (c) managed docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CHANGELOG.md under docs/ (today ARCHITECTURE.md is hand-written and the changelog is the generated root CHANGELOG.md). The file name REQUIREMENTS.md collides with queued RQM-docs-sync, which generates REQUIREMENTS.md from ENGINEERING requirements (agent standards, class and strength); that needs an operator decision, default: one document with the user requirements as the body and the engineering requirements as a section fed by RQM-docs-sync's collection.
- **Mechanism.** ddflow docs has only 'check' (docs drift). ddflow export lists 8 kinds, none 'requirements' or 'architecture'; D-export-documents governs it. CHANGELOG.md exists at the repo root (87 KB, header 'ddflow:generated doc=changelog v=0.2.1'); docs/CHANGELOG.md and docs/REQUIREMENTS.md do not exist; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md exists (31 KB, hand-maintained). Queued, overlapping but not the same: RQM-docs-sync (requirement documents <-> records, generated REQUIREMENTS.md doc type, export/kind_requirements.py; needs RQM-model), P-user-stories (26 open tasks: personas, epics, stories with criteria, US-trace, US-views generates story/epic/persona documents), B-dt-library (shipped doc types incl. ARCHITECTURE and CHANGELOG; chain of ~15 open B-dt-* tasks), B-dt-ownership (generated vs human sections), B-dt-obligations (code-to-doc coupling), RQM-trace and RQM-conflicts. Sources of user requirements already in the log: operator prompts recorded verbatim, accepted decisions (Operator ... quotes), research and tasks whose bodies quote 'Operator request'. Surface inventories for orphan-feature detection exist as data: surfaces/declared registry (CLI/MCP), config sections and knobs, harness descriptors, event kinds. Bug Ba41e4bb639 (version cut cannot commit the changelog it writes) affects any changelog move.
- **Falsifier.** If the regenerated code from the requirements document cannot reproduce the public surface (CLI help, MCP tool list, config knobs, event kinds: the golden snapshots) the document is not regenerable in the stated sense and SD-regen-check must report which surfaces are unspecified. If P-user-stories ships stories with trace and views first, SD-model should consume them and SD-doctype shrinks to a view.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow docs --help; ddflow export; ls docs; head CHANGELOG.md; ddflow search REQUIREMENTS.md; ddflow show RQM-docs-sync B-dt-library; list of US- RQM- B-dt- tasks; ddflow decision show D-export
```

**Sources:** ddflow/surfaces/declared; D-export-documents; RQM-docs-sync; P-user-stories; B-dt-library; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; CHANGELOG.md

STATUS: FINDINGS 1` records a `chunk_findings` entry whose `detail`.strip() == ''. If a '#N [MEDIUM] path:line' empty body persists, the claim is false.


## Does it make sense, and is it implementable, to unite two lanes whose items are done implementing and wait on the same remaining gate (hand the donor lane's context to the surviving lane, close both items together, reuse the freed lane), and would ddflow wait allow the interruption, merge and messages this needs?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes, but narrower than 'merge lanes'. (1) The lock/time saving comes from sharing the gate RUN, which P-batch-gates already designs and decided (D-BG-1..10: one CI/unit_tests/standards run on the merge of path-disjoint members, line-sized reviews, ddmin culprit search, one-transaction fan-out); uniting two agents does not by itself cut suite-lock contention. (2) The new value is freeing the LANE: when the remaining gates are machine gates (ci, unit_tests, standards via roborev) the agent need not wait at all, so release-at-enqueue plus a deterministic integrator frees the lane with no context transfer; only agent-judgement gates (rubber_duck, critic, bug_hunt, dedupe) need an agent, and there one surviving lane can review a combined unit while the donor's context travels as a handoff capsule. (3) ddflow wait cannot be interrupted today in the needed way: it is a blocking log poll, the holder is told at heartbeat, release or complete and never interrupted (services/waits.py), an MCP wait gives no progress and was aborted at 1800 s (Bfc43dae5b9), --max-s is ignored (B-wait-lease-max-s-ignored), and a message to a busy agent is delivered only at its next tool round. The pieces exist: DX-watch-job (done) gives bounded waits with resume tokens that renew leases; a wake reason (ready, merge_offer, yield, message) and an inbox are the missing part.
- **Mechanism.** Measured (ddflow metrics lanes/summary, this repo): lane utilisation 79%, 8 of 31 lane-samples idle beside ready work; ready-to-claimed wait p50 1.0 h, p90 31.3 h; ci n=2088 p50 8 min p90 24 min with lock/slot queueing n=241 p50 6 min max 1.8 h; unit_tests n=988 p50 10 min p90 24 min with queueing n=10 p50 1 min. The host-wide suite lock (services/suitelock.py, [ci].max_concurrent_suites default 1) is FIFO, so waiting agents only sit in a queue; running one combined suite instead of two is the real lock relief (batch gates), not merging agents. Constraints found: r-lock-cycle-selfheal forbids agents holding leases while they wait, so release-at-enqueue must hand custody of the item to the queue; each item has its own branch and worktree and own event stream (agent identity as_agent) so a survivor acting for a donor needs delegated custody recorded in the log; the cross-family reviewer rule is evaluated per item author, so a united lane must keep each item's author recorded; BG-4 already selects members that are pairwise path-disjoint. Context transfer can reuse DX-park-and-resume (derived resume brief), DX-handoff-pack, CC-resume-pack and SW-seed-pack instead of a new format. Prior art in queue: P-batch-gates (13 open tasks, waves 0-6), DX-park-and-resume (wave 2), SW-pull (wave 5), DX-lease-release-early (wave 0).
- **Falsifier.** If lane-hours spent waiting on a shared gate are small next to implementation time (the ci lock queue is p50 6 min on 241 of 2088 runs), release-at-enqueue plus batch gates already captures the benefit and lane unite is not worth building; if united lanes make the combined gate red more often than it saves (ddmin dissolves them), batch-only wins. A probe: LC-measure computes lane-hours waiting per shared gate from the event log.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow metrics lanes; ddflow metrics summary; ddflow wait --help; sed ddflow/services/waits.py suitelock.py; docs/ddflow/decisions/batch-gates.md; ddflow bug show B-wait-lease-max-s-ignored; ddflow recall idle lane; ddflow list task for BG- SW- DX-park-and-resume CC-resume-pack
```

**Sources:** ddflow/services/waits.py; ddflow/services/suitelock.py; docs/ddflow/decisions/batch-gates.md; D-BG-Q1..Q10; D-gate-economy-r3; r-lock-cycle-selfheal; Bfc43dae5b9; B-wait-lease-max-s-ignored

## Why does the dead-knob ratchet report enforce.machine_local_keys as dead when machine_local_keys is read and its behaviour tests pass, and what is the minimal fix?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B21ec47765c`

- **Claim.** enforce.machine_local_keys is reported as a dead knob only because _extra_keys reads it through getattr(..., None), which the name-based ratchet scan cannot see; reading it as cfg.enforce.machine_local_keys makes the scan see the read.
- **Mechanism.** Config.enforce is an EnforceConfig dataclass with machine_local_keys defaulting to [] so cfg.enforce.machine_local_keys always resolves; the dead-knob detector matches the literal .enforce.machine_local_keys token but not a getattr string literal.
- **Falsifier.** Replacing direct access with getattr(enforce,'machine_local_keys') would make test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py::test_no_knob_is_dead report enforce.machine_local_keys as dead again.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python -m pytest tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py -q
before: FAILED test_no_knob_is_dead (['enforce.machine_local_keys']); after the read change: passed
```

## Why does `ddflow bug fixed --lint-exempt --landed` refuse, and is the fix to allow --landed as the commit reference?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Bab0c83b80c`

- **Claim.** `ddflow bug fixed <lint-bug> --lint-exempt <reason> --landed <sha>` is refused because `--landed` is placed in `_close_lint_exempt`'s `takes_no` set, which refuses any non-empty entry.
- **Mechanism.** `bug_close.bug_fixed` builds `takes_no = {"--landed": landed, ...}` and passes its non-empty entries to `_close_lint_exempt`, which returns a refusal naming each disallowed flag. `--landed` names the commit reference, not the waived regression test.
- **Falsifier.** The command would return exit 0 (recording the landing) instead of exit 3 if `--landed` were not in the disallowed set.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python probe: init repo, file CI lint bug, commit a fix, then api.bug_fixed(repo, bug, lint_exempt="ruff format applied", landed=sha)
exit= 3
```

## What does it take to support Z.ai's ZCode coding agent in ddflow at the same level as the other supported agents, and what is already there?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** ZCode (binary 'zcode', repo github.com/zai-org/ZCode, site zcode.z.ai) has everything ddflow needs for full parity: documented hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop; exit code 2 blocks; PreToolUse can return additionalContext), MCP under mcp.servers, AGENTS.md instructions, skills in .zcode/skills and .agents/skills, plugins, a headless mode and a doctor command. The work is upgrading the existing 'glm' descriptor (family zcode, MCP path only, hooks 'nv') into a verified, complete 'zcode' harness plus a hook normalizer/emitter, a lane driver and tests, not adding a new engine. Several facts are undocumented and need a live probe before they may be stated: hook payload field names, session id source, the project hook config path, a project commands directory, subagent definitions and worktree behaviour.
- **Mechanism.** ddflow/harnesses/glm.toml already exists (id glm, family zcode, title 'Z Code (GLM)', delta zcode-glm.md, mcp path .zcode/config.json shape mcp.servers, verified 2026-10-09 with the only source github.com/zai-org/ZCode and 'everything beyond the MCP path' unverified); ddflow harness list shows glm hooks=nv best=nv, i.e. no hook support delivered. ZCode usage docs (apps/zcode-cli/docs/usage, Chinese): 02-cli-reference: 'zcode --prompt TEXT --cwd DIR --mode plan|build|edit|yolo|guarded --output-format text|json|stream-json', --resume ID / --continue, 'zcode doctor --json', --version; no --model, --permission-mode, --allowed-tools or --max-turns flags. 03-config: user config [REDACTED:path] (runtime, permissions, MCP, hooks, plugins), provider config [REDACTED:path], project config <project>/zcode.json and <project>/.zcode/config.json, features.mcp/subagent/memory/skill flags, env ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR, ZCODE_STORAGE_DIR, ZCODE_SESSION_DB_PATH, ZCODE_LOG_DIR and no session-id variable. 07-mcp: mcp.servers with type stdio|http|sse, user config wins over project config for a same-named server, features.mcp must be on. 08-skills: .zcode/skills and .agents/skills with SKILL.md (name, description), custom slash commands only through plugins (commands/hello.md, $ARGUMENTS), no subagent dir documented. 09-hooks: hooks must be enabled in run config (hooks.enabled), project hooks are UNTRUSTED by default and trust is bound to workspace identity and declaration content (fails closed), so ddflow cannot install working project hooks silently. 11-memory: reads [REDACTED:path] then the project AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md and other products' instruction files are not auto-imported.
- **Falsifier.** If a live zcode (install needs the operator's consent; 'zcode doctor --json' and a recorded hook payload) shows different hook event names, payload fields or config paths than the Chinese docs state, the descriptor must follow the probe and R-zcode-support is amended. If workspace-trust makes project hooks impossible to install without an interactive prompt, hook delivery must go through user-level config or a plugin, and the ladder level for zcode stays 'declared' until that works.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebFetch github.com/zai-org/ZCode README; usage pages 02-cli-reference, 03-config, 07-mcp, 08-skills, 09-hooks, 11-memory; ddflow harness list; sed ddflow/harnesses/glm.toml; ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml as the reference; docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md. NOT probed: a running zcode binary.
```

**Sources:** https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode; https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode/tree/main/apps/zcode-cli/docs/usage; https://zcode.z.ai/; ddflow/harnesses/glm.toml; docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md

## Can ddflow add a default 'security' gate covering security bugs and issues, dependency checks and upgrades, and compliance with security policies including corporate ones, and what already exists to build on?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Yes. ddflow has NO security gate today (ddflow gate list: research rules implement rubber_duck critic verify standards ci unit_tests bug_hunt dedupe live_test docs corrections tasks merge). The machinery needed already exists: GateDef (applies_to task|phase|both, applies_when path globs, requires_evidence, mutations, reviewer family), custom gates in .ddflow/gates.toml, a [gates] task_pipeline list, companions, layered config with company-enforced floors (D-config-layer-order), graded policies (P-graded-policies) and waivers (D-DEP-Q8). The work is a new GateDef plus one shared scanner runner, finding-to-bug filing and a policy checklist, not a new engine. It must reuse the scanners the ci gate already runs instead of adding a second copy.
- **Mechanism.** Security checks exist but outside ddflow's gates: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs gitleaks 8.30.1 (full history), bandit -r ddflow/ -ll (package only), pip-audit --strict whose failure is only a warning (|| echo ::warning), and CodeQL security-and-quality; the ci gate runs the pre-commit stages (D-ci-parity-r2) so bandit and gitleaks happen there but a result is just pass/fail with no severity, no finding record and no policy or dependency-upgrade view. Prior queue items overlap strongly and must not be duplicated: B-security-pass (operator 2026-09-28: phase-level security gate, cadence, SAST/secret/CVE/image scanners as companions; blocked on P-unify, SC-catalogue), B-dependency-upgrades, B-security-pass-sync, B-export-security-md (SECURITY.md), B-pi-review-lens (security review lens as data), B-par-phase-barrier, IA-supply-chain, IA-compliance, GV-guardrails, GP-org and CM-packs (company policy packs pinned by digest), P-deprecation (security exceptions need severity=security and a lesson). Note .ddflow/config.toml pins task_pipeline literally, so a packaged-default gate does not reach this project until that list is amended.
- **Falsifier.** If B-security-pass already specifies and is about to ship the same gate (its blockers P-unify, SC-catalogue close soon), a new phase duplicates it and the right move is to extend that item; if a new 'security' gate in the default task_pipeline makes every unit-test-only change wait on scanners that are unavailable on most machines, applies_when scoping and the unavailable-not-passed rule must keep it from stalling the queue.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow gate list; ddflow show B-security-pass B-dependency-upgrades B-security-pass-sync B-export-security-md B-pi-review-lens B-par-phase-barrier; grep bandit|gitleaks|pip-audit|CodeQL .github/workflows/ci.yml; ddflow decision show D-config-layer-order D-DEP-Q8; sed ddflow/services/gates/defs.py GateDef fields
```

**Sources:** ddflow/services/gates/defs.py; .github/workflows/ci.yml; .ddflow/config.toml [gates]; B-security-pass; D-ci-parity-r2; D-config-layer-order; D-DEP-Q8

## How should ddflow offer shell completion (commands, options, IDs) given its argparse CLI, two-runtime-dependency policy and slow startup?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** A stdlib-only, generated completion works: (1) static command/option tree is exported from build_parser() into per-shell scripts (bash, zsh, fish) at install/upgrade time; (2) IDs come from a read-only sqlite3 query of .ddflow/index.db-* items table, not from running ddflow; (3) argcomplete is not adopted as a runtime dependency. A per-TAB 'ddflow' subprocess is not viable.
- **Mechanism.** ddflow is pure argparse (SuggestingParser, build_parser() in surfaces/cli.py, subcommands registered from surfaces/parsers/*, compat aliases via _WordsRecorder/_hide_from_abbreviation). pyproject declares exactly two runtime deps (jinja2, tomlkit) by policy; argcomplete and shtab are not installed. 'ddflow --version' takes ~1.0 s and importing ddflow.surfaces.cli ~0.83 s (ddflow.api imports dominate), 'ddflow list/show' ~4.7 s on this loaded machine, so argcomplete-style per-TAB invocation would add 1-5 s per keypress. The derived index .ddflow/index.db-<code fingerprint> is plain sqlite: items(id,kind,title,state,needs,tags,...) 3488 rows, count query 0.0 s, openable read-only with stdlib sqlite3. Index name embeds code_fingerprint(), so a stale file can exist; the completer must pick the newest by mtime or fall back to nothing.
- **Falsifier.** If a bash/zsh completion that shells out to python -c 'import sqlite3' still exceeds ~100 ms per TAB, or if the newest-index heuristic offers stale ids in a repo with several index files, the sqlite approach fails and a pre-generated ids cache file refreshed by the post-merge hook is needed.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 sqlite3 read-only open of .ddflow/index.db-f4f40e138e77095d: select count(*) from items -> 3488 in 0.0 s; ddflow --version 1.01 s; python -c 'import ddflow.surfaces.cli' 0.83 s; python -c 'import argcomplete' -> ModuleNotFoundError
```

**Sources:** ddflow/surfaces/cli.py build_parser; ddflow/surfaces/registry.py; pyproject.toml dependencies; ddflow/infra/store.py index.db naming

## Will a pure triage classify recovered-at-a-glance facts into SAFE_AUTO/PROPOSE/OPERATOR exactly as orphan-recovery.md section 3.2 prescribes?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DX-recovery-plan`

- **Claim.** A pure function triage(facts, now, limits) maps measured rows (lease sweep, dead gate markers, unended jobs, orphaned queue entries) to one Action per item; every ACTION's class equals: SAFE_AUTO for nothing-to-lose effects (expire a clean lease, record unreported unavailable, job end from its logged exit, requeue orphans); PROPOSE for a resume (claim; force only for an expired lease holding commits); OPERATOR once attempts reach the cap. Nothing automatic ever keys off 'could not measure'.
- **Mechanism.** The safety contract is enforced by construction: salvageable=None/false/true map to disjoint branches; attempts>=cap gates the resume branch absolut; and only SAFE_AUTO actions carry effects the apply service recognizes.
- **Falsifier.** The suite test_recovery_plan.py asserting unmeasurable->propose and cap->operator FAILS (or the classification table row pairs disagree).

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow gate run DX-recovery-plan unit_tests (selection: tests/test_recovery_plan.py)
```

**Sources:** docs/ddflow/research/orphan-recovery.md#3

## Does the default pre-push ci fail a branch on errors the pushed diff does not make?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Bf333cb2f5d`

- **Claim.** Replacing --all-files with --from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD runs the pre-push hooks on the pushed change only, so an error the base carries outside the diff cannot fail the branch (pre-commit's three-dot range over a merged HEAD is exactly the pushed change).
- **Mechanism.** In the merged scratch tree HEAD holds the base, so merge-base(since,HEAD)=since and the three-dot diff is the branch's own files; unchanged base files never reach the hooks.
- **Falsifier.** A repo whose base has a python file carrying a BAD marker fails a docs-only branch's CI.run (status failed, grep finds BAD).

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run python -c 'CI.scope_to_diff(DEFAULT_COMMAND, tree, head_sha)' on a temp git repo
scoped: pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD
```

**Sources:** tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py

## Does roborev show --job N report 'no review found' for a merely-queued job while roborev list --json names its true status, making list-polling the only honest wait primitive?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DX-roborev-wait-no-review`

- **Claim.** A ddflow wait wrapper must poll roborev list --json status and say running vs failed itself: show/wait wording cannot distinguish a live job from a vanished one
- **Mechanism.** roborev show --job N reads 'no review found' for a queued job; the list JSON records the real status, so polling it separates still-running from ended
- **Falsifier.** Refuted if show --job 3711 names the queued job or a running status instead of 'no review found'

**Probe:**

```console
$ paused queue; fresh repo roborev init; roborev review HEAD; roborev show --job N vs roborev list --json; cancel job; resume queue
roborev review HEAD -> "Enqueued job 3711 for 0808c9a (agent: kilo)"; roborev show --job 3711 -> "Error: no review found for job 3711" (exit 1) while roborev list --json -> 3711 | queued | review | kilo | 0808c9a at the same second
```

## Can [agent].family / DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILY stand in for a model id as the author identity complete and gate record judge?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DX-author-family`

- **Claim.** AgentConfig has no family knob, DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILY is ignored, and a bare family name (an [agent].families value such as alibaba) is not accepted where a model id is: complete/reviewer_independence resolve it to the empty string and refuse the author.
- **Mechanism.** complete author identity is only a model id (flag or session), and family_for recognises needle keys, not family values; nothing maps a bare family or a configured family to the author.
- **Falsifier.** Config().agent.family existing, DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILY honoured, or family_of(alibaba) answering alibaba would refute/seal the probe.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python one-off setting DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILY=deepseek then hasattr(Config().agent, family) and G.family_of(alibaba, Config())
agent has family knob: False; env read as: AttributeError; family_of(alibaba): empty; accept FAMILY in place of a model: False
```


## DX-bug-repro-verify: does bug found --repro-cmd run the command; do bugs have a reproduced/unconfirmed state?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `DX-bug-repro-verify`

- **Claim.** bug found --repro-cmd CMD stores the command in the repro bundle with executed:false and never runs it; the Bug record has no reproduced/unconfirmed field, so ddflow cannot rank or wait on verification.


## Does the re-entrancy guard in EventLog.transaction() let a second THREAD of one process run inside concurrently with the holder?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Bf7f6540615`

- **Claim.** EventLog.transaction() lets a second THREAD of one process enter while the first thread holds it: the re-entrancy guard is keyed on (pid, lock path), so a different thread's EventLog is mistaken for a re-entrant caller, skips the flock, and its read-check-append races the holder's (2 successes where 1 is right).
- **Mechanism.** _HELD keyed (pid, str(path)): first thread takes the flock and sets _HELD=1; every other thread in the process matches that key, takes the re-entrancy branch and yields WITHOUT the flock. flock itself serializes across threads (separate open()s), only the shortcut lets them past.
- **Falsifier.** With the guard keyed (pid, thread, lock path), while thread A holds transaction(), thread B must NOT reach the inside: a handshake probe must print OVERLAP while held: False.

**Probe:**

```console
$ [REDACTED:path] /tmp/kilo/bf7_probe.py  (8-thread handshake: rival waits on holder's in-lock event, then enters its own transaction())
pre-fix: 'OVERLAP while held: True (a fix says False)'; post-fix: 'OVERLAP while held: False (a fix says False)'
```

## Does ddflow_wait over MCP still risk a client abort at 1800s idle, and where is the cap that governs it?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** ddflow_wait over MCP clamps any timeout to MCP_WAIT_MAX_S = WAIT_MAX_S = 1800 s -- exactly the idle window a silent client aborts at; a call whose client sent no progressToken can send no notifications/progress (the B7b3b4cf483 heartbeat needs a token), so such a call can still be aborted at 1800 s unanswered. Fix: cap the no-token wait strictly below 1800 s, keep the full 1800 s for a call carrying a valid progressToken.
- **Mechanism.** _wait_timeout() in ddflow/surfaces/tools/_common.py returns min(t, MCP_WAIT_MAX_S) and MCP_WAIT_MAX_S is core.clock.WAIT_MAX_S (1800); mcp.Server._progress() returns None without a string/number _meta.progressToken, and heartbeat() is a no-op with say=None
- **Falsifier.** a direct import calling _wait_timeout({'timeout': 1800}) shows a value below 1800

**Probe:**

```console
$ PYTHONPATH worktree python3 -c import _wait_timeout; print(_wait_timeout({'timeout': 1800}))
1800.0 (and 1e9 -> 1800.0, with token -> 1800.0; default 300.0)
```

## Does kind=bug have an owner filter on either surface, and what filters does the severity-sorted refetch replay?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B386e298783`

- **Claim.** Kind=bug has no owner filter: the engine (_FILTERS['bug']) does not take 'agent' and the CLI 'bug list' has no --owner flag, so a bug read echoes only its own filters ({state,phase,since,item}) and the sort refetch replays those; an owner asked on a bug read is the engine's refusal.
- **Mechanism.** services/viewers.list_view refuses a filter not in _FILTERS[kind]; kind=bug row owner is '' so filtering bugs by owner cannot match; finish_bug_list refetches dict(data['filters']) via _whole_bug_set.
- **Falsifier.** A bug read echoing an 'owner' key in filters, or 'bug list --owner' parsing, would refute it.

**Probe:**

```console
$ pytest -q tests/test_bug_list.py::test_mcp_bug_sort_serves_the_owner_filter; old form AssertionError 'owner' in {'state': 'open'}; corrected form passes
```

## Is an identical finding re-raised on another gate untriaged again, and does auto-linking the item's refuted triage to the raising gate fix it (B74d5c39e6e)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B74d5c39e6e`

- **Claim.** A review round of one gate raising a finding byte-identical to a finding the item already refuted (with a probe) on another gate is counted untriaged on the new gate; recording the item's refuted triage on the raising gate (keyed by the digest of its exact text) when the round is recorded removes the duplicate triage; a differently-worded claim stays untriaged.
- **Mechanism.** Triage verdicts fold per (item, gate, digest) in ddflow/core/handlers/gates.py _h_review_triaged; a second gate's re-raised claim has no verdict there. api/review.py _record_review records every gate's round, so digests already refuted in it.triage under another gate are one record-time chokepoint.
- **Falsifier.** tests/test_review_reraised_refuted.py FAILS on the unfixed code: rubber_duck counts refuted=0 untriaged=2 after raising the identical claim.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow gate run fix-B74d5c39e6e ci on the tree with the test but without the fix (queued behind other agents' whole-suite runs on the host lock): the two cases of tests/test_review_reraised_refuted.py FAIL.
```

## Where do session tokens go when ddflow is developed with Claude Code (one lead plus ~98 background subagents), and is the lead's 'messages 43.7%' the lever?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `TE-research`

- **Claim.** Subagents are 93% of weighted spend; 52% of subagent spend is whole-context cache rewrites after waits over the 5-minute subagent cache TTL; the lead is 7% so messages are a symptom, not the lever.
- **Mechanism.** Subagent requests use a 5-minute prompt-cache TTL (docs: subagents fall outside the main-conversation bucket); every wait over 5 minutes (review, CI, sleep poll loops capped near 570 s) makes the next call re-write the whole context at 1.25x instead of reading at 0.1x.
- **Falsifier.** Subagent cache writes would show ephemeral_1h tokens or few big writes after gaps over 5 minutes; or the lead would be the larger share of weighted units.


## Why do gate run ci waiters starve on the host suite lock?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B1fa77a6832`

- **Claim.** suitelock.hold races Slots.hold polling every 50 ms; a fresh arrival can win the flock over a waiter that queued earlier, so no order exists
- **Mechanism.** Slots.hold sweeps slots with flock LOCK_NB; no ticket or order, the first poller after release wins
- **Falsifier.** Four waiters enqueued in order get the lock in a different order, or the refusal lacks a queue position

**Probe:**

```console
$ pytest tests/test_suitelock_queue.py against HEAD's suitelock.py
6 failed against the unfixed code (no ticket queue, refusal lacks pid and queue position); 14 passed with the fix
```


- **Claim.** The pin is stale: two merged branches added result fields (landed from bug fixed/update --landed, kept_stash from merge-stash work) without re-recording; code is right
- **Mechanism.** pin compares exactly; each branch recorded only its own addition, so each passed alone
- **Falsifier.** regenerating from clean main would show a removed field, not only additions

**Probe:**

```console
$ git archive HEAD to scratch; pytest the test; DDFLOW_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; diff old new
fails; regenerated diff is +4 lines only: landed (2) and kept_stash (2), no removals
```

## Which pytest results does verify_regression_test misread as fails-before / passes?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Bregtest-skip-counted-as-pass`

- **Claim.** It reads only the unit_tests gate outcome (pytest exit code): exit 0 covers skipped and xfail, so a skip on the pre-fix tree is 'passes on pre-fix' and a skip on the fixed tree is 'passes'; exit 4/5 (not collected) and a fixture error (exit 1, 'N error') read as 'failed' = fails before
- **Mechanism.** mutation.py verify_regression_test/_prefix_check compare run_command_gate outcome only
- **Falsifier.** a skip/xfail/uncollected/erroring test on the relevant tree yields could-not-run on the unfixed code

**Probe:**

```console
$ pytest tests/test_regression_skip_not_pass.py on unfixed code
5 cases: skipped_before refused as 'PASSES on the pre-fix tree'; xfail_before same; skipped_on_the_fix, not_collected_before, error_before all 'verified' (assert 'verified' == 'could-not-run')
```

## Does ddflow have any record, tracker integration or criterion-to-test binding for user stories?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `US-research`

- **Claim.** ddflow has no story record, no tracker integration, and no acceptance-criterion verification; the only hooks are the inert requirement kind, the presence-only acceptance check in plan check, and the unexposed ask engine; descriptors cannot hold structured objects.
- **Mechanism.** Data kinds only allow string, array and integer fields; external sync reads sibling repo logs; bug regression verification is the only test-binding code.
- **Falsifier.** A story/criterion/tracker module or a nested field type in ddflow/core/kinddata.py.
- **Budget.** about 1 hour, no GPU

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow record requirement list; ddflow external --help; ddflow import --help; grep -n 'type = "' ddflow/templates/kinds/*.toml | sort | uniq -c; grep -rln 'services.ask' ddflow
No requirement records.; external sync = observe the sibling-repo items needs names; import reads markdown checklists; field types: 18 array, 5 integer; services.ask referenced only by core/handlers/asks.py, approvals.py and ask/engine.py
```

**Sources:** https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md, https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/, https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec, https://cucumber.io/docs/bdd/example-mapping/, https://cucumber.io/docs/bdd/better-gherkin/, https://alistairmavin.com/ears/, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/boards/work-items/guidance/agile-process-workflow, https://linear.app/docs/conceptual-model

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `SPEC-research`

- **Claim.** The completion ledger digests only the task's own title, body and globs; the injection collector knows only rules and decisions. So a spec edit after claim is undetectable and no spec text reaches a session.
- **Mechanism.** ledger.requirement_digest hashes title/body/globs; inject.collect returns rule defs and decisions.
- **Falsifier.** A cited-document digest in ledger facts or a spec kind in collect().

