## What makes ddflow merge print 'fatal: stash failed' and merge nothing, and why does the retry work?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-merge-stash-failed-transient`

- **Claim.** git merge (non-ff, dirty tracked tree) runs git stash create; with .git/index.lock held by another process it dies with 'fatal: stash failed' before merging; the lock is transient.
- **Mechanism.** builtin/merge.c save_state() -> git stash create; no stash call exists in ddflow code (grep).
- **Falsifier.** Merge with index.lock held succeeds, or fails with another message.

**Probe:**

```console
$ touch .git/index.lock; echo 7 > b; git merge --no-ff -m m br2 (scratch repo) ; GIT_TRACE shows 'git stash create'
fatal: stash failed (rc=128), tree unchanged; without lock the same merge works. New tests fail on old code with exactly 'fatal: stash failed'
```

## Is the ci 'passed' with 5 listed failing tests a legitimate recorded rerun or a false pass?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-ci-gate-prints-passed-with-failing-tests`

- **Claim.** run_command_gate classifies on exit code alone; flake accounting (_rerun_failed_tests/_account_flakes) runs only on FAILED results and never changes a verdict, so a command exiting 0 over output with FAILED lines is recorded passed with no rerun evidence. The doubled verdict is the nested command's 'ci: passed' in the tail plus run_text's 'ci: PASSED'.
- **Mechanism.** classify_exit -> PASSED when code==0; failed_tests evidence is lifted regardless; no code path reruns on a pass
- **Falsifier.** A gate whose command exits 0 and prints 'FAILED tests/x.py::t' ends non-passed or carries rerun evidence on the unfixed code

**Probe:**

```console
$ pytest tests/test_gate_passed_with_failures.py on unfixed code
unit_tests: PASSED after output 'FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_a - boom' / 'unit_tests: passed' (4 failed on old code, assert code==1 got 0). The original dx-round-justified command could not be inspected; its own retry is unverified, but ddflow could not tell either way: no rerun evidence existed.
```

## Does a chunk retry escape the hard wall-clock cancel (B587e607ad9)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-review-chunk-overran-bound`

- **Claim.** The retry path is not unbounded: _retry_truncated races through _race -> _bounded (cut at min(timeout_s, total_budget_s - elapsed)); the stated '2132s elapsed' was total time since review start (first round ~1800s + retry round 332s) shown beside a per-request bound, i.e. a misleading line, already fixed by round_started in 0d99adf99 which landed after the bug was filed

```console
1 passed; mutated: 1 failed AssertionError at line 35
```

## why does ddflow ci run --ref <sha> run the whole suite for a one-file change when tests_scope=selected

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-ci-selected-runs-full-suite`

- **Mechanism.** services/ci.py run(): scope = CS.plan(...) only if for_item and no command; otherwise scope None and _runs_whole_suite is True. The selection needs only the diff against base, not an item.
- **Falsifier.** A regression test calling cirun.run(ref=<branch sha>, base=main) on a one-file change shows scope=selected and one pytest call on the reaching file; if it shows scope full, the claim is wrong

- **Mechanism.** ExtensionAPI.on(event, handler); handlers may return {block,reason}, or continue:true at the actionable boundaries.

Guard continuation conditions because an unconditional continuation can loop." "A tool_call handler failure blocks the tool as a fail-safe."

## What does Claude Code 2.1.296 do when a stdio MCP server exits mid-session?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `SU-reconnect-research`

## Can an MCP server learn at initialize whether the client re-fetches on list_changed?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `SU-reconnect-research`

- **Claim.** On 2025-11-25 and earlier no negotiated field signals list_changed handling; clientInfo.name is distinctive for most clients but version is a constant for opencode ('unknown'), Qwen ('0.0.1'), Continue ('1.0.0'); on 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged:true is an explicit opt-in.
- **Mechanism.** Legacy capabilities carry only roots/sampling/elicitation/tasks/extensions; roots.listChanged is about client roots. Qwen (ignores) and Gemini (honours) both send roots.listChanged, Cline (honours) and Roo (ignores) both send {}, so capabilities do not discriminate.
- **Falsifier.** A client that sends a capability or experimental key whose presence perfectly predicts list_changed re-fetch.

**Probe:**

```console
$ rc.py logging stdio server run under claude -p and kilo run; spec pages fetched; client source reads at named commits
claude-code 2.1.296 initialize: {"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{"roots":{"listChanged":true},"elicitation":{"form":{},"url":{}}},"clientInfo":{"name":"claude-code","title":"Claude Code","version":"2.1.296"}} preceded by server/discover (2026-07-28 _meta). kilo 7.8.12: {"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{"roots":{}},"clientInfo":{"name":"kilo","version":"7.8.12"}}
```

**Sources:** https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions.md, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning

## Which other clients ddflow supports honour list_changed, and how does the 2026-07-28 revision change server-initiated list notifications and caching?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Client support is uneven: Cursor CLI is reported to ignore tools/list_changed mid-session (new tools need restart/config touch); Claude Code was reported the same (anthropics/claude-code#62058) but 2.1.296 honours it (R-soft-claude-listchanged); Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code/Copilot, opencode, Kimi, Qwen are unverified. Under 2026-07-28 list_changed is delivered only on an opted-in subscriptions/listen stream and tools/list results carry ttlMs/cacheScope; ddflow currently sets tools/list ttlMs=3,600,000 and implements no subscriptions/listen, so a 2026-07-28 client may legitimately keep a changed tool list for an hour.
- **Mechanism.** Soft upgrade via re-announcement needs both a server that can emit the notification on the negotiated revision and a client that acts on it; ttlMs must be short (or digest-versioned) for the cache path to converge.
- **Falsifier.** Any listed client re-fetching on an unsolicited notification (per-client probe), or a 2026-07-28 stdio client that ignores ttlMs.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebFetch of the 2026-07-28 changelog and the tools page; WebSearch for client reports; grep of ddflow for subscriptions/listen and CACHE_TTL_MS.
Changelog items 4 and 'Minor 5' (subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged/promptsListChanged opt-ins; CacheableResult ttlMs/cacheScope 'complement existing listChanged'); Cursor forum thread 161459 (2026-05-24) 'not acted on mid-session', no fix; grep: no 'subscriptions' in ddflow, CACHE_TTL_MS tools/list=3_600_000.
```

**Sources:** https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://forum.cursor.com/t/mcp-notifications-tools-list-changed-not-acted-on-mid-session/161459, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools

## Is in-process importlib reload (option B) a safe way to apply an upgrade to the running ddflow server?

**Verdict: REFUTED**

- **Claim.** Not safe: ddflow is 628 modules with 44 function-local imports and 158 modules already loaded, so after the package files change, lazily imported modules would come from the NEW tree while the loaded ones stay OLD (mixed versions), and importlib.reload does not rebind names imported with `from x import y` in other modules.
- **Mechanism.** sys.modules holds old module objects; function-local imports resolve at call time against the files on disk.
- **Falsifier.** A reload sequence over the whole package that leaves no stale references and passes the test suite, or zero lazy imports.

**Probe:**

```console
$ grep -rnE '^\s{4,}(from|import) ddflow|^\s{4,}from \.+' ddflow --include=*.py | wc -l; python3 -c 'import ddflow.surfaces.mcp, sys; print(sum(m.startswith("ddflow") for m in sys.modules))'; find ddflow -name '*.py' | wc -l
44 ; 158 ; 628
```

**Sources:** ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py

## Can a tiny stdio shim keep the client connection while its backend worker is replaced and the new worker's extra tool is announced?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** A 28-line stdlib shim that forwards JSON-RPC lines to a child worker, replaces the worker on request (replaying the cached initialize) and emits notifications/tools/list_changed lets Claude Code keep one connection, see a new worker pid and a brand-new tool, with no agent restart.
- **Mechanism.** The client only knows the shim's stdio pipes; worker identity and tool set are behind it, and list_changed (honoured per R-soft-claude-listchanged) refreshes the cache.
- **Falsifier.** The new tool absent after the swap, the old worker pid after the swap, or the client reporting the server disconnected.

**Probe:**

```console
$ scratchpad lc/shim.py + worker.py via `claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config`: whoami, swap, ToolSearch newtool, newtool, whoami.
whoami -> 'worker pid=3827680 version=1'; swap -> 'swapped worker; announcing list_changed'; ToolSearch -> mcp__d__newtool; newtool -> 'worker pid=3833416 version=2 tool=newtool'; whoami -> 'worker pid=3833416 version=2'. Same client connection throughout. The prototype ignores in-flight drain, id collisions of the replayed initialize and stdin closing; those are the real work.
```

**Sources:** scratchpad lc/shim.py

## Does Claude Code re-fetch the tool list on notifications/tools/list_changed mid-session, and does it reach the model, with deferred tool loading (ToolSearch) on and off?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Claude Code 2.1.296 re-issues tools/list on notifications/tools/list_changed, including an UNSOLICITED one sent while idle, and a tool added or removed that way becomes callable / uncallable in the same session with ToolSearch finding the new tool. A CHANGED inputSchema of an already-loaded tool is re-fetched but was NOT visibly adopted by the model (it kept the old argument name) with ToolSearch on or off. notifications/prompts/list_changed did NOT trigger a prompts/list re-fetch in -p mode.
- **Mechanism.** The client keeps a per-server tool cache invalidated by the notification; the model-facing definitions of tools it already loaded are frozen for prompt-cache stability / are already in context, so additions and removals propagate and in-place edits do not reliably do so.
- **Falsifier.** No tools/list request after the notification in the server log, or the added tool absent from ToolSearch, or the removed tool still callable.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Stdlib stdio servers in the scratchpad (lc/srv.py, srv2.py) driven by `claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config ...` (stream-json), server-side request log inspected; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false variant.
srv.py: bump -> list_changed -> client sent tools/list (id 3) -> ToolSearch listed mcp__lc__added_later -> call returned MAGENTA. srv2.py: 8 s after start the server sent prompts+tools list_changed while the agent ran `sleep 15`: log shows IDLE-CHANGE then `tools/list id 4` (no prompts/list after id 2); tool `gone` then answered 'No such tool available ... connected but does not offer this tool'; greet was called with the OLD arg `a` although v2 required `b` (server unvalidated), identical with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false. Also: the client first probes server/discover (2026-07-28) and falls back to initialize 2025-11-25. n=1 per variant, haiku; prompts result may be a -p artifact.
```

**Sources:** https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools

## What does the ddflow MCP server cost to start, what does it hold, and what does it do after its files change?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** The stdio server (hand-rolled stdlib JSON-RPC, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py) imports ~350 modules, holds ~300 MB RSS and takes 6-20 s to answer initialize, because _instructions() -> upgrade_start -> upgrade_plan.build -> fill_queue folds the whole event log ~6 times; tools/list itself is 0 ms (123 tools, 108 KB). After an upgrade the running process keeps the code it imported (and refuses writes by skew guard); the only in-place cure today is [mcp].on_upgrade=reexec, an exec on the same stdio.
- **Mechanism.** Python imports once; 44 function-local imports and the eager top-level imports mean the server is the whole library. State is per-connection (protocol, client_info, agent, notice counters), small and serialisable (reexec already hands it off through DDFLOW_MCP_HANDOFF). A shim holding only that state plus a cached initialize/tools/list answer would start in ~20 ms.
- **Falsifier.** initialize answering in well under 1 s on this repo, or the connection state not being limited to protocol/client_info/agent/called_from.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 spawn of `python -m ddflow.surfaces.mcp`, send initialize then tools/list, time + /proc RSS; cProfile of Server.handle(initialize); python3 -c 'import json' for shim floor.
initialize 6307 ms / 6523 ms (2 runs), tools/list +9..22 ms, RSS 304 MB; in-process: import 0.28 s, Server() 0.00 s, initialize 20.95 s under cProfile (10.0 s cumulative in mcp.py:_upgrade_line -> api/setup.py:upgrade_start -> upgrade_plan.build -> fill_queue -> model.fold x6 / log.read_all x7); 158 ddflow modules loaded of 628 files before any call; shim floor (stdlib json) 12 ms.
```

**Sources:** ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py, ddflow/surfaces/mcp_upgrade.py, ddflow/config_sections/mcp.py

## Why do reviews not scale linearly with code, and which levers are fast without losing recall?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `RV-scale-research`

- **Claim.** Review time is the heavy-tailed count of generated reasoning tokens per request (decode 99% of time), nearly independent of diff size; neither linear in size nor queueing
- **Mechanism.** vLLM decode dominates; chunks run in one parallel wave so wall time is the max of N heavy-tailed draws; roborev inputs are re-sent but prefix-cached
- **Falsifier.** time linear in diff size and delay is queueing only


## Does emitting MCP progress notifications alone keep long ddflow tool calls alive across clients?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `RM-long-ops-research`

- **Claim.** Only for Claude Code's idle timer; its wall clock ignores progress and other clients are unproven, so detach+poll handle is required
- **Mechanism.** Claude Code: idle window (30 min stdio) reset by progress, wall-clock MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT hard; ddflow gate_run/ci send no progress
- **Falsifier.** A client keeps a call alive on progress alone with no max

**Probe:**

```console
$ claude -p with /tmp/mcp-probe/server.py sleepy 40s: A idle=15s progress on -> completed; B progress off -> aborted 'no response or progress for 30s'; C MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT=15s progress on -> 'timed out after 15s'
A: slept 40.0s, [REDACTED:secret] (no SECRET-LOG seen by model); B: sent no response or progress for 30s; aborting; C: timed out after 15s
```

**Sources:** docs/ddflow/research/mcp-long-ops.md; code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp; modelcontextprotocol.io 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28

## How should ddflow's configuration become layered (packaged default.toml, project config.toml, .ddflow/conf.d drop-ins), dynamic (templates, interpolation), persistent for tool-written changes, and fast, and is dynaconf the right engine?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Keep the in-house tomllib+tomlkit loader and add dynaconf's capabilities to it: a packaged default.toml, sorted .ddflow/conf.d/*.toml drop-ins with replace/extend semantics and per-key origin, a managed drop-in for tool-written changes (comments preserved), lazy code-free ${...} interpolation, Jinja (sandboxed, extension allowlist, imported only when a template marker is present) and a compiled config cache. Dynaconf itself is a poor fit: +70-150 ms import and 12-15 MB per command (the hook path), loaders.write drops TOML comments, @jinja/@format/hooks can read the environment or execute code, no Jinja extension hook, and D-unify caps runtime dependencies at two.
- **Mechanism.** Config today: 35 sections, 314 knobs with Python dataclass defaults; layers default < committed .ddflow/config.toml < local < env; flow.* choices recorded in the log fill only unset knobs; no user/system layer; gates/reviewers/companions already load from per-topic files via a hand-written filename list; config.toml re-read 3-4 times per command, no cache; import ddflow.config 80-100 ms, Config.load about 2 ms, ddflow --version 0.72 s. B-org-layers (one layer stack) and B-org-bundle (a bundle mirrors .ddflow/) already describe the requested default.toml + conf.d layout, so it is their foundation, not a second mechanism.
- **Falsifier.** Wrong if the compiled cache plus lazy sections cannot keep Config.load under the hook latency budget, or if a drop-in directory makes provenance and merge conflicts worse than one file.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Two read-only research passes 2026-10-17 (web, installed dynaconf 3.3.5 in a scratch dir, measured import time and memory, source reading of @jinja/@format/hooks; internal code reading and timing). Not verified: dynaconf thread safety, systemd-analyze cat-config/cargo --show-origin details, direnv/mise hash details, pydantic-settings deep merge, dynaconf behaviour on Python 3.11, measurements are single-machine best-of-three. Operator decisions 2026-10-17 are in D-config-engine (full Jinja everywhere is the operator's choice against the research advice; knob [config].template_trust lets a user or org tighten it).
```

**Sources:** https://www.dynaconf.com/ ; https://github.com/dynaconf/dynaconf (CVE-2026-33154, @jinja) ; https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/ ; https://omegaconf.readthedocs.io/ ; systemd drop-ins (systemd.unit(5)) ; git config include/--show-origin ; direnv allow / mise trust

## How can ddflow integrate with spec-driven development tools (GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec, BMAD, Taskmaster) and with the native plan modes of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Windsurf, opencode, Cline, Kiro) over its own roadmap?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Feasible and worth building in this order: (1) import a Spec Kit / OpenSpec / Kiro tasks.md into ddflow phases and tasks through the existing `plan check` (dry run by default, imported text untrusted, ids namespaced, `[P]` only a hint because ddflow derives parallelism from disjoint globs and `needs`); (2) a read-only `tasks.md` export of a phase (region mode, checkbox state from ddflow); (3) a `plan export` slice (by label wave:N, phase or ready set) delivered as an MCP prompt and per-agent command files, plus `plan check` / `plan apply` for an accepted plan, with a Claude Code ExitPlanMode PermissionRequest hook that refuses a plan failing the checks; (4) ddflow as the executor behind `/implement` through an emitted command or extension. Execution always stays in ddflow's claim, gate and merge loop; native todo lists are only mirrors. Two-way sync is deferred (two sources of truth).
- **Mechanism.** Common denominator of all SDD tools: markdown on disk, checkbox tasks, no lease, no multi-agent claim, no gate, no event log; ddflow supplies exactly those. Plan modes are conversation states, not APIs: only Claude Code (ExitPlanMode hook, plansDirectory), Gemini CLI (plan.directory, policy engine) and Kiro (.kiro/specs/*/tasks.md) give an outside tool a documented handle; Cursor, Windsurf, Codex and Copilot keep the plan in home dirs or the conversation, so they get prompt text. Spec Kit tasks.md lines are `T001 [P] [US1] text path` with prose dependencies. ddflow already has plan check, import --verify, export, document types (B-dt-*), requirement records (PD-*), MCP prompts and adopt writers to reuse.
- **Falsifier.** Wrong if a tool's task file proves too irregular to parse safely, if `[P]` without file paths cannot be handled safely, or if clients do not render MCP prompts (then only files and commands carry the slice).

**Probe:**

```console
$ Two web research passes on 2026-10-16 (vendor docs, repos, secondary articles) plus read-only ddflow queue inspection; nothing was executed against the tools, hence THEORETICAL. Reports were written to scratch /tmp/claude-1001/research/sdd.md and plan-modes.md (not kept). Unverified: Spec Kit workflows, Kiro optional-task markers and licence, OpenSpec json flags and cadence, Tessl availability (closed beta per secondary sources; do not build against it), Codex official plan docs, Cursor plan save location (docs and forum disagree), Amp plan features, Cline headless, Copilot github.com plan gate, Claude Task store on disk, ACP plan update semantics, MCP prompt support outside Claude Code. Roo Code was archived 2026-05-15. Proposed phases: P-sdd (SDD-decide, probe, model, parse, import, export-tasks, rules-bridge, executor-ext, doctypes, trace, acceptance, eval) and P-plan-modes (PL-decide, probe, slice, prompts, apply, exit-hook, native-export, mirror, lane-plan, acp-plan, acceptance). OB-native-only already lists Kiro, Spec Kit and OpenSpec trees (D-ai-import made them managed), so P-sdd must align with it; `plan apply` and the add-time warning are still unbuilt (B-plan-apply-and-the-rest).
```

**Sources:** https://github.com/github/spec-kit ; https://github.github.com/spec-kit/ ; https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/ ; https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec ; https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes ; https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/plan-mode/ ; https://cursor.com/docs/agent/planning ; https://docs.cline.bot/core-workflows/plan-and-act ; https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/

- **Mechanism.** tests are all chains of run_cli subprocess calls; a call beyond its ceiling raises TimeoutExpired (reason hidden in the gate tail) and show_bug asserts elapsed time


## Does a persisted folded-State checkpoint beat folding the log on this 63.5k-event log, after the claim-window and renewal fast paths?

**Verdict: REFUTED** · item `B-gap-log-scale`

- **Claim.** Loading a pickled folded State is faster than folding the same events.
- **Mechanism.** A checkpoint replaces an O(N) fold with an O(N) load plus an O(tail) fold; it pays only when the load is cheaper than the fold.
- **Falsifier.** pickle.loads(State) takes about as long as fold(events), or longer.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3: st=fold(events,strict=False) 0.213 s; pickle.dumps(st,protocol=5) 0.225 s -> 31.96 MB; pickle.loads 0.213 s; repr(items) identical
fold 0.213 / loads 0.213 / 32 MB at 63.5k events (3.4 us per event folded)
```

## Where do status/next/brief time go on a 44.6 MB, 63.5k-event log, and which of coalesced renewals, out-of-line evidence and a flat claim copy buys most?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `B-gap-log-scale`

- **Claim.** Lease renewals (43% of events, 15% of bytes) and gate evidence (gate.passed+failed: 35% of events? no: 17% of events, 50% of bytes) dominate; the fold cost is dominated by dataclasses.asdict in records._claim, so a flat copy cuts status time by >=20% with a byte-identical fold.
- **Mechanism.** _claim runs asdict (deep copy) three times per lease.renewed during fold; renewals are 27.5k of 63.5k events. Coalescing renewals and moving evidence bodies out of the shards shrink parse and fold input.
- **Falsifier.** status time not reduced by the flat claim copy, or fold(repr items) differs from the asdict version on this repository's real log.

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 scripts/logbench.py --events .ddflow/events --repeat 2 (before): status 6.3s next 3.4s brief 7.1s heartbeat 3.3s session-start 11.5s; synth 60k events (29.8 MB): status 4.8s next 2.0s brief 19.0s heartbeat 2.7s session-start 20.0s. After asdict fix: status 5.35s next 2.92s on the real log; tests/test_log_scale.py compares repr(fold(...).items) with the asdict claim on the real log: identical. Renewal-gap simulation on the real log: W=120s keeps 19.1k of 27.5k renewals, W=300s 8.8k, W=600s 5.9k, W=900s 4.4k.
kind counts (bytes): gate.passed 8343 (11.2MB) gate.failed 2262 (11.0MB) lease.renewed 27512 (6.6MB) task.added 1989 (2.8MB) review.triaged 3831 (2.4MB). Fold-equivalence test passes (4 passed).
```

## How can an application project and its sister pipelines-and-infrastructure project coordinate, cooperate and be kept in sync by ddflow, and what does the planned constellation miss for that?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** The planned constellation covers the version pair, change request and drift ideas, but eleven specifics for infrastructure siblings (roles, environment contract adapters, artifact handoff, sibling proposals, deploy-aware matrix, plan impact, coordinated release, contract test, three-way drift, lifecycle, on-prem) are not planned.
- **Mechanism.** QUESTION: an application project and a sister project that holds the pipelines and infrastructure as code for it (cloud or on-prem): how do they coordinate so ddflow keeps both in sync? WHAT THE CONSTELLATION PLANS (P-constellation, D-constellation): a manifest of member projects with roles, spec records with format adapters (OpenAPI, protobuf, ASN.1, YANG, DBC, register maps), digest-pinned cross-project references, consumer edges and an impact query, change requests with a consumer state machine (pending, acknowledged, adopting, adopted, not_affected), baselines, a compatibility matrix with a can-i-release gate, a breaking-change gate classified by the adapter's checker, shared library registry (CN-libs) with a bump workflow that never edits another project's lockfile, a read-only sibling mirror, optional push nudge (CN-dispatch), a scheduled drift audit, topologies single repo, monorepo, polyrepo, submodule umbrella. THE WEB: a typical split is an app repo whose CI builds the image and a separate GitOps config repo that Argo CD or Flux watches (separate so the CD system does not trigger itself); promotion is a pull request that bumps an image tag or module version per environment (separate directories, branches, repos, or tag promotion); Flux image automation or Kargo promotion tasks do it automatically; versions follow semver with scope prefixes; the contract between the two is inputs and outputs of modules, Helm values and schema, manifests, environment variables, ports and health endpoints; a Pact-style can-i-deploy asks whether this version pair is verified together. WHAT FITS TODAY: infra and app can be two constellation members; CN-matrix and the can-i-release gate express version pairs; CN-cr carries change requests; ddflow promote and CN-libs bump workflows cover tags. GAPS: (1) no member roles for app, infra, gitops-config, module-library and pipeline-library, and no gitops-config topology; (2) no environment contract kind with adapters for Terraform variables and outputs, Helm values schema, Kubernetes manifests (kubeconform), config and environment-variable schemas, so what the app NEEDS from the infrastructure and what the infrastructure PROVIDES is not machine-checked; (3) no artifact handoff record (image digest, chart or module version, SBOM, provenance) that the infra project consumes by digest; (4) no way to open a proposal in the sibling repository through the forge with a change request attached; (5) the matrix is release-time, not deploy-aware: no rows per environment from deployment records and no can-i-deploy gate before an apply or promotion; (6) no plan-impact analysis: an infra plan diff that changes an output the app uses, or an app change that adds an environment variable, must raise a change request in the other project; (7) no coordinated release workflow (ordering, expand and contract, shared rollback, freeze windows); (8) no environment contract test against terraform output or rendered manifests; (9) no three-way drift audit (declared in the infra repo, deployed per deployment records and cloud reads, running version and health); (10) no lifecycle workflows for decommission, rename, secret rotation (references only) and deprecation notices; (11) no on-prem and air-gapped support (Ansible inventories, Packer images, offline registry and provider mirrors, hardware leases); (12) pipeline libraries (GitHub reusable workflows, GitLab includes, Jenkins shared libraries, Azure templates) are not versioned or pinned like code libraries.
- **Falsifier.** A read of CN-roles, CN-manifest, CN-matrix and CN-libs shows they already model environments, deployments or infrastructure contracts.

**Probe:**

```console
$ read CN-manifest, CN-matrix, CN-libs, CN-workflows, CN-dispatch, CN-adapter-* task bodies; ddflow promote --help; queue grep for environment, deployment, gitops, helm, contract
adapter groups: openapi, protobuf, asn1, yang/wsdl, embedded (dbc, arxml, ip-xact); no terraform, helm, kubernetes or env-schema adapter; matrix is spec@digest per release; no environment or deployment record; promote tracks branches only
```

**Sources:** https://semaphore.io/blog/how-to-integrate-ci-cd-with-gitops-tools-like-argo-cd-or-flux; https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-26-argocd-environment-promotion/view; https://mattias.engineer/blog/2023/gitops-environment-promotion/; https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/discussions/5667

## Can ddflow's current and planned features manage infrastructure-as-code, DevOps and DevSecOps projects and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps, and what is missing?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Command gates, per-project pipelines, reviewers, rules and promotion already carry the generic workflow; twelve specific gaps (IaC kind, plan-bound apply approval, cloud sandbox lifecycle, policy records, module kind, schema check, finding ingest, supply-chain verification, drift jobs, CI-platform and forge adapters, deployment records, compliance evidence) are not planned.
- **Mechanism.** QUESTION: can ddflow, with what exists and what is planned, manage projects whose product is infrastructure as code (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, CDK, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, Packer, Crossplane, Bicep, CloudFormation), DevOps and DevSecOps work, and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps? WHAT ALREADY WORKS TODAY: the gate pipeline is per-project data and any command can be a command gate (terraform fmt/validate/test, tflint, checkov, conftest, actionlint run as gates today); rules, decisions, lessons, goals engine (planned P-goals), leases and worktrees isolate agents, cross-family reviewers (Kimi, DeepSeek) review diffs, the codeguide and context7 companions serve standards and docs, ddflow promote tracks environment branches and recorded deploy shas, forge adapters (infra/forge.py) drive GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab for PR state, a ci gate runs the project's CI command set locally (D-ci-parity). Unavailable tools are recorded unavailable, never passed. WHAT IS PLANNED AND HELPS: SC-catalogue/SC-data-more (stack probe with an IaC data wave, data only), TF-flows-system pipeline-validate and TF-cadence (per-commit, per-PR, nightly, post-deploy sets), TD-emulation/TD-pins/TD-lease (containers, version pins and image digests, leases for scarce equipment), SE-ask-core approvals with content digests, SE-waiver, AG-deps-guard (dependencies agents add), P-safeguards (cards, consult action for context7/codeguide), P-schedule.watch, B-gap-checks-publish (gate state as a forge check), CP-intake (webhook intake), P-org-config (corporate policy layers), P-goals (measurable goals). THE WEB (2026): the IaC test pyramid is static (fmt, validate, tflint, checkov/trivy/tfsec/kics) about 70 percent, module-level plan and terraform test with mocks about 25 percent, apply-in-sandbox (Terratest) and nightly end-to-end about 5 percent; policy as code is OPA/Conftest or Sentinel run on the JSON plan (terraform show -json), first in warn mode then enforcing after two clean sprints; plan and apply are separated and the approved plan is what is applied (Atlantis, Spacelift, env0, HCP Terraform), with state locking and scheduled drift detection (plan -detailed-exitcode); modules are versioned by semver where removed variables, renamed outputs and changed resource types are breaking, published by git tag to a registry, documented by terraform-docs; HashiCorp ships a Terraform MCP server (registry search, provider docs, workspaces) and the TerraFormer paper (2026-01) and field reports show models hallucinate resource types and attributes, which a provider-schema check catches deterministically; DevSecOps means OIDC short-lived cloud credentials instead of static keys, SLSA provenance, Sigstore/cosign signatures, SBOMs, SARIF findings, secret scanning, and gates fast enough that nobody routes around them; pipelines are code with their own linters (actionlint, GitLab CI Lint API, the Jenkins declarative linter, Azure Pipelines validation, Gitea/Forgejo Actions on act_runner) and local runners (act, gitlab-ci-local). GAPS: (1) no first-class IaC stack kind with per-tool gate roles, tool and provider version pins and lock-file checks; (2) no plan record bound to commit, variables and workspace, so no 'apply only the plan that was approved' gate and no production-apply guard for agents; (3) no cloud sandbox lifecycle (TTL, guaranteed teardown, cost cap, orphan sweep, OIDC credentials) beyond local containers; (4) no policy-as-code record kind with enforce ramp and waivers with expiry mapped to executable bundles; (5) no module record kind (build, consume, semver by contract diff, registry provenance, lock hashes); (6) no provider-schema hallucination check and no registered Terraform MCP companion; (7) no SARIF/plan-JSON finding ingest with triage; (8) no provenance, signature and SBOM verification gate for images and modules; (9) no scheduled drift detection filing work; (10) forge support is GitHub and GitLab only (no Gitea/Forgejo, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) and there is no CI-platform adapter for detect, lint, local run, status and logs, nor pipeline generation from ddflow's own gates with drift check; (11) no deployment, environment and release record beyond branch promotion (artifact digest, rollback plan, freeze windows, change-ticket link, post-deploy gates); (12) no compliance evidence pack mapping controls to gates.
- **Falsifier.** A queue search finds planned tasks that already cover a listed gap, or a project of this kind cannot run its gates as command gates today.

**Probe:**

```console
$ queue grep for terraform, iac, pipeline, deploy, policy, drift, sandbox, gitea, azure, jenkins, sarif, sbom, slsa; read TF-flows-system, SC-data-more, TD-emulation, B-gap-checks-publish, CN-matrix, infra/forge.py; ddflow promote --help; ddflow companions
terraform/opentofu/pulumi/ansible/helm: 0 tasks; iac: SC-data-more (data only); gitea/azure devops/jenkins/bitbucket: 0; forge adapters: GitHub and GitLab only; promote: add/deployed/status by branch; sarif/slsa/sbom/cosign: 0 (AG-deps-guard covers app dependencies only)
```

**Sources:** https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-23-how-to-implement-infrastructure-as-code-testing-pyramid-with-terraform/view; https://kokil.com.np/blog/policy-as-code-with-opa-and-conftest; https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/06/10/codex-cli-terraform-infrastructure-as-code-mcp-server-terrashark-pulumi-agent-skills/; https://www.env0.com/frameworks/atlantis-for-terraform-how-it-works-limitations-better-alternatives; https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-01-30-terraform-module-versioning/view; https://cloudaware.com/blog/zero-trust-devsecops/

## Can B109-B112 and B13 be developed, extended by the planned work and merged without conflicts while keeping the original idea (a ddflow server that needs no client filesystem)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Yes: the storage seam, writer ratchet, lock strategy, merge strategy and locality split are one staged line that reuses P-remote.serve, the declared-command matrix and the org-config layer stack; B-mcp-http-transport duplicates P-remote.serve and must fold into it; B110 is mostly done already.
- **Mechanism.** ORIGINAL REQUEST (operator 2026-09-25, recorded in R14 and B109-B112): four parts: can a user ask what the workflow is and change it per project (answered: ddflow_workflow and friends); could the config live in a file the AGENT reads and writes on the server's behalf; could the other stores work the same way so the server needs no filesystem; and how is persistence implemented. THE IDEA: run the MCP server remotely or in a container without direct filesystem access. R14 REFUTED delegating file I/O to the agent over MCP (no primitive: roots/list is file:// URIs, sampling, elicitation; re-checked against the 2026-07-28 spec) and found that git, not storage, is the real coupling: concurrent-branch safety is merge=union on the event shards, flock is POSIX-only, gates run shell=True in a local worktree. The honest shape: a REMOTE-CAPABLE half (the queue as data) and a LOCAL-REQUIRED half (worktrees, merge, tree-fingerprint evidence, command gates). B109 storage seam (no abstraction exists), B110 scattered writers, B111 git coupling (THEORETICAL), B112 the split (build deliberately or not at all), plus B13 Windows (flock). WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE: (1) infra/fsio.py with atomic_write now exists and 12 modules use it, so B110's premise is mostly met (a search of its seven modules finds one raw write, gates/mutation.py); (2) D-remote (2026-10-12) chose an opt-in, stateless ddflow serve with state staying in the log, and P-remote.serve/auth/events/runs/ask implement the remote-capable half over the declared commands; (3) B-mcp-http-transport (operator 2026-09-29) asks for the same HTTP MCP server as P-remote.serve (TWO queue items for ONE server); (4) P-change-surface.split-log-records will turn infra/log.py (84 KB), core/records.py and infra/store.py into packages, so any seam must land after it or it is rewritten twice; (5) B-gap-log-scale moves gate evidence out of line (services/logblobs.py), a blob store that belongs behind the same seam; (6) P-knowledge-hub plans a reference hub whose storage is append-only with sequence (KB-hub) and a local SQLite mirror (KB-mirror), P-constellation a read-only sibling mirror, P-daemon a managed serve and hub mirror: each would otherwise invent its own storage; (7) P-core-records.matrix (running) builds a verb x kind x surface matrix, the natural home for a LOCALITY column (remote-capable or local-required); (8) P-org-config has a layer stack the client-held config of the original question can join as a session layer; (9) B13 now spans infra/fsio.py and services/flowstate.py as well as log.py and tomlcfg.py. COLLISIONS FOUND: B109 and B13 have identical globs; both and P-change-surface.split-log-records rewrite infra/log.py; B110 lists the whole services/gates/ directory against fix-gate-python-version (a lock clash, its real target is one file); B-mcp-http-transport and P-remote.serve both write surfaces/mcp.py or its serve replacement. MERGE PLAN: keep all four ideas and B13 as the real implementation items, re-scoped and ordered, and add a small phase P-storage with the decision, the writer ratchet, the locality tag, the merge-strategy interface, the client config overlay, and an acceptance with no filesystem on the client side.
- **Falsifier.** A probe shows the merge=union dependency cannot be expressed as a strategy interface, or serve cannot be the single writer without breaking worktree-bound commands, or the writer search finds many raw writes outside fsio.

**Probe:**

```console
$ docs/RESEARCH.md R14; grep raw writes in B110's seven modules; grep atomic_write users; grep fcntl/msvcrt; queue overlap of globs and duplicate HTTP transport (B-mcp-http-transport vs P-remote.serve)
raw writes: 1 (gates/mutation.py); atomic_write used by 12 modules via infra/fsio.py; fcntl in log.py, fsio.py, flowstate.py; two open items for one HTTP MCP server; split-log-records open
```

**Sources:** docs/RESEARCH.md R14; docs/BACKLOG.md B109-B112, B13; D-remote; https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28

## Read as one roadmap, are the open phases and tasks ordered, deduplicated, governed by decisions and free of gaps and contradictions?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** The graph is sound (no cycles or priority inversions) but the roadmap has hot-file glob collisions, 289 tasks without a specific governing decision, seven decision contradictions or stale rules, merge candidates among the decisions, 22 unphased tasks, and three missing capability areas.
- **Mechanism.** GRAPH: 909 open tasks in 78 phases, no cycles, no priority inversions, 0 dangling needs (needs on abandoned decide tasks are settled decisions). Depth 20 (CN-acceptance). 880 of ~890 non-running tasks are blocked behind two hubs, B-gap-log-scale (43 direct dependents) and B-gap-plan-lint (42); B-gap-log-scale needs the unphased B-log-snapshot-knobs. 355 needs edges are transitively redundant. 22 open tasks have no phase (B-semantic-recall, B-mcp-http-transport, fix-test-duration-*, ...) and cannot be moved until P-reshape.move exists. HOT FILES: README.md is listed by 63 open tasks (47 not docs tasks), ddflow/config.py by 58 (57 not), ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py by 56 (47 not), core/events.py 32, api/lifecycle 31; 93 percent of the pairs are unordered, so the conflict detector will serialise them at run time. D-readme-split, SE-globs and P-change-surface exist to fix this but the old phases still carry the coarse globs. DUPLICATES: the open-only near-duplicate pairs are template twins, not copies: the per-phase -docs (0.7-0.9), -surfaces (0.7), -eval and -acceptance tasks repeat one shape in 16 phases and each says 'table generated from the descriptors'; the P-change-surface.split-* tasks are mechanical twins. They share the declared-commands, docs-generation and SE-eval-harness engines; the risk is each phase writing its own table generator. DECISIONS: 164 records, 138 live, 23 superseded (chains sound), 3 proposed (D-B191-item-ids, D-gate-ratio-noise, D-old-work-behind-core-docs). 620 of 909 open tasks cite or inherit a specific decision; 289 do not (P-test-domains, P-docs-generic, P-subagents, P-agent-memory, P-observe, P-test-robustness, P-pipeline-ideas, P-agent-rules, P-resume, P-spawn, P-lessons, P-context-sync, P-reasoning, P-doc-templates and others) although same-named decisions exist for several (D-observe, D-subagents, D-perf, D-remote, D-agent-caps, D-agent-parity, D-agent-lifecycle, D-extension-seams, D-reasoning-log, D-session-context); P-spawn, P-resume, P-test-robustness, P-lessons, P-agent-hygiene, P-change-surface have no decision of their own. There is no structural task-to-decision link, only globs and prose. CONTRADICTIONS AND OVERLAPS: (1) D-subagents lets a declared other-family subagent count as a reviewer with no approval and says itself that it relaxes D-reviewer-trust; B-sub-trust is kept; the base rule was never amended. (2) D-upgrade-auto-check says auto=check never writes, D-upgrade-on-mcp-connect starts the upgrade on a version difference, D-self-upgrade-defaults applies safe categories at container start. (3) D-sched-no-daemon says no daemon; D-remote refines it; D-knowledge-hub adds an HTTP hub; the base text was not amended. (4) Ordering is spread over D-pause-after-upgrade, D-order-cleanup-then-upgrade-features, D-phase-order-gaps-first, D-phase-order-core-records-first, D-old-work-note-r1, D-schedule-early, D-perf-core-wave, all amending the still-PROPOSED D-old-work-behind-core-docs. (5) D-readme-current (every change updates the README) against D-readme-split (README is a front door): 63 tasks still name README.md. (6) D-push-after-acceptance still says nothing is pushed until P-unify acceptance passes although P-unify is done. (7) Agent authority is spread over D-stack-tools (agent accepts any tool role), D-decision-management, D-export-agent-enable, D-doc-types, D-product-docs-r3, D-safeguards, D-subagents, D-reviewer-trust, D-autopilot with no single matrix. MERGE CANDIDATES: the four export decisions; the upgrade family (about 12); the four enum-fallback decisions (D-enum-fallback-strict, D-fallback-no-remote, D6fc09b2590, D9b8061fd38); the three skills decisions; D-perf with D-no-duckdb; the MCP-surface decisions (D-lean-and-trusted, D-tools-list-budget-100k, D-mcp-output-schemas-off, D-viewer-lists-consolidated); D-quotas with D-governor. ENGINE OVERLAPS CHECKED AND SOUND: meters (B-quota-meters is the root; P-agent-parity.meters, P-governor.context-meter, PM-meters follow it), descriptors (P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2 is the root of 18), approvals (SE-ask-core), notifications (P-spawn.notify to CP-notify-sinks to CP-attention). MISSING EDGES: B-sub-trust and B-sched-escalation approve things but did not need SE-ask-core (added); B-dt-drafts (p10) also needs it but SE-ask-core is p26, a docs-wave versus shared-engines ordering question for the operator. WEB GAPS: A2A v1.0 (Linux Foundation, signed Agent Cards, 150+ organisations) has no task; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions (invoke_agent, chat, execute_tool spans; Codex and Claude Code export OTel) have two incidental mentions and no exporter; slopsquatting (4.6-21.7 percent fabricated package names; defences: allowlist or review gate, lockfile hashes, SBOM) has no gate for dependencies an agent adds to the project, nor licence or dependency-update intake.
- **Falsifier.** A fresh fold of the log shows cycles, priority inversions, or tasks whose globs are already narrow; or the operator rules a listed pair of decisions consistent.

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run python fold of .ddflow/events: needs graph, priorities, globs, decision globs and mentions; ddflow dupes --open-only --kind task; ddflow decision show on the pairs; queue grep for a2a, otel, sbom, slsa, licence

```

**Sources:** https://a2a-protocol.org; https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2026/genai-observability/; https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-slopsquatting-ai-supply-chain-20260419/

## Does every surviving mutant the sample listed now have a test that fails when its line is mutated?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `U4-weak-tests`

- **Claim.** Each of the 27 surviving mutants the 2026-10-10 sample listed corresponds to a behaviour no test observed, and a test written for it FAILS when that line is mutated (a harness applies one substitution at a time, runs the named test files, and restores).
- **Mechanism.** The sample named the LINES, not the behaviours: several had drifted (the file changed since 2026-10-10), so each candidate mutation was run against the existing tests first -- what survived is what needed a test. The tests then drive the smallest seam that reaches the line (a direct call, a monkeypatched collaborator, or one step of the rehearsal) and assert the OBSERVABLE difference the mutation makes.
- **Falsifier.** A mutation still passing after the test is written (the line is unobservable, so the finding is an equivalent mutant rather than a coverage gap), or a test failing on the UNMUTATED code (then it pins nothing and the kill is hollow).

**Probe:**

```console
$ python3 /tmp/mutate_u4.py <module> <test files> -- '<old>' '<new>' ... for each of the 27 sites, plus the whole-file baseline before each batch
27 mutants, each run against the named test files: all KILLED, with a green baseline in each batch (cliexec 6 passed; context_pack 15; identity 64; cmdrunner 49; upgrade_apply 72; upgrade_dry_run 51; config_writes+writer 31; search_core 14). Two hollow kills were caught and fixed rather than accepted: three dryrun tests failed on unmutated code (a GitResult where P.Captured was expected, and a monkeypatched method missing self), and one failure was a race with a still-running harness holding a mutated file. Two findings for the record: the depth line's 'default=0' is an EQUIVALENT mutation (the default is only used when there are no sources), and the sample's ":304 spawn OSError" needed start() patched at P.spawn_shell, since run() spawns with P.run_shell.
```

## What can Codex (subagents, app-server, exec, mcp-server), OpenAI Symphony and OpenAI Frontier teach ddflow, and what must ddflow add to drive and use them?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** The queue has no task for the gaps below; most of the surface is already planned (ACP, spawn, caps, governor, platform MCP, control planes); the real gaps are a Codex app-server lane backend with dynamic tools, native subagent definition sync and native cap mapping, a table fan-out run, a Symphony-style tracker contract, a work receipt, a human-review capacity cap, a per-worktree bootstrap, and an agent roster with scorecards.
- **Mechanism.** CODEX: subagents are TOML files in [REDACTED:path] or .codex/agents (name, description, developer_instructions; optional model, reasoning effort/summary, verbosity); built-ins default, worker, explorer; limits agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session (default 6), max_depth (default 1); subagents inherit the parent sandbox and approvals and cannot override them; results are consolidated by the parent; /subagents switches threads; spawn_agents_on_csv fans one worker out per CSV row; codex exec --json streams events headlessly; codex mcp-server exposes codex and codex-reply; the app-server is a JSON-RPC headless mode. SYMPHONY (OpenAI, 2026-04-28, Apache-2.0): a tracker board (Linear) as control plane over the Codex app-server; one isolated workspace per ticket, restarts crashed runs, posts proof of work (CI status, PR feedback, complexity) back to the ticket; dynamic tool calls instead of MCP so no token enters the container; a SPEC reimplemented per language. FRONTIER (2026-02-05): an enterprise platform to build, deploy and manage agents: shared business context, an execution environment, evaluation and optimization, agent identity with scoped permissions and governance; open to agents built elsewhere. PITFALLS named by practitioners: token cost grows with every agent, human review is the bottleneck (3-5 agents is the sweet spot), isolation does not give dependency alignment, depth above 1 explodes cost. ALREADY PLANNED IN DDFLOW (reused, not redone): P-acp (client, wrap, thin agent, permissions, steering, resume), P-spawn (route, steer, notify, tree, context), P-agent-caps (group caps, slots), P-governor (tiers, step cost, regret), P-platform-mcp (PM-codex-mcp, search-and-call facade), P-control-planes (intake, exporters, notify sinks, env ports), P-safeguards (envelopes, dispatch brief), P-knowledge-hub (shared context), P-observe (feedback proposals). GAPS: no Codex app-server backend or dynamic-tool door; no sync of ddflow subagent definitions with .codex/agents TOML and no mapping of ddflow caps onto Codex's own thread and depth limits; no table fan-out run; no tracker contract Symphony could drive; no work receipt posted to the ticket; review capacity is capped only for autopilot proposals; no per-worktree dependency bootstrap; no agent roster with identity, scopes and scorecards.

- **Falsifier.** A probe of the installed Codex shows the app-server lacks thread/turn/approval methods or dynamic tools, or the .codex/agents TOML cannot carry what the sync needs; then FL-codex-appserver and FL-subagent-sync shrink to the exec and MCP routes.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow list task --limit 3000 | grep -iE 'app-server|dynamic tool|fan-out|csv|symphony|proof of work|review capacity|roster|scorecard|worktree.*setup'
only AC-prefer names the codex app-server (a knob, no backend), AP-budget caps review for autopilot proposals only, CP-env-ports covers ports not dependencies, CP-intake/CP-exporters cover Linear in/out but no tracker contract; no task matches dynamic tool, fan-out, csv, roster or scorecard
```

**Sources:** https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents; https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/codex-multi-agent-orchestration; https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-frontier/; https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/28/openai-symphony-codex-orchestration-linear/; https://www.noqta.tn/en/news/openai-symphony-codex-autonomous-orchestrator-linear-2026

## Why do abandoned, removed and merged-from-inside items leave their worktree and branch behind?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B79319c6ada`

- **Claim.** merge disposes through dispose_tree (tree plus branch -d); abandon and remove only record the event; merge keeps the tree it ran from and nothing retries
- **Mechanism.** api/lifecycle/complete.abandon and remove never call dispose_tree; merge._dispose_tree refuses when the caller stands in the tree, and complete and brief never retry
- **Falsifier.** An abandoned item with a clean tree still has its tree and branch afterwards; a done item's kept tree survives a later complete or brief

**Probe:**

```console
$ tests/test_abandon_worktree.py tests/test_finished_tree_sweep.py
all 14 fail on the unfixed code, pass after
```

## Why does doctor list every finished item whose worktree is gone as an orphan_worktree?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B999669a8df`

- **Claim.** scan reports any item with no lease and a recorded worktree except REVIEW; finishing never clears item.worktree
- **Mechanism.** leases.scan elif not lease and it.worktree and it.state != REVIEW
- **Falsifier.** A done or abandoned item whose tree was removed still yields a recovery record

**Probe:**

```console
$ tests/test_recover_finished_items.py
2 of 4 failed before the fix with 'worktree is gone; nothing to salvage' for T1 and T2; pass after
```

## Why does version cut --changelog fail to commit under generated_views=block?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Ba41e4bb639`

- **Claim.** The cut renders the changelog with the new tag present but removes the tag before the commit; the pre-commit check regenerates the staged document with ddflow export, which places entries by tags, and gets a different file
- **Mechanism.** changelog_cut.prepare creates a temporary tag around rendering only; commit_on runs after it is gone
- **Falsifier.** A cut --changelog under [enforce].generated_views=block with the hook installed still commits

**Probe:**

```console
$ tests/test_export_version_cut.py::test_cut_with_changelog_commits_under_a_blocking_generated_views_policy
FAILED before: 1 staged exported document(s) differ ... CHANGELOG.md (stale: the log moved since it was exported); passes after
```

## Is the `[docs]` config section complete and consistent with the decision and the repo's config rules?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `B-docs-config`

- **Claim.** The `[docs]` section is complete for D-docs-stage: eight knobs with the quiet defaults (warn, local, empty), declared once on their dataclass fields, re-exported through `ddflow.config`, rendered by `config --explain`, and reusing `[enforce]`'s document scope instead of copying it. A typo in a config file cannot make the check less careful, and a malformed extractor table cannot load silently.
- **Mechanism.** `knob()`/`declare()` register each field in KNOB_DOCS/DECLARED; `ddflow.config` assembles `Config` from the section dataclasses and builds the choices/strictest/outward tables from those declarations, so an enum knob must answer the strictest and outward questions by construction. `Config.load` applies D-enum-fallback-strict to a FILE value it does not know, and runs a `check=` function for the rest. `docscheck.check_docs` already takes doc_globs/doc_exclude/ignore_paths/ignore_names/commands defaults, which is what `check_paths` empty means.
- **Falsifier.** A knob absent from `config --explain`; a bad file value that leaves the check LESS careful than before; `check_paths` carrying a second copy of the doc globs; or a malformed `[[docs.extract]]` loading without complaint (an extractor that cannot fire reads like a clean run).

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run pytest tests/test_docs_config.py -q; then the config family (test_config_layout, test_config_knobs_declared, test_config_enum_knobs, test_config_forward_compat, test_config_newer_than_code, test_compat_config, test_plain_config_keys, test_adaptive_config) plus tests/golden/test_golden_outputs.py; plus `Config().explain()` filtered to docs.*
tests/test_docs_config.py: 15 passed (defaults, explain listing, re-export, the reused triple, the link modes, the extract kinds, not-outward, the strictest fallback for both enum knobs, the reused [enforce] scope, four malformed extract tables refused, one valid table round-tripped). The config family + the config --explain golden: 262 passed (1 snapshot regenerated for the new section). explain() lists docs.severity, docs.check_links, docs.check_paths, docs.lint_command, docs.cli_command, docs.ignore_paths, docs.ignore_names, docs.extract.
```

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B72b73360bc`

- **Claim.** Yes: UM.lint compares the in-memory knob registry with the manifest read fresh from disk, so a long-lived process lacks knobs added since it started
- **Mechanism.** knob_defaults() reads the imported Config classes; replay(load()) reads files
- **Falsifier.** A stale in-memory registry (a knob removed from knob_defaults, process start before every source file) still lints clean

## Can 0.2.2 be cut locally from main without pushing, and does it need upgrade-manifest entries?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `release-0-2-2`

- **Claim.** 0.2.2 can be cut locally from main with no manifest entries needed: the upgrade-manifest lint is clean in a fresh process (0 unmanifested), the cut tags main without pushing, and the changelog is a generated view rendered from the log and the tags, so it must be regenerated AFTER the tag to carry the version's own section.
- **Mechanism.** `version_cut` and `version lint` run the same `_lint_outcome`/`UM.lint()`: it compares the manifest replay with `knob_defaults()` of the RUNNING process. A long-lived MCP server therefore sees the knobs it imported with; a fresh CLI process sees the current tree. The tag is `git tag` on the base branch (no commit to merge), and `export changelog` uses the version tags to decide which section a change lands in.
- **Falsifier.** A FRESH process reporting unmanifested changes (then entries or waivers would be needed), or the cut pushing, or the changelog rendering without a [0.2.2] section once the tag exists.

**Probe:**

```console
$ `ddflow version lint` (fresh CLI); `ddflow version cut --version 0.2.2 --changelog --dry-run`; then the real `version cut --version 0.2.2` and `ddflow export changelog --update`
Fresh CLI: "release manifest lint (block): 0 unmanifested, 0 waived". Dry run: "would write CHANGELOG.md (whole) / nothing written / v0.2.2 (dry run)". Real cut: "tagged 2e3c2ba8d60e as v0.2.2". After the tag, `export changelog --update` rendered "## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-14" with the fixes/added/changed sections. Nothing pushed: `main...origin/main [ahead 252]`. The SAME lint over MCP refused with 11 phantom knob_removed changes -- filed as B72b73360bc.
```

## What does GitHub Copilot's 'Optimize for' (Efficiency, Balance, Intelligence) do, what do other agents do for automatic model and effort selection, what are the best practices, and how should the planned ddflow governor change?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Copilot's three settings share one model pool and only change how Auto prefers models; Auto switches only at natural cache boundaries (the first turn and after compaction), which is why a mid-session change warns about the prompt-cache reset. Each model has its own cache (cache reads about 0.1x input, writes 1.25x to 2x), so a model switch pays a full uncached re-read; a top-level effort change can also reset the cache, per-message effort and an advisor model do not. Routing evidence for agents is thin and recent (SWE-Router, Agent-as-a-Router, Triage): trajectory-based routing beat prompt-only routing by about 15 points; single-shot results (RouteLLM, FrugalGPT) should not be assumed to transfer to long loops. So ddflow should add: switching only at safe points with an estimated switch cost, a per-agent routing capability table, an optimize_for preset compiled into the existing ladder knobs, role and stage routing (planner, implementer, reviewer, triage), cascade-with-escalation on ddflow's own signals (gate failures, loops, reviewer rejection, context ladder), guardrails presets cannot lower, step-cost events that record the model that actually ran, a regret and yield report with a per-tier break-even, and replay and A/B evaluation.
- **Mechanism.** The governor's decision function and ladders stay; a preset layer compiles to knobs; a capability table (extending the descriptor facts and ACP session config options) says which door switches model or effort and whether it preserves the cache; the escalation policy consumes gate, loop and review signals and emits requests applied at safe points; step-cost events feed the spend ledger and the regret report; replay of the event log scores policies.
- **Falsifier.** If a seeded replay shows the preset or escalation policy lowering a reviewer below its floor, switching mid-lane without a cost estimate, oscillating between tiers, or costing more per merged task than always-balanced, the design is wrong.

**Sources:** https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-14-configure-cost-and-quality-in-copilot-auto-model-selection, https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/getting-more-from-each-token-how-copilot-improves-context-handling-and-model-routing/, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00053 (SWE-Router), https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-config-options, https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/acp-server; the exact notice string, effort effects and VS Code setting keys are unverified

## Does it make sense for ddflow to implement ACP (Agent Client Protocol) to communicate with and control coding agents, and in which roles?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes as an ACP CLIENT (a lane driver): one driver for about 20 agents, ACP v1 is stable (schema tag v1.25.0, 2026-10-09), session/new carries cwd and mcpServers so the ddflow MCP server is injected natively, session/update gives structured events, session/request_permission and session/cancel give control, and a registry lists 41 agents with launch commands. Second as a WRAP proxy (ddflow acp --wrap) that rewrites session/new, built on the client's plumbing. Not as an ACP agent (editors want a model-driven agent; ddflow is a queue). Not on remote HTTP/WebSocket yet (an RFD). ACP has no hooks, so gate enforcement stays in per-agent hooks and MCP, and the Stop-hook substitute is a controller loop that re-prompts after end_turn; steering is non-standard; native APIs beat ACP for claude (SDK and -p), codex (app-server) and opencode (serve), so ACP is the generic backend beside native ones; tmux stays the fallback for agents with no ACP. v2 is a draft that removes fs and terminal methods and session/load, so the client advertises no fs or terminal and isolates turn completion.
- **Mechanism.** An ACP transport (NDJSON JSON-RPC peer over a pluggable byte stream), a v1 client, a registry reader feeding the harness descriptors, an update-to-event mapper, a permission broker on the approvals engine and the capability envelope, a continuation loop reusing the continuation engine, and an acp backend in the lane-backend interface; the wrap proxy is a thin consumer.
- **Falsifier.** If a fake ACP agent makes the broker allow a write outside the worktree, a crash or stdout garbage leaves a lease held or a zombie adapter, a cancel during a permission request wedges the lane, or the wrapped agent fails the ACP conformance kit, the design is wrong.

**Sources:** https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/overview and /protocol/v1/*, https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json (41 agents), https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/{claude-agent-acp, codex-acp, acp-tck, python-sdk}, https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/proxy-chains.md, https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/streamable-http-websocket-transport.md, https://opencode.ai/docs/acp/, https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/acp-server, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server; Paseo and Harness Remote ACP claims unverified

## Should ddflow probe a project's stack and propose per-stack developer-assurance tools (linters, types, contracts and provers like Creusot, LSP and AST servers, security and mutation tools, rule and style servers like codeguide) as companions, decided by the agent and the operator, and also use them in the research, test and other workflows?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes: a deterministic probe (manifests, existing tool configs, CI commands, language mix; no network, no install) feeding a data-driven catalogue of tools per stack and role, an optional agent-plus-internet step for tools beyond the catalogue (trust=agent, verified false, cited, operator accepts), and accept or decline recorded as events (declined means the gate records unavailable). Order of value: linters already configured in the repo, dependency and licence checks, type checkers, faster test runners, LSP MCP servers (advisory), shell/Docker/IaC linters, then Kani or CBMC, property-based tests, mutation on changed code, ast-grep or Opengrep rules; deductive provers (Creusot 0.14, pre-1.0, needs opam; Verus, Dafny, SPARK) are opt-in verifiers named by a workflow, not default gates. Main risks: the agent weakens specs or adds trusted/assume/suppression escapes to turn a tool green, installs are supply-chain events, tool descriptions of new MCP servers can poison, and licences (Serena GPL-3.0 core: run as a separate process).
- **Mechanism.** One companion catalogue (extending the existing companions registry) with roles mapped to gates and to workflow verifier slots; the stack probe shares its detector with decision inference at onboarding; suppression and config-edit counters guard the gates; ddflow prints install commands and never runs them; MCP tool descriptions are hashed at accept time.
- **Falsifier.** If a fixture lets an agent pass a gate by adding a suppression, weakening a tool config or marking a proof trusted without review noticing, installs a tool without an accepted proposal, or accepts a poisoned MCP tool description, the guards are wrong.

**Sources:** https://creusot.rs/ (v0.14.0, Rust deductive verifier via Why3, LGPL-2.1, needs opam), https://model-checking.github.io/kani/, https://github.com/oraios/serena (GPL-3.0 core), https://github.com/isaacphi/mcp-language-server, https://github.com/github-linguist/linguist, https://megalinter.io, https://github.com/aws/aws-doc-sdk-examples (none); the per-tool rows for Go, Java, C/C++, Solidity are unverified in the report, and the reward-hacking and token-saving claims come from blogs and snippets

## Is the new Kilo MCP server (a hosted MCP for the Kilo platform API) worth supporting in ddflow, and do other agents have similar platform APIs or hosted MCP servers worth adding to the agent support?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Yes, as an opt-in, guarded capability. The Kilo MCP exposes two tools, search over an API catalog and call with error feedback naming missing fields, covering usage and spend by feature, day and month, agent profiles and variables (create, update, delete) and the cloud agent lifecycle (start, status, send, interrupt, delete), authenticated as the user. For ddflow that is (1) a lane backend for cloud agents, (2) a usage and spend meter source for the governor and spend ledger, (3) a profile store to sync with the canonical subagent and skill store, and (4) a design pattern: a large surface behind two tools, search and call, which is a way to keep ddflow's own MCP tool list small. Similar surfaces exist for Devin (mcp.devin.ai: sessions, playbooks, knowledge, schedules), GitHub (create_pull_request_with_copilot in the GitHub MCP server), Jules (REST alpha with requirePlanApproval), Codex (codex mcp-server with codex and codex-reply), Cursor (Cloud Agents API) and Claude Code (Remote Control). Risk: these act as the authenticated user and can delete agents and spend money, so they sit behind a tool allowlist and approvals, tokens never in the repo, and returned text is fenced data.
- **Mechanism.** A [platform] section in the harness descriptor (kind mcp, rest or cli; url; auth method; org header; capabilities; tool allowlist; verified flag), consumed by the lane-backend interface (CP-backend-iface), the meters (P-agent-parity.meters, spend ledger), the profile sync (B-sub-sync) and the MCP guard (B-sub-mcp-guard); ddflow's own search-and-call facade is measured by the MCP budget reporter.
- **Falsifier.** If a fake platform server lets an agent delete a profile or start a billable cloud agent without an approval, leaks a token into the repo or the log, or obeys an instruction in returned text, the guard is wrong.

**Sources:** https://blog.kilo.ai/p/mcp (Kilo MCP: remote server https://mcp.kiloapps.io/mcp, kilo mcp auth kilo, tools search and call), https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-mcp.md (mcp.devin.ai, X-Org-Id), https://developers.google.com/jules/api/reference/rest (alpha), https://github.blog/changelog/2025-07-09-delegate-tasks-to-copilot-coding-agent-from-the-github-mcp-server/, https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/03/30/codex-cli-as-mcp-server/ (secondary), https://cursor.com/docs/background-agent/api/overview; seen as search snippets except the Kilo post

## When ddflow is introduced into a project with an existing AI workflow (instructions, rules, skills, subagents, commands, hooks, MCP configs, permissions, memory and steering files), how can it import, dedupe, convert and then manage them for every supported coding agent so operation afterwards is smooth?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Harnesses read each other's files (VS Code reads .claude/agents, Cursor reads .claude/skills, opencode falls back to CLAUDE.md, Claude reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md), so duplicates are often double-loaded and dedupe needs a who-loads-what graph; conflict handling differs (Claude concatenates, VS Code has no defined order, Roo replaces a mode by slug), so contradictions must be flagged and never auto-resolved; formats churn (Codex prompts, Windsurf under Devin Desktop, Kilo config, Gemini CLI replaced in part by Antigravity), so adapters need version stamps; imports carry hidden-Unicode, secret and permission-widening hazards and size caps (Codex 32 KiB, Windsurf 12,000 characters). So: read-only scan and inventory first, AGENTS.md as the canonical always-on file with pointers instead of copies, digest manifests and managed markers with drift checks, backup and revert, plan/apply as a queue item, glob rules and skills before subagents and commands, and permissions, hooks and MCP secrets native-only until the operator accepts.
- **Mechanism.** A data-driven adapter table per agent (glob, class, scope, loader semantics, also-reads, caps, version) drives scan, classify, dedupe and emit; canonical records are data-declared kinds with trust=imported; emit uses managed regions and a digest manifest (extending the install manifest of P-agent-lifecycle); drift and round-trip use a three-way compare against the last emitted content; everything is a plan applied through the normal queue with gates.
- **Falsifier.** If a seeded fixture with the same rule in five files, a contradiction, hidden Unicode, a secret and a permission-widening skill passes onboarding without a flag, or an apply cannot be reverted, or a native edit after emit is overwritten, the design fails.

**Sources:** https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://agents.md, https://agentskills.io, https://github.com/intellectronica/ruler, https://github.com/dyoshikawa/rulesync, https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-instructions, https://docs.cursor.com/context/rules; per-agent paths for Cursor commands, Cline workflows, Windsurf workflows, Zed, Junie, Amp, Goose, Continue config, Kilo modes, Qwen, Kimi, GLM unverified in the report

## How should ddflow manage collaboration between sister projects that share libraries, API specifications, test specifications, requirements, user stories, specifications and ICDs, and onboard a project that already has them?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** The proven shape is a registry of immutable, owned, versioned specs with consumer edges and a compatibility matrix (Pact can-i-deploy over provider/consumer/environment results; Confluent and Apicurio per-subject compatibility; Backstage ownership and lifecycle), with breaking-change classification by a format-specific checker (oasdiff, buf breaking, Avro modes, YANG revision rules) and identity by a canonical model digest next to the byte digest. ddflow needs a constellation manifest, a spec record kind with format adapters, digest-pinned cross-project references, consumer edges and an impact query, a breaking-change gate, a compatibility matrix with a can-i-release gate, change requests with per-consumer state, baselines with human approval (ICD), a read-only sibling mirror, a spec onboarding workflow and a drift audit with injection scanning; events reference sibling events by digest, never embed them.
- **Mechanism.** Specs, stakeholders, libraries, change requests and baselines are data-declared record kinds (SE-kind-data); adapters are registry entries; workflows are templates in a pack (SE-workflow-template, SE-packs); matrix and gate reuse test results with SUT pins (TF-record, TD-pins); baselines reuse the requirement baseline engine (PD-baseline); approvals and waivers use SE-ask-core and SE-waiver; the sibling mirror reuses the org git fetcher and the hub mirror.
- **Falsifier.** If a seeded two-project fixture lets a breaking OpenAPI, protobuf or ASN.1 change reach a consumer without a change request, accepts a non-owner spec edit, obeys an instruction hidden in spec text, or releases against a stale mirror, the design fails.

**Sources:** https://docs.pact.io (can-i-deploy matrix), https://github.com/oasdiff/oasdiff, https://buf.build/docs/breaking/overview, https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/schema-registry/fundamentals/schema-evolution.html, https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/specification/ (parsing canonical form), https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8407.html (YANG revision rules), https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/, https://www.apicur.io/registry/, https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/; ASN.1, DBC, IP-XACT, ICD and change-board practice mostly snippets or unverified in the report

## Does raising the tools/list budget to 100,000 leave the list inside it, and does anything else pin the number?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `mcp-tools-budget-100k`

- **Claim.** Raising TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET to 100,000 leaves the MCP tools/list inside it with real headroom (the list measures 97,394), and changes nothing else -- the check still fails past the new number.
- **Mechanism.** `TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET` is read by two tests: test_mcp_tool_budget measures the compact tools/list against it, and test_mcp_tool_tiers imports it for the full-list ratchet. No other file pins the number, so raising it only moves the ceiling.
- **Falsifier.** The measured list exceeding 100,000 (then the raise is already too small), or the budget test/tiers ratchet failing for any other reason, or the constant being pinned by a second copy somewhere.
