## How can rules and principles define a project's pipeline (extra gates, allowed skips, order), resolved per item and modified by agents within floors, reusing the guidance, waiver, config and workflow engines?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Pipeline requirements need no new store: ONE optional field `pipeline` on the existing guidance record (rule or decision, def.* events, record surface) names an effect on the effective pipeline of every item the record's Scope covers: require=[gate...] (additive, with optional after=), allow_na=[gate...] with a reason class, forbid_skip=[gate...], order=[[a,b]...], and kinds=[...] to restrict by item kind. Project-specific gates stay in [gate.<id>] (command gates are executable, so approved by digest, B-gap-command-trust). Strength reuses the P-goals pair enforcement x override: MUST (block, waive|none) = the gate cannot be dropped, skipped or made N/A; only a person's approved waiver (<=90 days, scoped) lifts it. SHOULD (warn, deviate) = the gate is added as recommended; an agent may record an item-scoped deviation with a reason, answered before complete. MAY = shown only. Resolution is a pure function effective_pipeline(cfg, item, records, diff_paths) -> gates each tagged with its source (base:kind, rule:id, principle:id, org:id) and N/A/deviations; resolved at claim and recorded as a pipeline.resolved event (digest of inputs), re-resolved at gate status/complete on the ACTUAL diff, additions only mid-flight. Agent changes are additive by default (add a gate to one item); any weakening (remove, demote, N/A of a MUST/required gate, change of a floor) is a proposal a person approves. Precedence = P-goals order (org floor > project MUST > accepted decision > principle > preference); additions collect (union), removals use the strictest-wins rule (a MUST require beats any allow_na), an order cycle is a doctor error that falls back to base order.
- **Mechanism.** A requirement is a guidance record effect, so lifecycle, scope matching, waivers, deviations, search and RAG come from the record surface; the pipeline stays one selector (pipeline_for) extended with recorded per-item additions.
- **Falsifier.** Falsified if, after B-pipe-acceptance, a project cannot express 'ddflow/core/** needs mutation_tests' and 'docs-only skips unit_tests' with the field alone, or if agents' additive changes exceed [pipeline].max_added on more than 10 percent of items, or if resolve differs between claim and complete for an unchanged rule set, or if any weakening applies without a person.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebFetch of the survey pages plus reading services/gates, completion, guidance, configwrite; probes in R-pipeline-configurable-today
Survey, fetched and read 2026-10-11 (WebFetch returns a model summary, quotes approximate) VERIFIED: GitHub rulesets layer, most restrictive wins, bypass list, org-level rulesets (docs.github.com .../about-rulesets); the available-rules page lists 'require status checks' and NO dedicated require-workflows rule, and docs .../required-workflows is 404 (so the removal of required workflows is NOT verified). Gerrit submit requirements: applicableIf / submittableIf / overrideIf expressions, children inherit and override only if parent sets canOverrideInChildProjects, override replaces the whole requirement, remove by is:false (gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-submit-requirements.html). GitLab pipeline execution policies: inject_policy adds to the project pipeline, override_project_ci replaces it, [skip ci] cannot bypass by default, scope by project/group/compliance framework (docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/application_security/policies/pipeline_execution_policies.html). Conftest: deny/violation/warn rules in Rego over CI pipeline definitions (conftest.dev; exception semantics not on the page). Kyverno: mutate runs before validate, chained rules need ordering (kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/cluster-policy/mutate/; PolicyException not covered by the page). Backstage golden paths: templates encode steps and let teams change inputs, rerun with edits (backstage.io/docs/features/software-templates/). Jenkins shared libraries: global trusted vs folder untrusted, @version pinning, 'allow default version to be overridden' (jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/shared-libraries/). Airflow dynamic task mapping: tasks created at runtime, visible in Grid view, max_map_length 1024 cap, zero inputs -> SKIPPED (airflow docs). LangGraph conditional edges / Send / Command route at runtime (docs.langchain.com .../graph-api). Tekton: runAfter, when expressions, skipped tasks listed in PipelineRun status, finally tasks (tekton.dev/docs/pipelines/pipelines/). Claude Code hooks: PreToolUse/TaskCompleted/ConfigChange exit 2 blocks, managed-policy hooks cannot be disabled by users, allowManagedHooksOnly (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Jira: workflows assigned to projects and work types by workflow schemes, active workflows cannot be renamed, copy-modify-activate (support.atlassian.com work-with-issue-workflows). INHERITED from R-goals-principles-proposals-design (fetched by the earlier author, not re-fetched here): Kiro steering/hooks, Gatekeeper enforcementAction dryrun/warn/deny, Kyverno Audit vs Enforce, RFC 2119, Spec Kit Complexity Tracking, ArchUnit FreezingArchRule. NOT VERIFIED (summarised from background): DMN hit policies (OMG PDF unreadable, Camunda page lacked the list), BPMN, Argo Workflows, Temporal, Linear workflows, GitHub required workflows.
COPY: Gerrit's applicable/submittable/override split and per-requirement inherit-with-explicit-override-permission (canOverrideInChildProjects = ddflow override none vs waive vs deviate); GitLab inject (additive) vs override (replace) as two distinct, named strategies with additive default; GitHub's most-restrictive-wins and evaluate/disabled states (a dry-run enforcement tier); Tekton skipped-with-reason listing and Airflow SKIPPED on empty; Jenkins version pinning of shared definitions; Claude Code managed hooks that users add to but cannot remove. AVOID: pipeline sprawl (Airflow needed a max_map_length cap; cap added gates per item), agents weakening their own gates (Jenkins trusted vs untrusted: the writer of the policy must not be the subject), undebuggable dynamic graphs (LangGraph/Airflow: freeze the resolved graph and show the source of each node), silent drift (a rule edit changing in-flight items: record pipeline.resolved with input digests), full-replace overrides (Gerrit/GitLab override_project_ci hide what was lost: diff against base).
```

## What can a project, an operator and an agent change about the gate pipeline today, and which of the four invariants is a real floor?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Today a project can shape its pipeline only through config: [gates].task_pipeline/phase_pipeline/promotion_pipeline/kind_pipelines (whole ordered lists per kind), [gate.<id>] definitions (command|prompt, reviewer, requires_evidence, applies_when on the item's DECLARED globs, needs_branch; required lives in [gates].required), and ddflow workflow pipeline|gate|drop (CLI and MCP, validated, dry-run; 'ask the operator' only in tool text). Nothing per glob/category/tag/rule: no rule, decision or principle influences the pipeline (guidance Scope.gates only selects which text is injected at a gate prompt). pipeline_for(item,cfg) is a pure function of (cfg, item.kind, promote_to); not_applicable is derived at read time from declared globs, not recorded. The four invariants are NOT a floor: unavailable-never-passed is structural (runner/outcomes), but require_outcome, agent.reviewer_family_must_differ, lessons.require_regression_test, gates.required and allow_skip_with_reason are plain knobs any writer (an agent over CLI or ddflow_configure) can flip with no approval; only gate.<id>.human and agent-written command reviewers are guarded (configwrite). Bug B-na-required-gate: a required gate becomes not-applicable by agent-editable declared globs.
- **Mechanism.** pipeline_for is the single selector (kind -> list); applies_when narrows per item from declared globs; completion.verdict reads status() so a not-applicable required gate is settled; invariants are knobs in config_sections/gates.py, agent.py, lessons.py with no policy tier until B-org-agent-guard.
- **Falsifier.** Refuted if a config write of gates.require_outcome=false were refused for an agent, or if a required gate stayed owed when applies_when misses.

**Probe:**

```console
$ see probe_output
Throwaway repo in scratchpad/probe: (1) [gate.unit_tests] applies_when=["src/**"], task globs docs/x.md: gate status printed "[-] unit_tests -- not applicable: applies only to work touching src/**; T1 declares docs/x.md"; ddflow update T1 --globs src/**,docs/x.md brought it back, --globs docs/x.md dropped it again (no approval). (2) ddflow config gates.require_outcome false / agent.reviewer_family_must_differ false / lessons.require_regression_test false / gates.allow_skip_with_reason false / gates.required [] all accepted and written ([file]). (3) ddflow workflow pipeline task implement,merge --dry-run and workflow drop unit_tests --dry-run accepted. Read: services/gates/{kinds,defs,outcomes}.py, services/completion.py:140-170 (missing excludes not_applicable), configwrite.py guards, surfaces/declared/hooks.py.
```

**Sources:** ddflow/services/gates/kinds.py, ddflow/services/gates/defs.py, ddflow/services/completion.py, ddflow/services/configwrite.py

## How should goals, defeasible principles, strict rules and periodic feature proposals be modelled in ddflow, reusing the guidance, waiver, record, schedule and research engines, given what comparable tools do?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Goals, principles and proposals need no parallel store: goals and proposals are two new definition-record kinds on the existing def.* model and record surface; a principle is a guidance record (rule or decision) whose override mode is deviate (an agent-recorded reason, item-scoped, counted) instead of waive (operator-approved, 90 days); strict rules stay enforcement=block with waive or none. Periodic discovery is a schedule job that files ONE research item whose output is at most K proposals, with backpressure (open-proposal cap), dedupe against the board and against rejected proposals, and an operator-only adopt/defer/reject that records the reason. THEORETICAL: this is a design, not measured; thresholds are initial hypotheses to calibrate in the evaluation task.

SURVEY (VERIFIED = page fetched and read; the fetch returns a model summary, so quotes are approximate):
- Hard vs soft is almost always 'context vs enforcement': Claude Code says CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced, and 'to block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook' (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, VERIFIED); Kiro steering is soft and hooks can gate (kiro.dev/docs/steering, /hooks, VERIFIED); Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot and OpenHands rules differ in WHEN text is loaded (always, globs, agent-chosen, manual), not whether it is obeyed (cursor.com/docs/context/rules; docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories; docs.github.com custom instructions; docs.openhands.dev microagents-overview; all VERIFIED).
- Graduated severity ladders exist in policy tools: Gatekeeper enforcementAction dryrun, warn, deny (open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper violations, VERIFIED); Kyverno Audit vs Enforce, with pre-existing resources grandfathered (kyverno.io validate docs, VERIFIED); Conftest deny, violation, warn (conftest.dev, VERIFIED thin); RFC 2119 MUST absolute, SHOULD 'valid reasons to ignore... implications understood and carefully weighed', MAY optional (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119, VERIFIED).
- Principles vs requirements: Spec Kit constitution (principles that stay constant) separate from specs; deviations go in a 'Complexity Tracking' section with justification (github.com/github/spec-kit spec-driven.md, VERIFIED, one page; amendment process not verified). OpenSpec records changes as ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED deltas (github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec, VERIFIED README).
- Exceptions: Kyverno PolicyException is a separate object, disabled by default; no expiry or approver field seen. ArchUnit FreezingArchRule stores existing violations so only NEW ones fail (archunit.org userguide, VERIFIED): the pattern for adopting a hard rule on legacy code. No verified tool combines reason + expiry + approver in one record; ddflow's waiver already does, which is beyond verified prior art.
- Goals: Linear initiatives have status and health, but health comes from a human-written update, not computed (linear.app/docs/initiatives, VERIFIED); GitHub milestones compute percent of closed issues (docs.github.com milestones, VERIFIED thin); SonarQube quality gates are numeric conditions on new code, 'Clean as You Code' (docs.sonarsource.com quality gates, VERIFIED); fitness functions are executable goals (thoughtworks.com fitness-function-driven-development, VERIFIED). Jira goals and OKR key-result design NOT verified.
- Proposal generation and noise control: Jules Suggested Tasks scans periodically, shows cards the user starts or dismisses, dismissal is used as feedback, daily task caps (jules.google/docs/suggested-tasks, /usage-limits, VERIFIED); Dependabot open-pull-requests-limit default 5, ignore rules, grouping, cooldown, security updates exempt (docs.github.com dependabot options reference, VERIFIED); Renovate prConcurrentLimit, prHourlyLimit, ignoreDeps, dependency dashboard approval (docs.renovatebot.com configuration-options, VERIFIED); Linear Triage: Accept, Decline with reason, Mark duplicate, Snooze (linear.app/docs/triage, VERIFIED); Devin Knowledge suggestions are edited or rejected by a human before saving (docs.devin.ai knowledge, VERIFIED). Claude Code /loop expires recurring tasks after 7 days and a bare loop 'does not start new initiatives outside that scope' (code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks, VERIFIED).
- ADR/MADR: status proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded by ADR-N, plus a 'Confirmation' section saying how compliance is verified (github.com/adr/madr template, VERIFIED).
NOT COVERED or not verifiable: Factory, LangGraph/AutoGen planner-executor, Jira goals, OKR design, CodeScene hotspots, import-linter contract types, Devin scheduled sessions, Copilot proactive tasks, defeasible-logic literature (used only as a pattern: default holds unless a recorded defeater), AI-product-owner tools (search snippets only).

DESIGN FACTS used: precedence org floor (override none) > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle (warn, deviate) > preference (advisory); goals never constrain, they steer ranking and discovery. Soft rules fail by silence, so a principle's finding must be answered (comply or deviate with a reason) before complete, and repeated deviations trigger a review of the principle (existing revisit-trigger mechanism). Proposal flood is controlled by an open cap (Dependabot default 5), a per-run cap, backpressure when the cap is reached, a rejected-ideas memory (Linear decline, Dependabot ignore) and a circuit breaker on zero-accept runs (B-sched-run).
- **Mechanism.** A principle differs from a rule only in how a finding is cleared (deviate by an agent with a reason, versus waive by a person with an expiry), so the existing waiver and review-trigger machinery carries it; a goal is a measurable target whose progress is computed from the DAG, metrics and approved checks (unavailable never counts as progress); a proposal is a record outside the queue until a person adopts it, so the scheduler and next never see unadopted ideas.
- **Falsifier.** Falsified if, after at least 3 discovery runs and 20 completed items under principles (task B-goal-eval): proposal acceptance stays under 10 percent (ideas are noise), or rejected ideas are re-proposed, or principle deviation rate is above 30 percent or the answered-finding rate is below 90 percent (soft rules are either wrong or ignored), or goal progress cannot be computed from the DAG for the first real goals.

**Probe:**

```console
$ WebFetch of the pages listed in sources (2026-10-11) for the survey; the design is checked against code by task B-goal-acceptance and calibrated by B-goal-eval.
Survey pages fetched; design not yet built or measured.
```

**Sources:** https://kiro.dev/docs/steering/, https://kiro.dev/docs/hooks/, https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks, https://cursor.com/docs/context/rules, https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/knowledge, https://docs.openhands.dev/usage/prompting/microagents-overview, https://jules.google/docs/suggested-tasks/, https://linear.app/docs/initiatives, https://linear.app/docs/triage, https://www.thoughtworks.com/insights/articles/fitness-function-driven-development, https://www.archunit.org/userguide/html/000_Index.html, https://github.com/adr/madr/blob/develop/template/adr-template.md, https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/violations/, https://kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/cluster-policy/validate/, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119, https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference, https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/, https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/quality-standards-administration/managing-quality-gates/introduction-to-quality-gates

## What does ddflow already have for goals, principles, strict and unstrict rules and periodic feature discovery, and which claims of the attached agentic-workflows document are true of this repository?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** ddflow already has the engine for strict and unstrict guidance, but no goal concept and no proposal store; the attached document (Architectural Orchestration of Goals, Defeasible Principles, and Invariants) is wrong about most names and about where the gaps are. Verified on main 2026-10-11.

EXISTS (read in code, ran commands): (1) one guidance engine, ddflow/services/guidance/: GuidanceRecord (kind rule|decision; scope globs/categories/gates; priority; enforcement advisory|warn|block; status proposed..rejected; owner; review_by; sources; checks; links), resolve.py (applicability + reason), inject.py (rank: pinned, always, enforcement, specificity, priority; budgeted via contextpack; fenced as data), checks.py (registry of check kinds, unavailable never pass, gate_verdict folds block/warn/advisory), waivers.py (record, reason, glob scope, expiry at most 90 days, approval by digest), review.py (review_by + revisit triggers, reaffirmed|changed). (2) Injection is wired at four doors: brief (api/lifecycle/brief.py GI.for_item), claim (claim.py GI.for_work), gate status (api/gates.py) and review prompts (api/review.py _with_guidance, verify=True, reviewer told to cite [id]). (3) Strict enforcement elsewhere: claim-before-edit lease, gate pipeline with require_outcome, unavailable outcome, cross-family reviewer rule, regression-test-for-bug rule, human approval gate (ddflow approve, no MCP tool), commit hooks (enforce.py), config strictest-value fallback. (4) Periodic work: ddflow cadence (count passes integration_tests, dedupe_sweep, architecture_review, mutation_tests, lessons_pass; calendar every_days; export staleness), schedule and trigger definitions (B-sched-model, B-trigger-model done; no ddflow schedule CLI yet: B-sched-author; no run: B-sched-run), D-sched-no-daemon, D-trigger-actions-create-items. (5) Record surface: RecordKind declares seven verbs and one MCP tool per kind; tools/list budget test allows about 8 more tools. (6) MCP resources ddflow://board brief lessons lessons-summary research bugs decisions sessions exist.

MISSING (verified absent by grep and by cli): goal records of any kind (README/ROADMAP Goals is user prose in B-rm-template); a principle/defeasible notion (decisions warn by default, but a warn finding needs no answer and a waiver needs a person and a 90 day expiry); deviation records; structured citation of guidance ids in review findings (the id is cited in prose only, nothing parses it); wiring of gate_verdict/run_record/waivers/review_due (only tests call them; there is no decisions gate yet, B-dec-monitor); a proposal store with adopt/defer/reject memory; enforcement/checks/owner/review_by flags on ddflow rule add (api/records.py RULE descriptor omits them; B-rules-onto-record-surface); any rule records in this project (ddflow rule list: No rules found). The document's names do not exist: ddflow/events.py, ddflow/replay.py (real: ddflow/core/events.py, services/sessions.py replay), ddflow principle add/override, ddflow_goal_*, ddflow_principle_*, ddflow_feature_propose, ddflow_proposal_triage, task adopt (ddflow adopt installs ddflow into a project), goal_upsert/principle_override/proposal_created events, and ddflow://research as a proposal feed (it renders the research log, findings with verdicts). Its four enforced rules, exit codes, event log, brief and cadence descriptions are right in substance.
- **Mechanism.** Read: ddflow/services/guidance/{record,kinds,resolve,inject,checks,waivers,review,deffields}.py, services/cadence.py, services/schedule.py, api/{gates,review}.py, api/lifecycle/{brief,claim}.py, api/records.py, surfaces/records.py, surfaces/mcp.py (RESOURCES), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, README sections on human approval; decisions D-decision-management, D-unify, D-rules-hierarchy, D-sched-no-daemon, D-trigger-actions-create-items, D-roadmap, D-old-work-behind-core-docs; bodies of B-dec-*, B-uni-guidance-*, B-sched-*, B-trigger-*, B-rm-*, B-rw-*, B-research-items, B-gap-plan-lint/metrics/lanes, B-security-pass, B-architecture-pass, B-dependency-upgrades, B-org-policy/kinds, B-coh-*, B-rules-*.
- **Falsifier.** Falsified if: any of the missing items is found in the code (grep -rni goal ddflow, grep -rn gate_verdict ddflow outside services/guidance and tests), or if a goal/principle command exists in ddflow --help.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow --help | grep -i goal (none); grep -rln "gate_verdict|run_record|review_due" ddflow (only services/guidance); ddflow rule list (No rules found); ddflow rule add --help (no enforcement flag); ddflow schedule list (invalid choice: schedule); ddflow cadence (count passes due); sed of RESOURCES in surfaces/mcp.py; ls ddflow/events.py ddflow/replay.py (missing).
```

## What do VS Code agent sessions/multiple chats and Claude Projects/sessions/teams do to share context between sessions, sub-sessions and agents, and what of that does ddflow already plan or lack?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** VS Code (docs read 2026-10-11): a SESSION is the unit of work with an agent: workspace + code changes + one or more chats (sessions.md, manage-sessions). A session has a main chat plus optional PEER chats that the USER prompts independently; each chat has its own history, title and agent/model, all share the session's workspace and worktree; a new chat starts BLANK and does not inherit other chats' history. Context moves only explicitly: FORK (branch a chat, inherits history, keeps prompt cache), side chat (privately inherits the source chat), /compact and automatic compaction (summary), HANDOFF (carries conversation history and context when the harness/environment/agent changes; custom-agent frontmatter handoffs[] = label, agent, prompt, send, model), delegation (remote: send_remote_message / get_remote_session / list_agent_hosts), and persistent sources (instructions, memory). Local subagents get NO parent history and are stateless (no follow-ups); settings chat.subagents.* (nesting depth max 5). Memory tool scopes: user /memories (first 200 lines loaded), repo /memories/repo (workspace-local, NOT shared), session /memories/session; all stored locally; team guidance is to move stable facts into source-controlled docs or instructions. Session history is a local SQLite DB synced to GitHub unless chat.sessionSync.enabled=false; search via /chronicle:search (keyword, file path, PR/issue ref). Export: command 'Chat: Export Chat...' (JSON). VS Code discovers local sessions created by Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, Claude Code and Codex. Agent Host owns sessions (AHP JSON-RPC, clients subscribe to session/chat URIs). Proposed extension API chatSessionsProvider. Hooks: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStart/Stop, Stop; files .github/hooks/*.json, [REDACTED:path]; Claude-format .claude/settings.json read when chat.useClaudeHooks (matchers ignored). Files: .github/agents/*.agent.md (also .claude/agents), .github/prompts/*.prompt.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md (applyTo), AGENTS.md (chat.useAgentsMdFile), CLAUDE.md (chat.useClaudeMdFile). Claude Code (docs read): session = JSONL transcript [REDACTED:path]<project>/<session-id>.jsonl (entry format internal, changes between versions); subagent transcripts .../<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl (30-day cleanup); --resume/--continue/--fork-session//branch; hooks get session_id, transcript_path, agent_id, agent_type; SessionStart source startup|resume|clear|compact|fork, additionalContext (10k chars); agent teams (experimental): lead + teammates, shared task list + JSON mailbox files under [REDACTED:path] and [REDACTED:path], no session resume of in-process teammates, one team per session; cross-session messaging (v2.1.224+): ListAgents/SendMessage over a per-session unix socket, plain text only, a message is never consent and cannot change config or approve prompts, inbound controls accept/hold/refuse; agent view (claude agents --json: sessionId, state working|blocked|done|failed|stopped, waitingFor, name, cwd); subagent persistent memory dirs .claude/agent-memory/<agent>/ (project scope shareable via git); Claude Code Projects (public beta, Pro/Max, not Team/Enterprise): one coordinator conversation starting a cloud-session THREAD per task; every thread gets project instructions (16,000 chars), project memory (MEMORY.md index + files) and repo CLAUDE.md, but not the coordinator's history; threads report back. claude.ai Projects (support article): knowledge base uploads + custom instructions + RAG on paid plans + sharing (can view/can edit) + chats inside the project.
ddflow today (measured by reading tasks and code in this repo 2026-10-11): ddflow session has start/prompt/note/adopt-orphans/end/list/show; session.started folds only the model; there is NO parent/child link, role or goal on a session; lanes U1..U6 have only lease events; brief + restart brief + PreCompact digest exist; P-agent-memory (B-am-*) already plans capture, handoff, restart-brief, search, session-cli, ingest of Claude transcripts, loops, retention; B-gap-lanes plans a lane ledger; adopt for vscode/copilot today writes only .vscode/mcp.json, .github/mcp.json, AGENTS.md and delta docs (verified by running adopt in a scratch repo): no .github/agents, .github/prompts, .github/hooks, .github/instructions.

## Does an older ddflow's write get refused for a mere patch skew, and does a log with two managed blocks go unreported?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B63635ddc6a`

- **Claim.** A stamp one PATCH above the running version (same FORMAT_LEVEL, no capability gap) raises SkewRefused today, and a file holding a stamped block plus a legacy-marker block is reported CURRENT by doctor and left with two blocks by adopt --refresh-docs.
- **Mechanism.** log._stamp_and_guard refuses on any is_older(version, highest); adopt._block_state/_upsert_block look only at the stamped grammar when one is present, so the legacy block is invisible to doctor and untouched by splice.
- **Falsifier.** If the failing-first tests pass on unmodified main, the claim is wrong.

## Does the observer's lease verdict depend on the claimant's wall clock?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B5a6651cd8e`

- **Claim.** Lease liveness for a foreign-clone lease is computed from the claimant's recorded at, so a -2h/+2h skewed claimant makes a live claim expired/overlong in another clone
- **Mechanism.** Lease.live compares recorded renewed_at (claimant time.time) with observer time.time; no receipt time
- **Falsifier.** With a sitecustomize-skewed claimant the observer still shows ~1800s left and no INTERRUPTED

**Probe:**

```console
$ pytest tests/test_lease_clock_skew.py against git archive of HEAD (unfixed)
10 failed, 1 passed (show: lease alice (-5401s left); status INTERRUPTED; claim EXPIRED; recover: ddflow release T1). With fix: 11 passed
```

## Why does rm -r .ddflow/local lock the agent out of its claim?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B839f599cb5`

- **Claim.** The derived id is host-dir-<clone-id>; the file is git-ignored so deletion mints a new suffix, making the old lease holder a stranger. Recovering the suffix from lease.acquired holders whose worktree is a directory under this checkout restores identity.
- **Mechanism.** infra/log._clone_suffix mints secrets.token_hex(3) whenever the file is missing, without consulting the log.
- **Falsifier.** After deleting .ddflow/local, heartbeat T1 still says 'no lease held' or a second shard appears.

**Probe:**

```console
$ uv run pytest tests/test_clone_id_recovery.py (run on unfixed main: test_deleting_local_keeps_the_identity failed with 'no lease held T1' rc 2 and test_newest_claim_wins failed ac3c5e != aaaaaa)
unfixed: 3 failed, 2 passed; fixed: 6 passed
```

## Do two clones sharing one agent name double-claim silently?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B36aa4c8ee5`

- **Claim.** A lease.acquired by the same holder from a different clone is folded as the holder's own re-claim, so no contest forms
- **Mechanism.** _clashing excludes same-holder claims and _h_lease_acquired treats cur.holder==new.holder as a re-claim
- **Falsifier.** If claims recording distinct clone ids still fold with an empty lease_contest, the claim is wrong

## How do comparable git-native and offline-sync systems handle many writers, identity, version skew and locks, and what can ddflow adopt without a server?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** Systems that stay correct across clones share four mechanisms ddflow lacks in part: collision-free or namespaced ids, a detected-and-surfaced conflict state for every record kind, a stored schema/version floor that older tools respect, and server-or-ref-backed arbitration only for exclusive claims
- **Mechanism.** git-bug and ddflow both use immutable ops ordered by Lamport clocks; Beads adds hash ids and a version guard; jj makes conflict a stored state; Gerrit keeps identity in the change; locks (git-lfs, merge queues, remote claim refs) need one arbiter
- **Falsifier.** A comparable system that merges concurrent same-id edits silently and is still considered safe

**Probe:**

```console
$ none possible: documentation survey
Fetched and summarised by a small model (summarised, not read in full): git-bug data model (operations as immutable blobs in a DAG, Lamport clocks, deterministic order by clock then pack id, no conflicts) https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/doc/design/data-model.md ; Gerrit Change-Id (an id in the commit footer that survives rebase, amend, cherry-pick; matched on id+repo+branch) https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/user-changeid.html ; Jujutsu first-class conflicts (conflict stored in the commit, resolved lazily, same-change auto-resolves) https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/technical/conflicts/ ; git-lfs locks (server-side lock registry, locks verified per owner, force unlock exists) https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/blob/main/docs/man/git-lfs-locks.adoc ; Beads (hash-based ids to avoid merge collisions, atomic --claim in one transaction, schema-version guard stops older binaries corrupting a migrated db, Dolt cell-level merge) https://github.com/steveyegge/beads ; Claude Code agent teams (shared task list, claiming uses file locking, tasks pending/in progress/completed with dependencies, one team per session, task status can lag) https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams ; protobuf rules (never reuse tag numbers, reserve removed fields, preserve unknown fields, no required fields) https://protobuf.dev/best-practices/dos-donts/ ; Tolerant Reader https://martinfowler.com/bliki/TolerantReader.html ; GitHub merge queue (temporary branch = base + queued PRs, required checks, failing PR dropped and queue rebuilt) https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue ; Zuul speculative gating (each change tested on top of those ahead) https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html ; OPA bundles (signed bundle, revision field, failed activation keeps the previous bundle) https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-bundles ; CRDTs (op-based need causal delivery and no duplication; tombstones; LWW vs OR-set) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict-free_replicated_data_type ; Taskwarrior sync (server replicas via TaskChampion; warns against file-sync tools, page does not describe conflict handling) https://taskwarrior.org/docs/sync/ ; Backlog.md (markdown tasks in the repo, checkActiveBranches to read task state across branches, no conflict rules documented) https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md. Not verified: Fossil tickets and clock skew (the page fetched did not cover them), Perforce exclusive checkout, Amp threads, Dolt conflict tables (redirected, not fetched).
```

**Sources:** see body of probe_output

## What does ddflow do when several users with their own clones, versions and agents work and merge periodically, and what breaks?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Textual merging of shards is safe in every tested git flow, but cross-clone meaning is protected only for item ids and claims; same-id knowledge records, shared agent names, clocks, version skew, generated files and history rewrites are silently wrong or noisy
- **Mechanism.** Events are per-writer shards merged by git (merge=union), ordered by (lamport, agent, id); B191 folds a second definition or an overlapping claim of one id into CONTESTED. Everything else is last-writer-wins on (lamport, agent) or wall-clock based, so correctness across clones depends on (a) distinct agent ids, (b) every record kind having a contest rule, (c) the reader noticing foreign events, (d) all clones running compatible ddflow.
- **Falsifier.** Any two-clone run in which same-id decisions, a shared agent name or a force-push is detected by doctor with a PROBLEM and a named remedy

**Probe:**

```console
$ python <scratchpad>/mu/s*.py with real git, bare origin, private HOME, ddflow main 0.2.1, v0.2.0, v0.1.18 trees (git archive)
Harness: harness.py/common.py in the mu directory; scripts s1 s1b s2b s2c s2d s3b s4 s4b s5(v0.2.0,v0.1.18) s6 s6e s6g s6i s7 s8 s9 s10 s11 s11e s12 (200 and 2000 events per shard). Observed (PASS=safe, D=degraded, B=broken): claim same task offline -> D (doctor rc1 CONTESTED; status/next silent; merge not refused); remote claims ref -> PASS (second claim rc3, offline remote refuses); same id task/phase -> PASS contested; same id decision/lesson/research -> B silent last-writer-wins, doctor clean, decision fields mixed across authors; same agent name on two clones -> B double claim, one shard with lamport 6..14 twice, doctor NOTE only; non-holder release -> D; removed item with live lease -> D; contradictory decisions -> D; older ddflow v0.2.0/v0.1.18 -> writes refused rc3 with a clear message, reads work, but its adopt rewrites newer managed files and duplicates the AGENTS.md block -> D; squash/rebase/merge of shards -> PASS; force-push/revert/reset loses events silently -> D; torn line, conflict markers, edited event -> PASS (doctor PROBLEM), CRLF and duplicate lines tolerated; shard deleted -> D silent; concurrent render of tracked views -> conflict on 3 files every time; conflicted config.toml -> every command dies with TOMLDecodeError; clock 2h behind -> live lease shown expired, recover advises release; local config differs -> pass looks identical; fresh clone has no hooks and doctor Healthy; rm .ddflow/local -> own lease locked out; scale 1.5MB 6000 events status 1.0s, 14.8MB 60000 events status 7.3s on a loaded host. 13 bugs filed (B230e852e10, B36aa4c8ee5, B2809f4213b, B71dedb76d2, B0dcccd8594, B90b43dd2d8, B5a6651cd8e, B839f599cb5, B6b8d1f7a0f, B63635ddc6a, Ba24a8d32ee, Bec9a971c5d, B924bdc92d7).
```

**Sources:** docs/ddflow/MULTI-USER.md, tests/test_multiuser_merge_model.py, docs/ddflow/compatibility.md

## Can gate verify see a mutation for a gate that reads HEAD?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B-verify-ci-blind`

- **Claim.** verify writes the mutation uncommitted, so a gate reading a committed ref (ci, git show HEAD:f) reports passed on mutated source
- **Mechanism.** ci.run merges the committed branch in a scratch worktree; the working-tree edit is never in it
- **Falsifier.** a gate 'git show HEAD:src/calc.py | grep -q ...' with a mutation of that file comes back detected on the unfixed code

**Probe:**

```console
$ pytest tests/test_gate_verify.py::test_a_gate_that_reads_head_sees_the_mutation on unfixed code
FAILED: a HEAD-reading gate could not see the mutation (3 new tests failed before the fix, 16 pass after)
```

## Can gate verify prove ci and unit_tests go red with a registered mutation?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `U4-mutation-registry`

- **Claim.** unit_tests goes red when clock.UNPARSEABLE drops ValueError; ci cannot, because ci run checks the committed HEAD while verify mutates the working tree
- **Mechanism.** mutation.verify writes the edit uncommitted; ci.run(ref=HEAD) merges the committed branch in a scratch worktree
- **Falsifier.** verify reports ci detected the unused-import mutation


## Does the event-evolution machinery work against a real bump, over logs releases wrote, and does a long-lived server survive a self-upgrade?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `B-arch-upgrade-risks`

- **Claim.** A phase.added v1->v2 rename upcaster plus a handler that knows only the new shape folds every released fixture log to the same state, an older reader skips the v2 line it did not write, and an old MCP server refuses writes (exit 3) after the new code stamped the log
- **Mechanism.** EventLog reads the release shards from disk, fold upcasts per event (ids kept); NewerPayload is counted as skipped by non-strict folds; the skew guard compares the process version with the log's stamps
- **Falsifier.** a released log folds to a different state with the upcaster, the older reader crashes or loses the line, or the old server writes after the new code stamped the log

```console
71 passed; the dry run on the 0.2.0 project of this repository folds through an upcaster for its most common kind
```

## What do comparable AI-agent workflow tools, work-queue and merge-queue systems do that ddflow lacks, and where is ddflow ahead?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** FETCHED (primary page read through WebFetch, which summarises with a small model, so treat details as second-hand) 2026-10-10: Beads github.com/steveyegge/beads (Dolt-backed, hash ids bd-a1b2 with hierarchical .1/.1.1 children, `bd ready --claim` claims atomically, memory decay summarises old closed tasks, `bd prime`/`bd remember`); claude-task-master github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master (PRD parse to tasks, analyze_project_complexity, expand_task, tags, 36 MCP tools in core/standard/all tiers); GitHub Spec Kit github.com/github/spec-kit (constitution, specify, clarify, plan, tasks, analyze, implement, converge loop); OpenSpec github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec (specs/ vs changes/<name>/{proposal,specs,design,tasks}, WHEN/THEN scenarios, delta specs, propose/apply/archive); Backlog.md github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md (markdown tasks in git, terminal kanban, web UI, MCP, Definition of Done, three review checkpoints spec/plan/code); BMAD-METHOD github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD (role personas, durable context docs); Kiro docs kiro.dev/docs/specs (requirements/design/tasks, tasks grouped into dependency waves run concurrently); Superpowers github.com/obra/superpowers (brainstorm, worktree, plan, subagent-per-task, TDD, review between tasks as mandatory skills); Claude Code agent teams code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams (shared task list with dependencies, file-locked claiming, TeammateIdle/TaskCreated/TaskCompleted hooks that exit 2 to block, mailbox JSON, no resume of teammates, one team per session, 'task status can lag'); Claude Code costs code.claude.com/docs/en/costs (/usage session cost from token counts at list price, --max-budget-usd, OpenTelemetry, per-teammate token cost ~7x in plan mode); Vibe Kanban github.com/BloopAI/vibe-kanban (kanban, workspaces, inline diff comments, PR creation, 10+ agents; README says SUNSETTING); Crystal github.com/stravu/crystal (deprecated Feb 2026, replaced by Nimbalyst); Claude Squad github.com/smtg-ai/claude-squad (tmux session per agent plus worktree, autoyes); OpenHands github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands (sandboxed runtimes, stuck detection, max_budget_per_task, max_iterations, SWE-bench, GitHub resolver); GitHub Copilot cloud agent docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/coding-agent/about-coding-agent (ephemeral environment, 59 minute cap, one branch, branch rules may block); GitHub merge queue docs.github.com/.../managing-a-merge-queue (temporary gh-readonly-queue branches, merge_group event, build concurrency 1-100, group size, failed PR removed and rest regrouped); Zuul zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html (speculative testing of A, A+B, A+B+C in parallel, failure restarts those behind it, Depends-On footers, shared change queues); Mergify docs.mergify.com/merge-queue (batching, priority rules, scopes for monorepos, two-step CI, freeze, analytics); bors-ng github.com/bors-ng/bors-ng (ARCHIVED 2024, staging branch, batch bisection on failure, points users to GitHub merge queue); Nx nx.dev/docs/features/ci-features/affected (git diff to project graph to reverse dependency closure, run tasks on affected only); Temporal docs.temporal.io/workflows (event history replayed deterministically, activity results reused on replay); Langfuse langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview (traces, token and cost per model, sessions, scores, datasets); Inspect inspect.aisi.org.uk (tasks/solvers/scorers, Docker/K8s sandboxes, log viewer, eval sets with retry). SEARCH-SNIPPET ONLY (not fetched, SUMMARISED): Conductor (Melty Labs, macOS, closed source, worktree per agent, PR and CI checks inline) and Emdash (open source, issue intake from Linear/GitHub/Jira/GitLab/Asana, SSH to remote machines) via paralect.com and emdash.com blog results; Launchable predictive test selection (ML on change log plus test history, claims up to 80% less test time) via help.launchableinc.com; Linear for Agents linear.app/developers/agents (agent delegated via assignment, AgentSession lifecycle webhook). NOT READ AT ALL (from memory, THEORETICAL): Devin, Factory, Amp, Jules, Cline/Cursor background agents, Gerrit, Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Argo, Buildkite, Bazel, Phoenix, SWE-agent, aider-composer, GitHub Projects, Jira.
- **Mechanism.** What others have that ddflow lacks (mechanism): (1) Plan decomposition from a spec/PRD plus plan review before code: Task Master, Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec, Backlog.md; ddflow has no plan lint or plan-review step, only hand-filed tasks. (2) Atomic ready+claim in one call (Beads `ready --claim`): ddflow has next then claim, two calls with a race the lease already refuses, so this is cosmetic. (3) Memory decay / summarisation of closed work (Beads): ddflow has brief budgets and BL-knowledge compaction tasks. (4) Dependency waves shown up front (Kiro): ddflow has B-dag-waves-fanout open. (5) Speculative combined-tree testing and bisecting a failed batch (Zuul, bors, GitHub queue, Mergify): ddflow has B-batch-integration open, with no bisect-on-failure stated. (6) Affected-target test selection from a dependency graph (Nx, Bazel; ML in Launchable): ddflow selects by name and governs only. (7) Per-task token and cost attribution plus hard budgets (Langfuse, OpenHands max_budget_per_task, Claude Code --max-budget-usd and OTel): ddflow has quota percent windows planned (B-quota-*), no per-task or per-lane spend. (8) Stuck/loop detection with automatic stop (OpenHands): ddflow has B-am-loops planned. (9) A live board/TUI/web view (Backlog.md, Vibe Kanban, Claude Squad, Conductor): ddflow renders markdown and text only. (10) Issue intake and PR/check-run feedback (Emdash, Copilot agent, Linear agents): ddflow has external sync, pr_sync and a one-way tracker sink planned, no check-run publishing. (11) Sandboxed execution (OpenHands, Inspect, Copilot firewall): ddflow runs gate commands from repository config unsandboxed. (12) Hooks that block task creation/completion (agent teams TaskCreated/TaskCompleted): ddflow gates are stronger. Where ddflow is ahead: append-only content-addressed log with Lamport order and per-agent shards (merge without conflict, replay), expiry leases that report rather than steal, unavailable-not-passed gate semantics, enforced cross-family review and failing-first regression tests, glob-based admission with named alternatives, decisions/lessons/research as governed records with dedupe and provenance fencing, one declaration for CLI and MCP with a parity test, upgrade model with skew guard. None of the fetched tools had an equivalent of any of these as an enforced rule; Beads and Backlog.md are closest on storage in git but have no gates. The bors-ng and Vibe Kanban/Crystal status facts show that thin worktree-manager UIs are being sunset or absorbed by harness vendors and merge queues by GitHub, which is the evidence for 'do not build a UI or a merge-queue service'.
- **Falsifier.** A fetched page's current text contradicts the summary above, or a tool listed as lacking a capability documents it.

**Sources:** https://github.com/steveyegge/beads, https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master, https://github.com/github/spec-kit, https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec, https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs, https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html, https://github.com/bors-ng/bors-ng, https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue, https://nx.dev/docs/features/ci-features/affected, https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands, https://kiro.dev/docs/specs/, https://github.com/BloopAI/vibe-kanban

## What does ddflow's own event log and code show about where the queue and workflow core is weak (growth, latency, gate friction, missing capabilities)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Measured on this repository's event log on 2026-10-10 (53,163 events, 35 MB, 13 active days 2026-09-28..2026-10-10, ~4,090 events and ~2.7 MB per active day): lease.renewed is 24,413 events = 46% of all events (17% of bytes); gate.failed + gate.passed carry 52% of bytes (evidence stored inline); wall time of `ddflow status` 5.4 s and `ddflow next` 2.2 s on this log. 850 item.completed, median item.started->item.completed 1.04 h, p90 2.8 h, max 31.8 h (n=667). 508 bug.found against 850 completions. Gate outcomes: rubber_duck failed 860 / passed 639, critic failed 849 / passed 618 (each review round that reports findings is a failed event), ci failed 168 / passed 527, unit_tests failed 83 / passed 966; 330 gate.skipped of which docs 149, dedupe 43, bug_hunt 42; 962 gate.out_of_order; 419 ci.result of which 412 true. ddflow/ is 106,688 lines, tests/ 124,749 lines. No source file mentions forecast or supervisor; throughput appears only in services/review.py; critical_path exists in core/schedule.py and core/graph.py; `ddflow tests` exists and selects tests by name and governs only (services/testselect.py); an outside-globs check exists (api lifecycle). origin remote exists (github.com/delian/ddflow-mcp). No gate-command trust or approval of a gate command found in services/gates/defs.py or api/gates.py (grep for approv/trust).

## Does the external `sequential` companion compute or persist anything ddflow lacks, and is it worth recommending versus a native reasoning log in ddflow?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** The `sequential` companion is @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking (tool `sequentialthinking`, v2026.8.31). It COMPUTES nothing and RETURNS no thought text: it appends the input to an in-process array, adds it to a branches map when branchFromThought and branchId are both set, raises totalThoughts to thoughtNumber if lower, optionally prints a boxed copy to stderr, and returns only {thoughtNumber, totalThoughts, nextThoughtNeeded, branches (ids), thoughtHistoryLength}. It validates types only (ints >= 1): it does not check that revisesThought or branchFromThought refer to an existing thought, that numbers are monotonic or that isRevision is paired with revisesThought. There is no tool to read, search, persist or export the history, which dies with the process (so with a harness restart or context loss). Marginal value is therefore the agent's own discipline, not the server. Anthropic's own think-tool post (updated 2025-12-15) now recommends native extended thinking instead of a dedicated think tool in most cases.
- **Mechanism.** processThought() in dist/lib.js: push to thoughtHistory; branches[branchId].push when both branch fields present; Math.max-style totalThoughts bump; console.error(formatted box) unless DISABLE_THOUGHT_LOGGING=true; JSON of counters returned. index.js registers one tool with a zod schema and readOnlyHint true. Nothing reads thoughtHistory except its own length. The value the description promises ('generates a hypothesis, verifies it') is prompt text only; no code does either.
- **Falsifier.** A tools/call response that contains the thought text, a restart that preserves the history, a refusal of revisesThought=42 when only thought 1 exists, or any tool in tools/list other than sequentialthinking.

**Probe:**

```console
$ npm pack @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking (2026.8.31), npm install --omit=dev, then JSON-RPC over stdio: initialize; call thought 1/3; call thought 9/3 isRevision revisesThought=42 branchFromThought=1 branchId=b.
call1 -> {"thoughtNumber":1,"totalThoughts":3,"nextThoughtNeeded":true,"branches":[],"thoughtHistoryLength":1}
call2 -> {"thoughtNumber":9,"totalThoughts":9,"nextThoughtNeeded":false,"branches":["b"],"thoughtHistoryLength":2}   (revisesThought 42 accepted; totalThoughts bumped 3->9)
stderr: boxed copies of the two thoughts only; no thought text in either response.
```

**Sources:** https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking (tarball read and run: verified); https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/sequentialthinking (README, summarised); https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-think-tool (update note 2025-12-15 and tau-bench numbers: fetched, summarised); https://github.com/arben-adm/mcp-sequential-thinking (persistent fork, summarised); https://github.com/spences10/mcp-sequentialthinking-tools (tool-recommendation variant, summarised); https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/agent-stuck-detector (summarised); https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05410 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04388 (CoT unfaithfulness, summarised from search)

## What of an agent's context and communication does ddflow keep today, what survives a context-exhaustion restart, can agents and the operator search it, and what do other tools do that we lack?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** ddflow records operator prompts (260 session.prompt events, ~121 KB of a 35 MB log), a few session notes (44) and one-line session.ended summaries (42), plus one PreCompact tail digest of at most 2000 chars when the PreCompact hook is installed. It does NOT record: the briefs a coordinator sends a lane (U1..U6 have 0 session.prompt events; only lease/gate events), a lane's final report, tool calls or results, or any harness transcript. The PreCompact digest is the last turns BEFORE compaction, not a summary; the harness writes the real compaction summary into the transcript as an isCompactSummary entry (verified locally) that no ddflow code reads. There is no cross-agent or semantic search over session content beyond BM25 over prompts/notes (+ query-time rerank only when [rag] is configured), no session search/timeline/diff/dump CLI or MCP tools (only list/show/start/prompt/note/end), and the loop detectors (7 kinds) cover queue/gate behaviour only, never repeated commands, repeated refusals or recurring lessons.
- **Mechanism.** Gap analysis by reading code and running commands (file:line in the task bodies), plus a primary-source survey. Design: reuse sessions/searchcore/contextpack/redact/LocalStore/def-records/upcasters/command registry/guidance inject/ticks; add (1) harness transcript pointers + read-only redacted ingestion into a local-only store, (2) lane brief/report capture, (3) a structured session.handoff event written deterministically at PreCompact/lane stop and enriched from the harness compaction summary, (4) restart brief injection, (5) a transcripts SearchSource, (6) session search/timeline/diff/dump/export on CLI+MCP, (7) command-signature loop detection with reminders, (8) retention/privacy.
CONFIRMED covers only the ddflow gap claims (verified by command and local files). The outside survey (Letta, mem0, Zep, claude-mem, Factory, JetBrains, OpenHands, Amp, Entire) was read through page summaries and is design input, not verified fact; vendor benchmark numbers are unverified and disputed.
- **Falsifier.** Falsified if a lane (U1..U6) has recorded briefs or reports in .ddflow/events, if `ddflow session --help` lists search/timeline/diff/dump, if a code path reads isCompactSummary, or if a loops detector keyed on repeated commands exists. Part 2 claims are falsified by the cited primary sources saying otherwise.

**Probe:**

```console
$ ddflow session --help; ddflow hooks status; ddflow search --help; ddflow loops; python over .ddflow/events counting kinds per agent (U1..U6 have only lease.acquired; U6 has 1 session.started + 1 session.ended of 335 bytes); search for 'ddflow implementation agent' in .ddflow (no hit); python over [REDACTED:path] finding an isCompactSummary:true user entry whose text begins 'This session is being continued ... Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent'; find [REDACTED:path] -path '*subagents*' -name '*.jsonl' | wc -l -> 541.
session kinds: session.note 44 (35254 B), session.started 58, session.ended 42 (22997 B), session.prompt 260 (120749 B) of 53056 events / 35 MB. hooks status: 'Claude Code PreCompact hook: not installed'; 'prompt capture hook: Claude Code: not installed; Gemini CLI: not installed'. session list: U6 0p 0n; ddflow loops prints only gate_flapping/duplicate_work warnings. Transcript: isCompactSummary True, message content 'This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context ... Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent:'. subagent transcripts on disk: 541 files. Docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, fetched): PreCompact/PostCompact payload = session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name; SubagentStop adds agent_id, agent_type, last_assistant_message; a PostCompact compact_summary field is claimed only by third-party issues and is NOT verified. Sub-agent transcripts live at [REDACTED:path]}/{sessionId}/subagents/agent-{agentId}.jsonl and are deleted after cleanupPeriodDays (30 default).
```

**Sources:** https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents, https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents, https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system, https://claude.com/blog/context-management, https://factory.com/news/evaluating-compression, https://blog.jetbrains.com/research/2025/12/efficient-context-management/, https://docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/agent-stuck-detector, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03704, https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, https://ampcode.com/news/handoff, https://cognition.com/blog/dont-build-multi-agents, https://docs.entire.io/guides/sessions/overview, https://docs.cline.bot/prompting/cline-memory-bank, https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/, https://aider.chat/docs/config/options.html

## What can a cleanup after P-unify realistically remove from ddflow/ and tests/, which guard baselines can it take to their floors, and is the -10% line target reachable?

**Verdict: THEORETICAL**

- **Claim.** A cleanup slice after P-unify can remove about 2,200 lines of ddflow/ (range 1,500 to 3,000; 104,929 -> about 102,700, -2%) and about 1,000 lines of tests (119,528 -> about 118,500), and take the guard ratchets to subprocess_calls 13->4, write_text 10->0, tempfile 6->0, deferred_imports 534->90, surfaces-through-api 34->6, subprocess-home 7->1, fsio-home 7->1, complexity_d_or_worse 100->85, duplicate_code_clusters 4->0, unreferenced_functions 5->2. It cannot reach the -10% line target (66,060 lines): that needs -38,869 lines (-37%), about 17 times what cleanup removes.
- **Mechanism.** The lines are not duplicated helper bodies: pylint finds 4 duplicate clusters, an AST scan finds 3 exact duplicate function bodies in ddflow/ (15 lines), and 161 one-line delegating shims (62 with 2 or fewer uses) are about 3 lines each. They sit in three structures. (1) The command registry generates the argparse parser and the MCP tool, but each of the 134 declared commands is still named a second time in glue (surfaces/parsers/*.py 745 lines: 53 HANDLERS rows and imports; surfaces/tools/*.py 828 lines: 107 `BY_TOOL[..].tool_entry()` rows) and a third time in a hand-written CLI handler that repeats the `call` lambda's argument translation and the JSON/refusal emission (surfaces/commands/*.py 5,051 lines; commands/rules.py: 120 of 190 lines are call translation and emit, 60 are rendering). `Command.render` and `Command.handler` exist and no declaration uses `render`. (2) 507 of the 534 deferred imports have no import cycle (top-level reachability graph, 9 cycles, 56 stdlib/optional) and the CLI already loads 331 of 393 modules at startup (0.42 s), so the deferral saves nothing; each removal also merges duplicates (309 distinct new top-level targets for 507 sites). (3) tests define `_git` in 91 files (494 lines, 27 distinct bodies) and 838 further lines of byte-identical helper copies.
- **Falsifier.** Refuted if B-uc-acceptance measures ddflow/ above 103,500 lines or any ratchet above the value named here without a recorded reason, or if golden snapshots / the full suite are not green and not slower. The CLI-executor estimate (-1,160, 22% of the 5,051 hand-written command lines, measured exemplar 60% for rules) is the main uncertainty: the pilot on `rule` (B-uc-surf-registry) re-measures it before the family slices start.

## Did P-unify reduce the ddflow package by 10 percent or more against the 73.4k lines R-unify measured, with no feature loss?

**Verdict: REFUTED** · item `B-uni-acceptance`

- **Claim.** P-unify does not meet its -10% line target. Counted as R-unify did (all lines of every .py file under ddflow/, newline count): main e4342e62 had 73,400 lines in 176 modules; HEAD (caebb49a, before this task) has 104,929 lines in 393 modules: +31,529 lines, +43.0%. Non-blank lines: 64,479 -> 91,358 (+41.7%). Tests: 75,515 -> 119,528 lines (330 -> 559 files). By package (lines, before -> after): services 34,447->47,736; surfaces 11,591->16,242; core 5,866->10,477; api 13,598->18,088; infra 4,879->7,393; config_sections 0->2,534 (config.py 2,013->966 after its split, so config as a whole +1,487). Net ddflow/ lines added by first-parent merges since e4342e62, by phase: P-unify +16,879 (the shared interfaces, compat contract, record surface, guidance, tests-first migration), B-upgrade +3,418, Unphased +2,484, P-schedule +1,533, B-adaptive-flow +1,205, B-hot-files +1,084 (splits add module headers), bugs +930, P-harness-adapters +685, P-id-schemes +608, other mined backlog +546, gate-economy +451. About 13.8k net lines are features that did not exist at the baseline (upgrade, schedule, adaptive flow, harness adapters, id schemes, export, reporting); about 16.9k are P-unify's own, which landed the interfaces and migrated call sites in slices but has so far removed little duplicate code in absolute terms, and the largest removal was config.py (-1,047 before its sections moved out). Ratchets did go down (git_argv 26->0, hashlib 23->0, os_replace 1->0, write_text 40->10, subprocess_calls 42->13, tempfile 12->6, deferred_imports 620->534, complexity_d_or_worse 112->100, duplicate clusters 6->4) but none of subprocess_calls, write_text, tempfile reached zero.
- **Mechanism.** Line count is a size measure, not a cost measure: the shared interfaces were built before most call sites moved, and 2,100 commits of new features landed in the same period. The -10% target would hold only if the removals outweighed the roughly 14k net lines of new features, which they did not.
- **Falsifier.** Refuted if the same count at HEAD is above 66,060 (73,400 x 0.9). It is 104,929.

## Does ddflow support Grok and the grok bots, and what does it take to test that every coding agent and bot we want to support actually works with ddflow (integration, hooks, identity, MCP, headless runs, bot modes)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Grok is not supported as an agent today: it appears only as a model family (agent.families grok -> xai) and a reviewer preset (xAI endpoint, grok-4); there is no Grok adopt target, hook, instruction-file or test. Of Grok's surfaces exactly one is a drivable agent: the official Grok Build CLI (`grok`; AGENTS.md from the root down plus .grok/rules/ and CLAUDE.md/.cursor/rules for compatibility; MCP in [mcp_servers.<name>] of [REDACTED:path] or .grok/config.toml via `grok mcp add`; JSON hooks in [REDACTED:path] and .grok/hooks with PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop; skills and .grok/agents subagents; `grok -p` headless with --output-format json|streaming-json, --always-approve, `grok agent stdio` ACP; XAI_API_KEY or a subscription; no documented session-id variable), with a community near-twin superagent-ai/grok-cli ([REDACTED:path], MCP via `grok mcp add`, hooks unconfirmed; the two share [REDACTED:path]). Grok inside Copilot, Cursor, Cline, Kilo, opencode, Windsurf is a model, covered by the host agent's row and the xAI family rule. Grok chat/web/mobile/@grok on X and the xAI API are not agents ddflow can drive; no official xAI GitHub bot exists. Bots: ddflow can use a stdio MCP server only where the agent runs code in a VM we control (Claude Code Action, Gemini CLI Action, Copilot cloud agent via copilot-setup-steps.yml and COPILOT_MCP_-prefixed secrets, OpenHands, Amp, Droid); Jules, Devin, Cursor cloud agents and Codex cloud are instructions-only or remote-MCP-only until probed; review bots (CodeRabbit, Qodo) and Dependabot/Renovate are event sources; Sweep is deprecated. Nothing in the repo exercises a real agent or bot: P-harness-adapters (0/11) plans descriptors and fixture-based conformance only. Open facts to probe: Grok Build hook payload and session id and MCP approval step, Codex cloud custom MCP, Cursor cloud custom stdio MCP, Devin stdio inside its VM, Copilot AGENTS.md support, exit codes of grok/amp/droid.
- **Mechanism.** Three test layers: (1) deterministic MCP layer with no LLM (the MCP inspector CLI and the official conformance runner against ddflow's stdio server at pinned protocol versions); (2) offline conformance from live-recorded payload fixtures per agent (replay catches schema drift cheaply); (3) live smoke runs of each headless agent (claude -p, codex exec, gemini -p, grok -p, amp -x, droid exec, openhands --headless) with a fixed tiny task, asserting on ddflow's event log and not on prose, with turn caps, timeouts, one retry, majority-of-3 and 'unavailable' on missing key, CLI or rate limit; bots (Copilot cloud agent, @claude, Codex cloud, Jules, Devin, Cursor cloud) via a sandbox repo with scheduled smoke issues, advisory only. Prior art for adapters: Harbor and Terminal-Bench install-and-invoke agent adapters.
- **Falsifier.** A throwaway repo is adopted for Grok Build; a scripted `grok -p` run calls ddflow_brief and claims, edits and completes a trivial task, the event log shows it under a distinct identity, a replayed recorded hook payload fixture passes conformance offline, and the same harness reports 'unavailable' (not pass) for an agent without a key.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Code grep (grok appears only in agent/config_sections/agent.py families and services/review.py xai preset), board census of P-harness-adapters and P-agent-hygiene, web survey of Grok Build, grok-cli, xAI API and 13 bots/cloud agents (confidence per fact tagged V/S/? in the report).
```

## How should ddflow's research system serve every context, including the writing and review of code that implements a formula, algorithm, constant or protocol, be correctable, verify duplicates and contradictions per claim, and reuse the shared components?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Today (main 478ae1e8): a research note is flat (core/records.py:756 ResearchNote: question, claim, mechanism, falsifier, probe, probe_output, verdict, flat sources, tags, item); one event research.recorded replaces the whole note; no edit, supersede or retire; probe is never re-run and a CONFIRMED verdict never goes stale; no link to code (no globs, no anchors), tests or decisions; the research gate (gates/defs.py:92, outcomes.py:365) accepts any non-empty free text and never looks for a linked record; brief and claim carry no research (brief.py injects lessons, decisions, memories); FTS indexes question, claim, probe and verdict only; duplicate detection is record-level TF-IDF (api/_dedupe.py) with no polarity, number or verdict logic, and a new REFUTED against an old CONFIRMED is accepted silently; 523 research rows exist. Of P-research's 16 tasks none depends on a P-unify component: B-rw-schema writes its own events though def-records reserves kind 'claim' (core/defs.py:38); B-rw-inject, B-rw-query and B-semantic-recall build their own injection, search and embedder; B-rw-stale and B-rw-sources build their own change and source checks; B-rw-revise duplicates def-records; B-rw-gate-link overlaps kind-pipeline. Landed and unused by research: ChangeDetector, run_shell, approval, upcasters, def-records, core/globs, OverlayLoader, GOVERNS test selection. Missing and unplanned: a typed link from a claim to code and tests, re-running a claim's check, a gate that makes implementation cite and match its claim, edit-time retrieval, claim-level duplicate and contradiction checks, and research-vs-research contradiction.
- **Mechanism.** Prior art: OpenFastTrace (spec items with revision; source tags [impl->dsn~x~1]; a bumped revision makes tags 'outdated coverage'), StrictDoc (@relation markers resolved to a symbol), Doorstop (links carry the target fingerprint; changed target = suspect link until reviewed), Swimm (auto re-pin of trivial change vs fail on substantive change), Reqstool/Tiger (build fails on missing implementation or passing test), DO-178C/ISO 26262 bidirectional trace matrices and change-impact analysis; executable specs: known-answer test vectors (NIST CAVP, RFC appendices), property-based and oracle and metamorphic tests, doctests, design by contract; claim-level verification: FActScore (atomic claims), ALCE and AIS (does the stored passage entail the claim), Chain-of-Verification, CRITIC (tool-checked), GRADE evidence grading; retrieval: hybrid BM25 + embeddings with reciprocal-rank fusion and rerank (Contextual Retrieval), repo maps, path-keyed edit-time injection; maintenance: Graphiti/Zep validity windows with invalidate-not-delete, Mem0, normalised subject/attribute/value/unit claims for exact contradiction detection, NLI for the rest.
- **Falsifier.** A formula claim with known-answer vectors is implemented in code carrying '# ddflow: implements C-x@1'; changing the code or revising the claim to @2 surfaces 'outdated' or 'suspect' at the next gate, the vectors run and fail a wrong implementation, editing that file shows the claim in context, and a new REFUTED claim against an old CONFIRMED one is flagged; none of this requires a new search engine, queue or injector.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Code survey of core/records.py, handlers/knowledge.py, api/knowledge/research.py, api/lifecycle/brief.py, services/gates/defs.py and outcomes.py, infra/store.py, api/_dedupe.py, services/verify.py, board census of P-research and P-unify; web survey of the tools named.
Confirmed as listed in the claim. 4 web sources re-fetched (OpenFastTrace, StrictDoc, Swimm, Graphiti); the rest are canonical pages not re-fetched.
```

**Sources:** https://github.com/itsallcode/openfasttrace/blob/develop/doc/user_guide.md, https://strictdoc.readthedocs.io/en/stable/stable/docs/strictdoc_11_developer_guide-TRACE.html, https://doorstop.readthedocs.io, https://swimm.io/blog/continuous-documentation-through-continuous-integration-with-swimm, https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13956v1, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14251, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14627, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12870, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11495, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11738, https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval, https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io, https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-algorithm-validation-program, https://www.gradeworkinggroup.org, https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/

## Does running only testselect's selection in unit_tests for fix and small tasks save the time D-gate-economy measured, and what must stay full?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `B-gate-econ-tests`

What it misses (subprocess-only tests, >2 import hops, re-export __init__s) is caught only by a full run, so the full suite must still run once on the merge result: selection is safe only where the pipeline has a ci gate; otherwise unit_tests stays full.

- **Falsifier.** A selection for a one-file fix that is most of the suite, or run_command returning '' for this project's pytest command.

**Probe:**

```console

11 of ~470 test files; 24 s vs 281 s; run_command keeps runner prefix and options, replaces tests/ with the files
```

## Can the write_text/mkstemp writers in companions, adopt, enforce, api/rules, services/rules, operations and flowstate move to fsio.atomic_write with no user-visible change?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `B-uni-fsio-writers.1-write`

- **Claim.** Not as atomic_write stands: it differs from Path.write_text in three observable ways - it replaces a symlink with a regular file instead of writing through it (CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md is a common layout adopt writes), it creates missing parent directories where write_text raises FileNotFoundError, and it writes '\n' untranslated where text mode writes os.linesep (Windows CRLF). A write-through, no-mkdir, newline-translating wrapper (fsio.replace_text) keeps every site identical. Separately, api/rules DDFLOW.md and services/rules rule files are written (and rules read) in the LOCALE encoding: a non-ASCII rule fails under an ASCII locale - a bug, fixed by utf-8 both ways.
- **Mechanism.** os.replace(tmp, link) renames over the link itself; Path.write_text opens the link (follows it); open() text mode newline=None translates; write_text() without encoding uses locale.getencoding().
- **Falsifier.** atomic_write on a symlink leaves the link in place, or write_text under LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 writes a non-ASCII string.

**Probe:**

```console
$ scratchpad U2_probe2.py (symlink, missing dir) and U2_enc.py under LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0
write_text: link kept: True target: via write_text / atomic_write: link kept: False (link replaced by a regular file) / write_text into missing dir: FileNotFoundError / Path.write_text('café') under C locale: UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character
```

## Why does the loaded crash-recovery scenario fail in ci under heavy load?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-Bb070dd642d`

- **Claim.** The injected delay (TTL/2+0.5 = 4.5 s of an 8 s lease) leaves 3.5 s for show + the real claim; at load 120-220 those cost 3.6-4.8 s, so every _while_live attempt outlives the lease. - **Falsifier.** the test with +4.8 s latency passes under an 8 s lease, or fails under the 24 s lease

```console
TTL 8: FAILED 'every attempt outlived the 8s lease (load average (29.8, 146.5, 181.3))'; TTL 24: 1 passed in 99.29s. Original failures: ci logs .ddflow/runs/fix-B028b11b4cb/ci-20261007T000506*.log (attempts finished 8.1-9.3 s after heartbeat) and fix-B4af8a88294 ci runs twice at load ~180.
```

## Can one fsio.ensure_ignored_dir, one fsio.repo_rel and one Region.splice replace the self-ignoring-directory copies, worktree.repo_relative and append_block's join with no behaviour change?

## Which rule selects the tests that read a changed data file under a test directory, without over-selecting?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** · item `fix-B20b7744905`

- **Claim.** select() picks no test for a changed non-test file under tests/ today; picking the tests whose source names (1) the file name together with one of its directories below the nearest test-holding directory, else (2) the nearest such directory, else (3) the file name, maps every one of this repo's 30 data files under tests/ to the test that reads it and nothing else
- **Mechanism.** tests read fixtures and baselines by path literal: a full name (corpus.jsonl, schema.json) or, when built dynamically (f'{name}.toml'), only the directory (guard_baselines); a bare file name (.gitattributes, LICENSE) is too generic alone, so it is paired with a directory first
- **Falsifier.** the current select() returning a test for a data-only change, or the rule selecting a test that does not read the file (e.g. .gitattributes picking the ~10 tests that write their own .gitattributes)

## How should ddflow keep, preset, monitor and maintain a project's architectural decisions (infrastructure, coding style, libraries, dependencies, upgrade policy, tests, security) so they are checked and reminded wherever they apply, and managed like every other record (CLI, MCP, config, add/edit/remove, search, RAG)?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

- **Claim.** Decisions are an ADR-shaped log record (core/records.py:632: title, context, decision, consequences, alternatives, globs, tags, sources, status proposed|accepted|superseded, decided_by, supersedes) with add/list/show/search/applicable/supersede on CLI and MCP, recall and DECISIONS.md export, ADR import from docs/adr. Reminder exists only in brief/claim by glob overlap (api/lifecycle/brief.py:104-112). Gaps: (1) advisory only -- no checks that code follows a decision (no fitness functions); (2) review gates (rubber_duck, critic, standards) do not receive governing decisions; no commit-time or periodic check; (3) no category, owner, enforcement level, review date or revisit trigger; statuses lack deprecated/retired/rejected; (4) no dependency/library policy (allow, forbid, version ranges, tech-radar ring) checked when a manifest changes; (5) no violation workflow: no waivers with expiry and approval; (6) no staleness review; (7) no edit/retire (B199 plans a generic one), no file-authored decisions; (8) no presets (stack packs) and no inference of current decisions from an existing codebase; (9) ADR files are imported once, never kept in sync. Planned work covering slices: B199, B-path-rules-to-decisions, B-architecture-pass (default style decision, generated layer rules), B-coh-contradiction, B-rw-vs-decision, B-semantic-recall, B-provenance-remaining-surfaces, B-uni-def-records, B-uni-record-surface, B-dt-library (ADR collection), P-org-config (company decisions), B-sched-defaults (architecture review job).
- **Mechanism.** Prior art: ADRs (Nygard, MADR statuses incl. deprecated and review dates, adr-tools, log4brains), architectural fitness functions (Ford, Parsons, Kua: Building Evolutionary Architectures), ArchUnit, import-linter, dependency-cruiser and Semgrep rules as executable decisions, Thoughtworks/Backstage Tech Radar rings (adopt/trial/assess/hold) for library policy, Renovate packageRules and deptry for dependency policy, OPA/conftest for config assertions, Danger-style PR-time checks, CODEOWNERS for decision owners, exception/waiver registers with expiry (security programmes).
- **Falsifier.** A project whose decision forbids a library, pins a layer rule and requires a test style gets a failing decisions gate on a diff that violates any of them, a reviewer prompt naming them, a time-boxed waiver path, a reminder when the decision's review date passes, and all of it manageable on CLI, MCP and files.

**Probe:**

```console
$ Read core/records.py Decision, core/handlers/knowledge.py, api/lifecycle/brief.py, api/decisions.py, surfaces/tools/decisions.py, services/importer.py ADR globs, export kind decisions; board census.
Confirmed as listed.
```

**Sources:** https://adr.github.io/madr/, https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools, https://www.thoughtworks.com/radar/faq, https://backstage.io/docs/features/techdocs/, https://www.archunit.org/, https://import-linter.readthedocs.io/, https://github.com/sverweij/dependency-cruiser, https://semgrep.dev/docs/writing-rules/overview, https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/, https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#packagerules
